chapters.heading: OFFENSES AGAINST THE STATE AND PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION
THE STATE BAR AND LEGAL PRACTICE

sections.heading: Unauthorized distribution of classified information
sections.text: See Statute
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Espionage
sections.text: Any person who distributes, or attempt to distribute, classified information to foreign governments, with intent or reason to believe that it is to be used to the injury of the State of Mayflower or advantage of a foreign government shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Conspiracy to Defraud the State
sections.text: Any two or more persons who conspire either to commit any offense against the State of Mayflower, or to defraud the State of Mayflower, or any agency thereof in any manner or for any purpose, and one or more of such persons do any act to effect the object of the conspiracy, shall both be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Criminal Anarchy ("Terrorism")
sections.text: Any person who commits a felony for the purpose of intimidating, coercing, or in furtherance of affecting the conduct of a government and is found guilty through criminal charges from the Department of Justice in a court of law shall be guilty of criminal anarchy.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Treason
sections.text: Any person who, owing allegiance to the state, wages war against the state or provides aid to enemies of the state shall be guilty of treason.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Insurrection
sections.text: Any person who participates in or incites an armed rebellion or violent resistance against the government or laws of the state shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Participation of War as a Foreign Actor
sections.text: Any individual who, owing allegiance to a foreign nation state, participates in acts of war against the State shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Concealing/destroying evidence
sections.text: Any person who willingly destroys or conceals evidence that will be presented as evidence on trial with the specific intent to prevent it from being shown shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: False filling of a police report
sections.text:
Any person who reports to a State certified peace officer, prosecutor, or person designated to receive reports of unlawful actions, that an unlawful act has been committed, knowing that the report is false, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.

Any State-certified law enforcement officer who has knowingly lied, embellished, or falsified statements on an official arrest report, warrant return, warrant request, or citation shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Fabricating evidence
sections.text: Any person who willingly creates or passes off as genuine false or untrue evidence for use in a court or nonjudicial proceding shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Commercial instrument falsification in the first degree
sections.text: Any person who, with intent to defraud, knowingly falsifies, alters, or forges any commercial instrument, with the intent to commit another crime, or aid to conceal the commission thereof, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Commercial instrument falsification in the second degree
sections.text: Any person who, with intent to defraud, knowingly falsifies, alters, or forges any commercial instrument shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Definition of "Commerical Instrument"
sections.text: For the purposes of 1 M.S.C. §§ 1204 and 1205, "commercial instrument" means any document or item utilized in the course of commercial transactions or business operations that holds legal or financial significance that evidences, constitutes, or facilitates a business or financial transaction.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Archival Misconduct Class I
sections.text: A person commits Class I Archival Misconduct when they fail, after being duly required by the State Archive Commission, to submit, import, or provide archival materials within a reasonable period of time.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Archival Misconduct Class II
sections.text: A person commits Class II Archival Misconduct when they hold a senate-confirmed office and knowingly fail, after being required by the State Archive Commission, to submit archival materials within a reasonable period of time.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Archival Misconduct Class III
sections.text: A person commits Class III Archival Misconduct when they knowingly destroy, delete, conceal, or otherwise eliminate any archive under the custody of the Commission; or destroy any record expected to be submitted to the Commission while aware that such record is required.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Felony misconduct
sections.text: Any person who incorrectly or immorally abusing one’s position as defined by law with corrupt intent to obtain a benefit for himself or herself or another or in which results in a threat to life shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Gross misconduct
sections.text: Any person who intentionally incorrectly or immorally abuses one’s position as defined by law which does not result in a threat to life shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Misconduct
sections.text: Any person who unintentionally, incorrectly or immorally abuses one's official position as defined by law to gain any type of benefit for himself or his associates shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Failure to comply
sections.text: Any person who willfully fails or refuses to comply with any lawful order or direction of any law enforcement officer, traffic accident investigation officer, traffic infraction enforcement officer, or member of the fire department at the scene of a fire, rescue operation, or other emergency shall be guilty of a misdemeanor. Notwithstanding the provisions of this subsection, certified emergency medical technicians or paramedics may respond to the scene of emergencies and may provide emergency medical treatment on the scene and provide transport of patients in the performance of their duties for an emergency medical services provider, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Failure to identify
sections.text: Any person who willfully fails or refuses to identify themselves by either not providing an identification card or license, username, or failing to take off a ski mask when ordered by any law enforcement officer, traffic accident investigation officer, or traffic infraction enforcement officer while being lawfully detained shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Evasion
sections.text: Any person who willfully flees or attempts to flee from a peace officer is guilty of evasion, provided the officer is uniformed and using his voice or emergency lights to hail the person from a reasonable distance shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Felony evasion
sections.text: Any person who flees from a peace officer as described in 1 M.S.C. § 1307 while endangering the lives of others shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Impersonation of a Peace Officer
sections.text: Any person, other than one who is given authority to act as such by law, who willfully wears, exhibits, or uses the authorized uniform (or which bears a sufficient likeness to such), insignia, emblem, device, label, certificate, writing, or badge of a peace officer, with the intent of fraudulently impersonating a peace officer, or of fraudulently inducing the belief that they are such, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Impersonation of a Public Servant
sections.text: Any person, other than one who is such, with intent to obtain a benefit, injure or defraud another, or facilitate an unlawful activity, who then assumes the character of a public servant and does or purports to act in that capacity, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Escape
sections.text: Any prisoner confined in any prison, jail, road camp, other penal institution, or being transported to or from a place of confinement who escapes or attempts to escape from such confinement shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Obstruction of justice
sections.text: Any person who hinders any peace officer, judge, or other government official from carrying out their official duties, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Obstruction of correspondence
sections.text: Any person who knowingly and willfully obstructs or retards the passage of the mail, or any carrier carrying the mail shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Obstruction of Transportation Authority Personnel
sections.text: The act of continuing to interfere with the operations of bus drivers or any transit personnel performing their duties despite warning(s) shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Obstruction of Emergency Services
sections.text: Any person who knowingly obstructs, hinders, or interferes any emergency medical technician, paramedic, rescue technician, or firefighter, from carrying out their official duties shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Obstruction of Conservation
sections.text: The act of continuing to interfere with the operations of Parks and Wildlife conservation officers performing their lawful duties despite warning(s).
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Impersonation of an Individual
sections.text: Any person who falsely impersonates another in his or her private or official capacity and in that assumed character injures, deceives, or defrauds another with fraudulent intent, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Obstruction of Senate
sections.text: Any person who knowingly and willfully obstructs, impedes, or interferes with the Senate’s lawful inquiries, investigations, or proceedings; fails to comply with a Senate subpoena, order, or writ; obstructs the Sergeant-at-Arms in the execution of their duties; destroys, conceals, alters, or conceals any document, record, or evidence with intent to impair its integrity or availability for use in a Senate proceeding; intimidates witnesses; or provides false or misleading information to the Senate with intent to deceive; or as defined in 3 M.S.C. 3 § 1303, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unauthorized Disclosure of Trade Secrets
sections.text: Any person who knowingly and willfully distributes, or makes otherwise available to an unauthorized person, or uses for the benefit of any unauthorized third party any trade secret, shall be guilty of a felony. Furthermore, any revenue generated from the usage of such property must be given in full to the property owner.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unauthorized Usage of Intellectual Property
sections.text: Any person who knowingly replicates, utilizes or intentionally displays a copyrighted or trademarked property for commercial gain without the permission of the property owner, unless it is used for study, criticism, news reporting, parody, or satire, shall be guilty of a misdemeanour. Furthermore, any revenue generated from the usage of such property must be given in full to the property owner.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unlicensed possession of non-civilian equipment
sections.text: Any person who possesses non-civilian equipment who is not an on duty state certified peace officer, national guardsman, firefighter, park ranger, or transportation authority operator, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unfair Housing Practices
sections.text: Any person who violates the Code of State Regulations pertaining to the ownership or use of residential property shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Criminal Trademark Infringement
sections.text: Any person who uses someone else's trademark without authorization or illegally to create confusion between the original and/or another mark shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unlawful Operation of a Business
sections.text: Any person who operates a business or partakes in the operation of a business without proper licensure and registration, or with suspended or otherwise inactive licensure and registration shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Obstruction of Railroad Operations
sections.text: Any person who wilfully contravenes any portion of Title 6, Subtitle 2, Chapter 1 of the State Code shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Felony Obstruction of Railroad Operations
sections.text: Any person who wilfully contravenes any portion of Title 6, Subtitle 2, Chapter 1 of the State Code and does so in a manner that endangers the life or safety of another person shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Smuggling
sections.text: Any person who knowingly and willfully imports goods or people into the territory of the State of Mayflower or refuses to submit to a request by the Port Authority for inspection shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Corporate Espionage
sections.text: Any person who distributes, or attempts to distribute, trade secrets, with intent or reason to believe that it will be of disadvantage to the owner of the trade secret or of advantage to an unauthorized third party, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Definition of "Trade Secrets"
sections.text: A "trade secret" shall be defined as confidential property or information of commercial benefit, where the owner of the trade secret has taken steps to maintain secrecy of the property.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Insurance Claims Misconduct
sections.text: Any Insurance Business that rejects a Claim by an Policyholder for a reason not outlined in 4 M.S.C. 6 § 4501 et seq., or fails to publish a summary claims report where required shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Failure to Pay a Private Driver
sections.text: Any customer that fails to pay a fare, agreed between the transportation service provider and customer, upon successful completion of the requested journey, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, unless the customer was injured due to an avoidable collision made by the driver due to their reckless vehicle operation.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Contempt of Court
sections.text: Any person who either: (1) misbehaves in the presence of a court or near thereto as to obstruct the administration of justice; (2) misbehaves as an officer of a court in their official transactions; or (3) disobeys or resists a court’s lawful writ, process, order, rule, decree, or command; shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Contempt of Senate
sections.text: Any person who knowingly and willfully obstructs, impedes, or interferes with the Senate’s lawful inquiries, investigations, or proceedings; fails to comply with a Senate subpoena, order, or writ; obstructs the Sergeant-at-Arms in the execution of their duties; destroys, conceals, alters, or conceals any document, record, or evidence with intent to impair its integrity or availability for use in a Senate proceeding; intimidates witnesses; or provides false or misleading information to the Senate with intent to deceive; or as defined in 3 M.S.C. 3 § 1303, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Failure to Appear
sections.text: Any person who, upon being issued a lawful summons or subpoena by an authorized officer or the Senate fails to appear with a timely manner shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Perjury
sections.text: Any person who, having taken an oath before a competent tribunal, officer, or person, in any case in which a law of the State of Mayflower authorizes an oath to be administered, that he will testify, declare, depose, or certify truly, or that any written testimony, declaration, deposition, or certificate by him subscribed, is true, willfully and contrary to such oath states or subscribes any material matter which he does not believe to be true; or in any declaration, certificate, verification, or statement under penalty of perjury, willfully subscribes as true any material matter which he does not believe to be true; is guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Failure to Pay a Citation
sections.text: Any person who fails to pay their citation within thirty minutes of its time of issue is guilty of failure to pay a citation shall be guilty of an infraction.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Disorderly Conduct before Senate Chambers
sections.text: Any person who causes a disturbance, enters the Senate Chamber or Senate Committee Room without permission, or refuses to cooperate with a law enforcement officer during a session of the Senate at-large or a hearing, meeting, or session of a Standing Senate Committee shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unlawful Conduct in a Protected Building
sections.text: Any person who violates 5 M.S.C. 1 §§ 1303.1-1303.6 or a regulation prescribed under 5 M.S.C. 1 § 1304.1 et seq. shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Witness Tampering
sections.text: Any person who attempts to improperly influence, alter or prevent the testimony of a witness shall be of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Jury Tampering
sections.text: Any person who attempts to influence the composition or decision of a jury during a trial through threats, force, or bribery shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Fraudulent Practice of Law
sections.text: Any person who does not have an active bar certification and represents another individual in a legal proceeding or advertises oneself as a legal professional shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: False Statements
sections.text: Any person who willfully makes a false statement that is in fact material, in writing, directly or indirectly, to any instrumentality of the State of Mayflower, under circumstances in which the statement could reasonably be expected to be relied upon as true; provided, that the writing indicates that the making of a false statement is punishable by criminal penalties; is guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Delinquent Registration by High-Risk Offender
sections.text: Any person who, being required to register as a predatory offender under 3 M.S.C. 1 § 5809, fails to register or update their registration as required within the stipulated timeframe, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Bank Robbery
sections.text: Any person whether by force or intimidation, that takes any property or money in the care, custody, control, etc. of any bank, credit union, or savings and loan institution shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 30 minutes in prison.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Money Laundering
sections.text: Any person, knowing that the property involved in a financial transaction represents the proceeds of some form of unlawful activity, conducts or attempts to conduct such a financial transaction which in fact involves the proceeds of unlawful activity with the intent to promote the carrying on of specified unlawful activity; or knowing that the transaction is designed in whole or in part: to conceal or disguise the nature, the location, the source, the ownership, or the control of the proceeds of specified unlawful activity; or to avoid a transaction reporting requirement under Local, State or Federal law, shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 30 minutes in prison and/or face a fine of not more than $5,000 or twice the value of the property involved in the transaction, whichever is greater.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Embezzlement
sections.text: A person who shall, having lawful custody of property not his or her own, appropriate the same to his or her own use, with intent to deprive the owner thereof shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 50 minutes in prison and/or face a fine of not more than $5,000 or twice the value of the property involved in the transaction, whichever is greater.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Counterfeiting
sections.text: Any person, with intent to defraud, falsely makes, forges, counterfeits, or alters any obligation or other security of the State of Mayflower or Union of Columbia shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Bribery
sections.text:
Any person who directly or indirectly, gives, offers or promises anything of value to any public official or person who has been selected to be a public official with intent to influence any official act shall be guilty of a felony.

Any public official or person who has been selected to be a public official who directly or indirectly, accepts or receives anything of value from any person with intent to influence any official act shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Loan Sharking
sections.text: Any lender which creates a loan not in accordance with Usury Laws or Loan Prohibitions shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 25 minutes in prison and/or face a fine of not more than $20,000 or twice the value of the loan, whichever is greater.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Insider Trading
sections.text: Any person who buys or sells a security while in possession of non-public price-sensitive information about the security, or tips off another individual about the non-public price-sensitive information who then buys or sells the security, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Securities Fraud
sections.text: Any individual who misrepresents or omits key facts of a business or security to investors shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Market Manipulation
sections.text: Any individual which falsely portrays a business to have a security which is actively being bought or sold shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Import of Prohibited Goods
sections.text: Any person whether by force or intimidation, that takes any property or money in the care, custody, control, etc. of any bank, credit union, or savings and loan institution shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 30 minutes in prison.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Possession of Prohibited Goods I
sections.text: Any person, knowing that the property involved in a financial transaction represents the proceeds of some form of unlawful activity, conducts or attempts to conduct such a financial transaction which in fact involves the proceeds of unlawful activity with the intent to promote the carrying on of specified unlawful activity; or knowing that the transaction is designed in whole or in part: to conceal or disguise the nature, the location, the source, the ownership, or the control of the proceeds of specified unlawful activity; or to avoid a transaction reporting requirement under Local, State or Federal law, shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 30 minutes in prison and/or face a fine of not more than $5,000 or twice the value of the property involved in the transaction, whichever is greater.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Possession of Prohibited Goods II
sections.text: A person who shall, having lawful custody of property not his or her own, appropriate the same to his or her own use, with intent to deprive the owner thereof shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 50 minutes in prison and/or face a fine of not more than $5,000 or twice the value of the property involved in the transaction, whichever is greater.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Possession of Prohibited Goods III
sections.text: Any person, with intent to defraud, falsely makes, forges, counterfeits, or alters any obligation or other security of the State of Mayflower or Union of Columbia shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Possession of Prohibited Goods to Craft
sections.text:
Any person who directly or indirectly, gives, offers or promises anything of value to any public official or person who has been selected to be a public official with intent to influence any official act shall be guilty of a felony.

Any public official or person who has been selected to be a public official who directly or indirectly, accepts or receives anything of value from any person with intent to influence any official act shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Petty Possession of Controlled Goods ("Petty Possession of Controlled Substances")
sections.text: Any lender which creates a loan not in accordance with Usury Laws or Loan Prohibitions shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 25 minutes in prison and/or face a fine of not more than $20,000 or twice the value of the loan, whichever is greater.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Grand Possession of Controlled Goods ("Grand Possession of Controlled Substances")
sections.text: Any person who buys or sells a security while in possession of non-public price-sensitive information about the security, or tips off another individual about the non-public price-sensitive information who then buys or sells the security, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Felony Possession of Controlled Goods ("Felony Possession of Controlled Substances")
sections.text: Any individual who misrepresents or omits key facts of a business or security to investors shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unlawful Introduction, Possession, or Manufacture of Prohibited Merchandise in a Correctional Facility
sections.text: Any individual which falsely portrays a business to have a security which is actively being bought or sold shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Operation of an Aircraft in Restricted Airspace
sections.text: Any person who operates an aircraft in an area prohibited by law or the Mayflower Aviation Administration shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Obstruction of a Flight Crew
sections.text: Any person who obstructs a pilot or other member of an aircraft flight crew in a manner that jeopardizes the safety of any person onboard an aircraft shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unlawful Operation of an Aircraft
sections.text: Any person who operates an aircraft without the required license, permit, or credentials shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Sabotage of an Aircraft
sections.text: Any person who defaces, damages, or destroys an aircraft shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Use of Explosives to Destroy an Aircraft
sections.text: Any person who uses an explosive to deface, damage, or destroy an aircraft shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Aeronautical Smuggling
sections.text: Any person who transports illegal cargo with an aircraft shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Fraudulent Usage of an Aircraft
sections.text: Any person who operates an aircraft in a manner prohibited by the type of aviation license or permit they possess shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Failure to Comply with Air Traffic Control
sections.text: Any person who operates an aircraft and fails to comply with a lawful order by Air Traffic Control shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Aircraft Hijacking
sections.text: Any person who operates an aircraft underneath an altitude requirement decided by the Mayflower Aviation Administration, without a reasonable explanation, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Violation of Flight Codes
sections.text: Any person who operates an aircraft in a manner that infringes on a Flight Code or Regulation mandated by the Mayflower Aviation Administration shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Aircraft Hijacking
sections.text: Any person who steals an aircraft shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Conspiracy against rights
sections.text: If two or more persons conspire to injure, oppress, threaten, or intimidate any person in the free exercise or enjoyment of any rights, privileges, or immunities secured or protected by the Constitution or laws of this state or of the Union of Columbia, they shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Deprivation of rights under color of law
sections.text: Any person who, under color of any law, statute, ordinance, regulation, or custom, willfully subjects any person to the deprivation of any rights, privileges, or immunities secured or protected by the Constitution or laws of this state or of the Union of Columbia, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: First-degree murder
sections.text: Any person who intentionally and maliciously kills another person with premeditation, or who kills whilst in the commission of a felony, or who kills a protected person in the commission of their duties, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Second-degree murder
sections.text: Any person who intentionally kills another person with intent to kill or commit great bodily harm shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Voluntary manslaughter
sections.text: Any person who, while in a heat of passion or sudden quarrel, kills another person shall be guilty of a felony so long as there is no malice aforethought.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Involuntary manslaughter
sections.text: Any person who inadvertently or accidentally causes death to another, not as a result of an intent to kill, rather as a direct result of a dangerous behavior performed without due caution shall guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Vehicular homicide
sections.text: Any person who uses a motor vehicle in a reckless manner resulting in the death of another individual shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Assassination of an Elected Official
sections.text: Any individual who kills an elected official with intent to kill or commit great bodily harm shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Kidnapping
sections.text: Any person who uses force or fear to transport a person across a significant distance without their consent, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: False imprisonment
sections.text: Any person who deprives another person of their personal liberty, unless done in good faith during an arrest, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Hostage Taking
sections.text: Any person who deprives another person of their personal liberty with the intent to use them as leverage for demands, including ransom, exchange, or coercion, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Hostage Taking of an Elected Official
sections.text: Any individual who deprives an elected official of their personal liberty with the intent to use them as leverage for demands, including ransom, exchange, or coercion, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Attempted murder
sections.text: Any person who, with the intention to kill and with malice, takes a substantial step towards committing the murder of either degree, but fails to cause death shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Assault with a deadly weapon
sections.text: Any person who assaults a person with an object capable of causing severe harm to the person, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Aggravated Battery
sections.text: A person who willfully and maliciously uses physical force against another with an object capable of causing serious bodily harm, or who commits battery against a protected person, shall be guilty of aggravated battery, a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Battery
sections.text: Any person who unlawfully and maliciously applies physical force to another person without that person's consent shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Assault
sections.text: Any person who willfully and maliciously attempts to, or causes reasonable fear or apprehension that they are going to touch or harm another person without that person's consent shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Felony hit and run
sections.text: Any person who fails to stop when involved in a traffic accident, where a person was injured, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Criminal threats
sections.text: Any person who threatens to kill or physically harm a person with means to carry out such a threat, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Extortion
sections.text: Any person who uses force or fear in order to acquire property, or to prevent an official from conducting his duty, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Hijacking
sections.text: Any person who forcefully steals an occupied vehicle shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Armed robbery
sections.text: Any person who uses a weapon in order to intimidate or use force to steal from another person’s immediate presence shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Robbery
sections.text: Any person who steals from a person's immediate presence with the use of force or fear, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Grand theft auto
sections.text: Any person who steals another’s vehicle whilst it is unoccupied shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Grand theft
sections.text: Any person who steals another's property with a value of over $200, including local, county, or state issued equipment to public services; or the theft of a firearm, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Petty theft
sections.text: Any person who steals another's property with a value of under $200, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Fraud in the first degree
sections.text: Any person who engages in a scheme or systematic course of conduct with intent to defraud or to obtain property of another by means of a false or fraudulent pretense, representation, or promise and thereby obtains property of another or causes another to lose property shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Fraud in the second degree
sections.text: Any person who engages in a scheme or systematic course of conduct with intent to defraud or to obtain property of another by means of a false or fraudulent pretense, representation, or promise shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Insurance Fraud
sections.text: Any Policyholder that fraudulently submits a Claim to an Insurance Business shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Evidence Theft
sections.text: Any person who picks up an item that was in possession of an individual detained or killed by law enforcement officers after being warned to not pick it up shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Evidence Theft Relating to Firearms
sections.text: Any person who picks up a firearm or ammunition that was in possession of an individual detained or killed by law enforcement officers after being warned to not pick it up shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Breaking and entering
sections.text: Any person who uses force in order to bypass physical restrictions to enter another’s property or vehicle without consent, and has been informed to leave or uses force in order to bypass physical restrictions to enter property with a posted notice or whitelisted door shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Arson
sections.text: Any person who willfully setting fire to another person's property without consent, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Burglary
sections.text: Any person who enters another person's private property without consent and with the intent to commit a theft or felony, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Hit and run
sections.text: Any person who fails to stop when involved in a traffic accident, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Trespassing
sections.text: Any person who enters any structure or vehicle of another without consent, including government property that has been restricted from public access, and who has been informed they must leave the property or has entered property protected by a posted notice or whitelisted door, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Vandalism
sections.text: Any player who wilfully defaces or damages the property of another player or the government, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Felony Trespass
sections.text: Any person who enters any National Guard vehicle or property without consent or authorization, or enters any protective exclusion zone repeatedly or while armed, or enters the Grounds of the Capitol Building while armed, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Destruction of Property
sections.text: Any player who destroys a property of another player or the government, causing it to be inoperable or unusable, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Destruction of a Vehicle
sections.text: Any player who destroys a vehicle of another player or the government shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Destruction of a Commercial Vehicle
sections.text: Any player who destroys a commercial vehicle of another player or the government shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Disorderly conduct
sections.text: Any person who intentionally or knowingly fights with another in a public place; uses abusive, indecent, profane, or vulgar language in a public place that by its very utterance tends toincite an immediate breach of the peace; makes an offensive gesture or display in a public place that tends to incite an immediate breach of the peace; abuses or threatens a person in an obviously offensive manner in a public place; makes unreasonable noise in a public place or near a private residence without consent via the use of a boombox; civilian grade communication radio, or car horn; displays a firearm or other deadly weapon in a public place in a manner calculated to alarm shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Disturbing the peace
sections.text: Any person who by shouting, noise, alarm or any other misbehavior wilfully disturbs the peace, public order, or causes scandal using offensive words, physical force or any other mean that can spark violence shall guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Inciting a riot
sections.text: Any person who urges four or more persons to engage in tumultuous and violent conduct of a kind likely to create public alarm shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Rioting
sections.text: Any person who, with four or more persons, engages in tumultuous and violent conduct and thereby intentionally or recklessly causes or creates a grave risk of causing public alarm shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unlawful assembly
sections.text: Any person who assembles with four or more other persons for the purpose of engaging or preparing to engage with them in tumultuous and violent conduct likely to cause public alarm, or when, being present at an assembly which either has or develops such purpose, he remains there with intent to advance that purpose shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Truancy
sections.text: Any person who, for the purposes of 4 M.S.C. 4 § 1801, fails to attend or otherwise provide excuse for lack of attendance to any class meeting, lecture, program, trip, or activity, is guilty of an infraction.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Violation of MTA Rules of Conduct
sections.text: Any person who violates the Mayflower Transportation Authority’s Rules of Conduct or any other regulation while utilizing public transit services—including, but not limited to, MTA operated buses, shuttles, subways, trains, railcars, and taxis—or while upon property owned, operated, or maintained by the Mayflower Transportation Authority shall be guilty of a misdemeanor. This includes failure to comply with fare regulations and any other actions that disturb the public peace or disrupt the safe and effective operation of Mayflower Transportation Authority services and facilities.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Stalking
sections.text: Any person who willfully, maliciously, and repeatedly follows or harasses another person, and who knows or reasonably should know that their conduct would cause a reasonable person to feel fear for their own safety, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Aggravated stalking
sections.text: Any person who commits the offense of stalking and who makes a credible threat with the intent to place the targeted person in reasonable fear for their own safety, or who violates a restraining order, injunction, or court-issued condition of release relating to that same person, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Conspiracy to commit a crime
sections.text: Any person who plans, or participates in a plan to commit a crime, and then carries out one action towards completing the plan shall be guilty of a felony
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Attempt to commit a crime
sections.text: Any person who intends to commit a crime, but is either interrupted in the process or decides to abandon their plan, is guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Solicitation to commit a crime
sections.text: Any person who verbally encourages another person to commit a felony shall be guilty of a misdemeanor
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Aiding and abetting
sections.text: Any person who commits an offense or aids, abets, counsels, commands, induces or procures its commission, is punishable as a principal.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Definition of "Aiding and abetting"
sections.text: It is the intent of the legislature that 1 M.S.C. § 4301 shall not carry a penalty or prison sentence independently and shall serve solely as a basis for imposing criminal liability.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Engagement in organized crime
sections.text: Any person who participates in organized criminal conduct and is a member of a criminal organization that is listed on official criminal organization list created by the Attorney General.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Direction of organized crime
sections.text: Any person who directs or organizes or leads an organized criminal enterprise shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Engagement in a Criminal Anarchy Organization ("Engagement in a Terrorist Organization")
sections.text: Any person who participates in a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Direction of a Criminal Anarchy Organization ("Direction of a Terrorist Organization")
sections.text: Any person who directs or organizes a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Supporting a Criminal Anarchy Organization ("Supporting a Terrorist Organization")
sections.text: Any person who gives material or financial support to a Terrorist Organization or a State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Coercion by threats
sections.text: Any person who uses threats to compell or induce a person to engage in criminal conduct shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Racketeering
sections.text: Any person who, being employed by or associated with any enterprise, conducts or participates in, directly or indirectly, such enterprise through a pattern of racketeering activity shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Racketeering conspiracy
sections.text: Any person who conspires to commit the offense of racketeering shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unauthorized possession of a destructive device
sections.text: Any person who knowingly possesses any device, explosive, incendiary item, or other object designed or intended to cause damage to persons or property through detonation, ignition, or combustion shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unlicensed possession of a firearm
sections.text: Any person who possesses a firearm without holding a state issued firearms license, or possesses a firearm within a firearm free-zone as defined in Title 4 Code of State Regulations, Subtitle 5 Public Safety, Chapter 6, or possesses a non-civil grade firearm who is not a state certified peace officer or national guardsman who is authorized to do so, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unauthorized possession of a high-capacity magazine
sections.text: Any person who knowingly possesses, receives, or transfers a firearm modification (as that term is defined in 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4304), that enables a firearm to accept more than twenty rounds of ammunition shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unlicensed possession of ammunition
sections.text: Any person who knowingly possesses ammunition, without holding a license to possess and carry a firearm, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unauthorized Stockpile of Destructive Devices
sections.text: Any person who knowingly or intentionally is in possession of four or more devices, bombs, or items capable of exploding or igniting, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unauthorized Stockpile of Ammunition
sections.text: Any individual who is in unlawful possession of 20 or more ammunition magazines shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unauthorized Stockpile of High-Capacity Ammunition
sections.text: Any individual who is in unlawful possession of 20 or more high capacity magazines shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: High-risk offender in possession of a firearm
sections.text: Any person who, being required to register as a high-risk offender under 3 M.S.C. 1 § 5609, knowingly possesses, uses, or has under their control any firearm, whether loaded or unloaded, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unauthorized possession of non-civilian firearm
sections.text: Any person who is in unauthorized possession of a non-civilian grade firearm shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unauthorized possession of military-grade firearm
sections.text: Any person who is in unauthorized possession of a military-grade firearm shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unauthorized possession of a Taser
sections.text: Any person who is in unauthorized possession of a taser shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Stockpile of a Taser
sections.text: Any person who is in unauthorised possession of two or more tasers shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unlawful possession of a firearm
sections.text: Any person who knowingly possesses, receives, or transfers an automatic firearm, as defined in 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4303, or who knowingly possesses a firearm without a valid license to possess and carry the same, shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unlawful dealing of a firearm
sections.text: Any person who knowingly or intentionally transfers, sells, trades, gives, transports, or delivers a firearm, without being a licensed vendor (as that term is defined in 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4305), shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unlawful dealing of ammunition
sections.text: Any person who knowingly or intentionally transfers, sells, trades, gives, transports, or delivers ammunition, without being a licensed vendor (as that term is defined in 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4305), shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unlawful Dealing of restricted-grade equipment
sections.text: Any person who purchases, sells, donates, or transfers restricted-grade firearms or equipment shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unlawful Dealing of military-grade equipment
sections.text: Any person who purchases, sells, donates, or transfers military grade firearms or equipment shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Discharging of a destructive device causing death or bodily harm
sections.text: Any person who discharges a device containing an explosive ordinance which causes death or bodily harm to another shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Carrying a firearm in a firearm-free zone
sections.text: Any person who knowingly possesses or causes to be present a firearm within a firearm-free zone (as that term is defined in 4 M.S.C. 5 § 6102) shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Discharging of a destructive device
sections.text: Any person who discharges a device containing an explosive ordinance without causing death or bodily harm shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Discharging a destructive device around a Commercial Property
sections.text: Any person who discharges a destructive device at or around a commercial point of sale shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Discharging of a destructive device within a Port-of-Entry
sections.text: Any person which causes an explosion within the premises of the Lander Marine Terminal shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Discharging of a destructive device within a Vehicle Dealership
sections.text: Any person which causes an explosion at or around a property whose purpose is to sell vehicles shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Discharging of a destructive device within a Commercial Dealership
sections.text: Any person which causes an explosion at or around a property whose purpose is to sell commercial vehicles shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Discharging of a destructive device within a Aviation Property
sections.text: Any person which causes an explosion at or around a heliport or airport shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Discharging a firearm within the grounds of the Capitol
sections.text: Any person who discharges a firearm within the Grounds of the Capitol, except when lawfully defending themselves or when authorized to do so by law, is guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Discharging of a destructive device within the grounds of the Capitol
sections.text: Any person which causes an explosion within the grounds of the Capitol shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Brandishing a Firearm in City Limits
sections.text: Any person who turns a firearm on another person or carries it in their hands within the Cities of Lander or Winchester, except when lawfully defending themselves or another pursuant to Title 5, Subtitle 1, Chapter 5, Subchapter 2, or are reloading a newly purchased weapon within a dealership shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Discharging a Firearm in City Limits
sections.text: Any person who discharges a firearm within the Cities of Lander or Winchester, except when lawfully defending themselves or another pursuant to Title 5, Subtitle 1, Chapter 5, Subchapter 2 is guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Street Racing
sections.text: Any two or more persons who engage in a speed competition on a public street, road, or highway without authorization from local governments shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Operating a Unroadworthy Vehicle
sections.text: Any person who operates a vehicle that is damaged enough to see visible smoke emerging (except when driving to the nearest repair center), operates a vehicle without a visible license plate, or operates a civilian vehicle with an invalid license plate shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Illegally Tinted Windows
sections.text: Any person who operates a motor vehicle while having windows tinted to a degree that prevents visibility of the vehicle's interior and/or driver from the exterior shall be guilty of an infraction.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unlawful Transport of Persons
sections.text: Any operator of a motor vehicle who permits any person to ride on the bumper, radiator, fender, hood, top, trunk, truck bed, or running board of such vehicle when operated upon any street or highway maintained by the state, county, or municipality shall be guilty of an infraction.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Driving Without a License
sections.text: Any person who operates a motor vehicle without a valid license issued by the state, suspended license, or equivalent status shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unlawful Use of Special Equipment
sections.text: Any individual or organization who operates, or causes to be operated, any motor vehicle or equipment in violation of 6 M.S.C. 4 Chapter III restrictions, including unauthorized use of emergency lights, sirens, airhorns, or restricted signal lights shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Careless Driving
sections.text: Any operator of a motor vehicle who operates a motor vehicle without exercising reasonable care or consideration for other drivers on the roadway shall be guilty of an infraction.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Failure to Maintain Lanes
sections.text: Any operator of a motor vehicle operating a motor vehicle who fails to keep the vehicle within its designated lane while driving, except when changing lanes, shall be guilty of an infraction.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Failure to Yield
sections.text: Any operator of a motor vehicle who, where: a non-stationary emergency vehicle within 50 studs of the rear of their vehicle, has their emergency light and/or sirens activated; or where (b) a non-stationary amber light vehicle, that is within 50 studs of the rear of their vehicle, has their warning light activated (1) fails to move their vehicle into another lane, when travelling on a roadway with two or more lanes in the same direction, when such movement can be made with due regard for safety and traffic conditions; or (2) fails to slow down to at least 20 MPH below the posted limit, where such a decrease would not result in the vehicle coming to a stop shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Failure to Signal
sections.text: Any operator of a motor vehicle who fails to signal or indicate a change of direction at an intersection by using the appropriate turn signals, except where the vehicle does not have the proper signals, is guilty of an infraction.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Failure to Stop at a Traffic Control Sign
sections.text: Any operator of a motor vehicle who does not come to a complete stop at a traffic control sign before crossing the marked stop line, crosswalk, or before obstructing the intersection will be guilty of an infraction.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Failure to Stop at a Traffic Control Device
sections.text: Any operator of a motor vehicle who does not come to a complete stop at a steady red traffic control device except after making the complete stop and turning right will be guilty of an infraction.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Illegal Parking
sections.text:
Any person who parks upon a curb marked with red paint, an area marked with a posted no parking sign, or with both tires of the same axle reasonably far enough upon a sidewalk, or with both tires of the same axle upon a road, or with both tires of the same axle parked upon the side of a tunnel or bridge, or by parking their vehicle in a fashion which occupies more than one parking space inside a parking lot, or by parking or leaving their vehicle on a vehicle spawner without moving it within a reasonable timeframe in a fashion that a reasonable person would construe to prevent the spawning of more vehicles, is guilty of an infraction.

A “Parking Space” shall be defined as a space in which approximately one car fits, demarcated by white lines.

A “Parking Lot” shall be defined as an area in which cars are allowed to park legally, containing one or multiple parking spaces.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Impeding Traffic
sections.text: Any operator of a motor vehicle who drives at a slow rate of speed that could/does hinder or impede the flow of traffic, shall be guilty of an infraction.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Improper Lane of Travel
sections.text: Any person who operates a motor vehicle in the opposite lanes of traffic, otherwise failing to stay on the right side of the road, shall be guilty of an infraction.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Driving without Headlights
sections.text: Any operator of a motor vehicle that fails to turn their headlights on between sunset and sunrise or during foggy conditions while the vehicle is operating on a public roadway will be guilty of an infraction.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Obstruction of Traffic
sections.text: Any player who intentionally prevents, or reasonably could prevent cars from passing freely along the roadways by is guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Reckless Driving
sections.text: Any operator of a motor vehicle who commits three traffic violations within a short timespan, or drives in a manner that a reasonable person would consider reckless shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Felony Reckless Driving
sections.text: Any operator of a motor vehicle who commits three traffic violations within a short timespan, or drives in a manner that could endanger the lives of persons around and other drivers on the roadway shall be guilty of a felony.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Speeding
sections.text: Any operator of a motor vehicle who exceeds a declared speed limit is guilty of speeding.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Excessive Speeding
sections.text: Any operator of a motor vehicle who exceeds the declared speed limit by 20 miles-per-hour or over shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Following too Closely
sections.text: Any operator of a motor vehicle who drives behind the operator of another vehicle close enough so that they would not be able to safely stop if the driver in front of them came to a swift halt, shall be guilty of an infraction.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Unlawful Overtaking or Passing of a Vehicle
sections.text: Any operator of a motor vehicle who overtakes or passes another motor vehicle in a double yellow line, shall be guilty of an infraction.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Interference with a Traffic Control Sign
sections.text: Any person who stands on, sits on, hinders, or obstructs any traffic control sign with their body, or another vehicle, shall be guilty of an infraction.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Interference with a Traffic Control Device
sections.text: Any person who stands on, sits on, hinders, or obstructs any traffic control device with their body, or another vehicle, shall be guilty of an infraction.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Noise Pollution
sections.text: Any operator of a motor vehicle who uses a horn, brake feature, car engine, or any other vehicular function to disturb the peace through excessive noise shall be guilty of an infraction.
sections.notes: Consolidation draft. 1 legacy provision combined. Existing cross-references require review.

sections.heading: Disabled Vehicles Obstructing Traffic
sections.text: Whenever a vehicle is disabled on any street or highway within the state or for any reason obstructs the regular flow of traffic, the driver shall move the vehicle so as not to obstruct the regular flow of traffic or, if he or she cannot move the vehicle alone, solicit help and move the vehicle so as not to obstruct the regular flow of traffic. Any person failing to do so shall be guilty of an infraction.
