sections.heading: National Guard Organization and Command
sections.text:
The "Guard" shall be known as the Mayflower National Guard, or any known variation thereof.

The Adjutant General shall be defined as the head of the Mayflower National Guard.

The Deputy Adjutant General shall be defined as the deputy head of the Mayflower National Guard.

Command Group shall be defined as the central command of the Mayflower National Guard designated by the Adjutant General and the Deputy Adjutant General.

Senior Officer shall be defined as any guardsman at or above the rank of O4/Major within the Mayflower National Guard.

Defense Policy shall be defined as any official written policy instituted by the Adjutant General, the Deputy Adjutant General, or any member of Command Group.

The terms ‘on-duty guardsman,’ ‘guardsman’ and ‘active duty’ for the purposes of this document shall refer to persons that are on the Mayflower Army National Guard team in-game and actively serving or representing the Mayflower National Guard.

For the purposes of this subtitle, ‘Misconduct’ or ‘Mishandling’ of proceedings shall be defined as any unethical overtures, instances of corruption or favor based on status, failing to include reasonable arguments and/or evidence, failing to file charges for reported incidents, or other such instances as one may reasonably believe to be prosecutorial misconduct.

In this subtitle, a Military Installation means any of the following properties below:

(a) Fort Standish within the Military Exclusion Zone;

(b) Lander City Berginson Armory;

(c) Winchester Recruitment Center; and

(d) Camp Bryant.

In this subtitle, the "Military Exclusion Zone" or "MEZ" shall be defined as the land surrounding the Fort Standish and Camp Bryant properties within the perimeter formed by appropriate signage and/or perimeter fencing.

(a) This shall extend to any river or stream directly below a perimeter fence or posted sign and open water within 1000 studs of any perimeter fence or posted sign.

Unauthorized individual” shall refer to any individual who enters a Military Exclusion Zone while not explicitly authorized by an on-duty Senior Officer, or Military Police Officer to enter that Military Exclusion Zone.

“Drawn firearm” shall refer to any firearm that is being held using at least one hand and is not contained wholly within a storage device.

A “Military Arrest Order (‘MAO’)” shall be defined as:

(a) Any issued order, by a sitting Judge within the State of Mayflower, to have a person arrested for a specific charge that falls under military jurisdiction.

A “Military Seizure Order (‘MSO’)” shall be defined as:

(a) Any issued order, by a sitting Judge within the State of Mayflower, to have a person and/or their property inspected for any military property to be seized, or any other articles that fall under military jurisdiction.

The term “Military Housing” or “Military Home” shall refer to:

(a) “Any Residential Property within a Military Exclusion Zone, as defined within Title 3, Chapter VII of the Mayflower State Code.”

The term Forward Operating Base or FOB shall be defined as the public land temporarily utilized by the National Guard as a military base.

Militia shall refer to an organisation of civilians who wish to exercise their 2nd Amendment rights in a regulated manner.

A General Officer shall refer to an individual holding the rank of Brigadier General or higher, excluding the Commander-in-Chief.

Honor Guard shall refer to the ceremonial unit established and maintained by the Mayflower National Guard pursuant to 3 M.S.C. 4 § 8101, tasked with rendering honors at official events and state functions, safeguarding designated sites, and upholding ceremonial drill proficiency.

Parade Fire shall refer to ceremonial volleys or salutes conducted by the Honor Guard during authorized events.

Designated Sites shall refer to the State Capitol, Supreme Court, The Volunteers’ Valor Memorial, and any other locations approved for ceremonial activity by the Governor, Adjutant General or their designee.

(a) Volunteers’ Valor Memorial shall refer to the memorial site located in Winchester, dedicated to the service and sacrifice of the 67th Eirinnite Regiment.

Proctees shall refer to individuals designated by the Adjutant General for ceremonial escort or protection during official Honor Guard operations.

The detainment powers established herein shall override those otherwise stipulated within the Mayflower State Code, including those established by the Chapter on Police Detainment Limitations.

(a) This scope of detainment powers within this section does not apply to the powers of detention or arrest delegated to Military Police, who shall retain those powers and will not be bound by the provisions of this section while serving in their capacity as Military Police.

The Adjutant General of the Mayflower National Guard is delegated the power to equip with, provide training in the use of, and dictate policies governing the use of handcuffs by guardsmen. The Adjutant General shall be empowered to instruct guardsmen, through the use of policy or direct orders, to detain any citizen in breach of state law within the direct vicinity of any Military Installation provided such detention is necessary to prevent damage to any person, property, or to prevent any action deemed subversive to the continuity of government.

During Martial Law, the Adjutant General shall have the power to dictate policy related to the detention of individuals who pose a threat to the restoration of order within the state. Any such detention should be ended as soon as is practical after the detaining guardsman becomes aware, or could reasonably be considered to have been made aware, of the end of any Martial Law.

A guardsmen shall not arrest any person, unless the guardsman is a serving member of the military police. Guardsmen shall transfer custody of any detainee to a member of the military police or civilian law enforcement as soon as it is practical to do so.

(a) Guardsmen, or any individual processing the arrest of the detainee, can not detain any individual for more than 20 minutes, at which point they must be released.

(b) If the detainee, on their own accord, takes measures to voluntarily delay the arrest process, the time taken during the delay shall not be counted to the overall time they have been detained for.

The Adjutant General may dictate policies allowing Guardsmen to transport an individual under military detention in such cases where transport is necessary to bring the individual to an officer able to make an arrest. Such situations include, but are not limited to, the transport of an individual to a point within city limits, in order to allow a peace officer with confined jurisdiction to affect the arrest of the individual.

On-duty members of the Mayflower National Guard reserve the right to search any person, vehicle or property within a Military Exclusion Zone.

On-duty members of the Mayflower National Guard reserve the right to search any person, vehicle or property attempting to gain entry to a Military Exclusion Zone.

(a) The person or owner of the vehicle/property may refuse the search but they shall be ordered to leave, and must leave the Military Exclusion Zone and shall not return without explicit permission of a Senior Officer, otherwise they shall be guilty of Failure to Comply.

The Adjutant General, or their designee, shall—

(a) Be able to prohibit individuals or groups from loitering within 50 studs of any Exclusion Zone where the individual:

(i) Repeatedly trespasses into a Military Exclusion Zone or otherwise restricted military property while armed with a firearm.

(ii) Repeatedly kills Guardsmen at or in close proximity of a Military Installation.

(iii) Is a member of a declared Criminal Street Gang.

(iv) Is a member of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization.

(b) Be responsible for maintaining a public database which contains the list of individuals or groups who are prohibited from loitering within proximity of a Military Exclusion Zone as outlined in this provision.

(i) No loitering ban shall be effectuated by the National Guard without first servicing a notification on the prohibition of loitering to the target of the order, and listing such an order on the aforementioned database.

During deployments, the Adjutant General, or their designee(s) may create a Forward Operating Base within a jurisdiction as decided by the Governor. When a FOB is created, the National Guard may prohibit individuals from entering such an FOB at their discretion where it can be reasonably determined that the FOB is visibly discernable.

(a) Individuals who enter a Forward Operating Base may be arrested for 1 M.S.C. § 3207 “Felony Trespass” after being warned and given a chance to leave the FOB at least once.

Should an individual enter a Forward Operating Base whilst in possession of a firearm without explicit permission of a Commissioned Officer, ranking Second Lieutenant or above, of the Mayflower National Guard, then on-duty guardsmen may use lethal force against them, provided a warning to leave is given where practical.

(a) Should an individual enter or approach a Forward Operating Base with a firearm drawn, on-duty guardsmen may use lethal force against them.

On-duty members of the Mayflower National Guard reserve the right to search any person, vehicle or property attempting to gain entry to a Forward Operating Base.

The Adjutant General, or their designee, shall reserve the right to prohibit individuals or groups from loitering within 100 studs of any Forward Operating Base as outlined in paragraph 1307 of this subchapter.

“Logging Run(s)” shall refer to the Mayflower National Guard sanctioned event where guardsmen log for wood.

“Checkpoint(s)” shall refer to barriers set up to block traffic by Law Enforcement Officers or Guardsmen to check for BOLOs, warrants, driver licenses, and firearm licenses

During a Logging Run or Checkpoint, Senior Officers and Command Group Personnel may create a Forward Operating Base within a reasonable area to protect Mayflower National Guardsmen and their equipment. When a FOB is created, the National Guard may prohibit individuals from entering such an FOB at their discretion where it can be reasonably determined that the FOB is visibly discernable.

(a) Individuals who enter a Forward Operating Base may be arrested for 1 M.S.C. § 3207 “Felony Trespass” after being warned and given a chance to leave the FOB at least once.

The Mayflower National Guard shall establish and maintain Special Forces (“SF”) designated for special operations. SF may be separate from the Infantry body. SF shall be defined as whichever unit(s) the Adjutant General of the Mayflower National Guard deems fit.

SF shall have the ability to wear civilian clothing and use civilian vehicles when acting in the capacity of the Mayflower National Guard for operations should their Commanding Officer deem such fit for the operation. Command Group reserves the right to devise policy around such and overrule the commanding officer’s decision on such.

SF may be deployed statewide outside of regular Guard deployments under the discretion of the Governor, Lieutenant Governor, or through other entities as designated by the Governor.

Members of Special Forces units may utilize tasers and other specialized equipment made available to them by the Command Group.

(a) Members of SF shall not be considered peace officers nor act as such, except when there is an activation of the guard, as prescribed by the constitution.

It shall be unlawful for any individual to possess an Explosive Device, except serving members of the National Guard as stipulated by this section.

The Adjutant General shall retain the express authority to authorize, and delegate the authorization process, for access to and use of Explosive Devices amongst guardsmen.

Those authorized to possess said Explosive Devices must only utilize them under at least one of the following parameters:

(a) The designee is participating in sanctioned training conducted with the knowledge and written permission of a Senior Officer.

(b) The designee is participating in an activation of the Guard, related to a declaration of war or an ongoing war.

(c) The designee is participating in an deployment of the Guard, related to counter terrorism or counter insurgency operations.

(d) The designee is detonating an Explosive Device seized by the Mayflower National Guard or law enforcement agencies in order to conduct an explosive ordnance disposal.

Any utilization of an Explosive Device that causes intentional and/or negligent damage or non-combatant casualties shall be properly reported, documented, and sent to the Adjutant General or his designee to allow for review by the Senate’s Intelligence & Military Affairs Committee, the Legislature at large, or a court of law.

Guardsmen may take pistols, as defined in 4 M.S.C. 5 § 2201, off-duty in accordance with rules and regulations set by the Adjutant General.

1 M.S.C. § 1403 “Unlicensed possession of non-civilian equipment” shall not extend to guardsmen who are permitted under their respective department’s policies to use a pistol issued by the Mayflower National Guard when not acting in the capacity of the Mayflower National Guard.

(a) This subchapter only applies when the pistol is physically present on the person, and does not extend to:

(i) A vehicle;

(ii) A dwelling; or

(iii) Any other method of storage where the pistol would not be present on the person.

(b) This subchapter does not exempt any person from any requirements or responsibilities normally required when carrying a firearm.

Any guardsmen who carries a pistol off-duty under this subchapter is required to identify themselves to any peace officer upon request, in addition to stating that they are employed with the Mayflower National Guard.

Members of the Mayflower National Guard shall be free from civil and criminal liability for violations of the Mayflower Vehicle Code when—

(a) Part of a convoy when a member of the Military Police is participating;

(b) During an activation or official operation of the guard;

(c) Taking part in a training exercise authorized by a Senior Officer; or

(d) When a State of Emergency has been declared.

Military aircraft and pilots shall be exempt from MAA flight regulations when:

(a) during an activation of the Guard.

The Mayflower National Guard shall be responsible for the protection of the following individuals at all times, including during peace time operations:

(a) The Adjutant General of the Mayflower National Guard.

(b) The Governor of Mayflower, when designated to be accompanied by the National Guard.

(c) General Officers of the Mayflower National Guard.

(d) Any other official expressly designated by the Governor of Mayflower or the Adjutant General.

The protections provided under this section shall extend to government officials, including those in the line of succession, when such an individual is within a Military Installation.

Nothing in this section shall preclude civilian law enforcement from exercising concurrent jurisdiction, but the Mayflower National Guard Military Police shall have primary responsibility for the protection duties described herein.

Any guardsmen who receives a general discharge from the Mayflower National Guard shall receive the following benefits:

(a) Free tuition at any university or college.

Any guardsman who receives a honorable discharge from the Mayflower National Guard shall receive the following benefits:

(a) Free tuition at any university or college; and

(b) Prioritization by the Department of State’s Commerce Office when seeking a Residential Property.

It shall be unlawful for any individual to manufacture/create or attempt to manufacture/create an Explosive Device, except serving members of the National Guard or a registered business authorized by the Adjutant General through written consent as stipulated within this section.

The Adjutant General shall retain the express authority to authorize, and delegate the authorization process, for access and to use of materials necessary to manufacture/create an Explosive Device.

The Adjutant General shall retain the express authority to enter into contracts with registered businesses to manufacture/create Explosive Devices for use by the National Guard and armed forces within the State.

A registered business manufacturing/creating Explosive Devices shall be authorized to possess any paraphernalia that would otherwise be considered illegal contraband provided that the intended use of the material is to fulfil functions necessary to furnish the National Guard or armed forces with Explosive Devices.

A registered business manufacturing/creating Explosive Devices shall be authorized to possess Explosive Devices that would otherwise be considered illegal contraband provided that the intended use of the material is to fulfil functions necessary to furnish the National Guard or armed forces with Explosive Devices.

(c) Taking part in a training exercise authorized by a Senior Officer; or

(d) When a State of Emergency has been declared.

Military aircraft and pilots shall be exempt from MAA flight regulations when:

(a) during an activation of the Guard.

parts.heading: Subchapter VII — PROTECTIONS OF GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS BY THE GUARD
parts.text:
The Mayflower National Guard shall be responsible for the protection of the following individuals at all times, including during peace time operations:

(a) The Adjutant General of the Mayflower National Guard.

(b) The Governor of Mayflower, when designated to be accompanied by the National Guard.

(c) General Officers of the Mayflower National Guard.

(d) Any other official expressly designated by the Governor of Mayflower or the Adjutant General.

The protections provided under this section shall extend to government officials, including those in the line of succession, when such an individual is within a Military Installation.

Nothing in this section shall preclude civilian law enforcement from exercising concurrent jurisdiction, but the Mayflower National Guard Military Police shall have primary responsibility for the protection duties described herein.

parts.heading: Subchapter VIII — PROTECTION OF VETERANS
parts.text:
Any guardsmen who receives a general discharge from the Mayflower National Guard shall receive the following benefits:

(a) Free tuition at any university or college.

Any guardsman who receives a honorable discharge from the Mayflower National Guard shall receive the following benefits:

(a) Free tuition at any university or college; and

(b) Prioritization by the Department of State’s Commerce Office when seeking a Residential Property.

parts.heading: Subchapter IX — MANUFACTURE OF EXPLOSIVES
parts.text:
It shall be unlawful for any individual to manufacture/create or attempt to manufacture/create an Explosive Device, except serving members of the National Guard or a registered business authorized by the Adjutant General through written consent as stipulated within this section.

The Adjutant General shall retain the express authority to authorize, and delegate the authorization process, for access and to use of materials necessary to manufacture/create an Explosive Device.

The Adjutant General shall retain the express authority to enter into contracts with registered businesses to manufacture/create Explosive Devices for use by the National Guard and armed forces within the State.

A registered business manufacturing/creating Explosive Devices shall be authorized to possess any paraphernalia that would otherwise be considered illegal contraband provided that the intended use of the material is to fulfil functions necessary to furnish the National Guard or armed forces with Explosive Devices.

A registered business manufacturing/creating Explosive Devices shall be authorized to possess Explosive Devices that would otherwise be considered illegal contraband provided that the intended use of the material is to fulfil functions necessary to furnish the National Guard or armed forces with Explosive Devices.

sections.heading: Military Police
sections.text:
The Mayflower National Guard shall establish and maintain a body known as the Military Police. This body shall be subordinate and answerable to Command Group, or any administrative entity supervising the body, who shall appoint a Senior Officer, hereinafter referred to as “Commanding Officer”, to oversee and direct the Military Police.

The Military Police shall be the military law enforcement branch of the Mayflower National Guard.

(a) The Military Police shall be tasked with enforcing Guard regulations, protecting Military Installations, convoys and members of the Guard.

“Military Police” shall be defined as military law enforcement officers.

“Military Police Officers” shall be defined as Commissioned Officers within the Military Police.

Members of the National Guard must meet the following prerequisites before joining any Military Police unit or body:

(a) The guardsman holds an active Law Enforcement Training Institute certification.

(b) The individual is currently serving within the Mayflower National Guard.

The Military Police shall have a budget given to the Commanding Officer by the Adjutant General and his Deputy.

This subchapter shall not apply during peacetime, outside of an activation of the Guard by the Governor as prescribed by the Constitution.

The Military Police shall operate in any place where the Mayflower National Guard are operating from or based, including locality surrounding serving members of the Guard.

(a) This shall not be limited to overseas.

Military Police shall be given temporary jurisdiction within the state in which their service and assistance has been requested by any peace officer of the state. This shall include, but not limited to, “10-58” or “58” calls on a radio or when Military Police assistance is specifically requested.

Military Police may not assume custody of a person from civilian peace officers unless:

(a) The person is a serving member of the Guard.

(b) The person has a Military Seizure Order or Military Arrest Order issued by the District Court.

(i) Members of civilian law enforcement that fail to turn over a suspect with an active Search Warrant relating to military property or equipment, MSO or MAO shall be guilty of “Obstruction of Justice” and “Misconduct” as defined within the Mayflower Criminal Code.

The Military Police have jurisdiction to conduct traffic stops when attempting to detain, or when otherwise authorized to arrest, on-duty national guardsmen when a crime, Defense Policy violation or a Code of Conduct violation has occurred. Military Police may also conduct traffic stops on sections of roadways within, or adjacent to, a Military Exclusion Zone.

The Military Police may only have jurisdiction to engage in a vehicle pursuit to detain or arrest a person if:

(a) A felony has been committed against on-duty national guardsmen and said person is evading Military Police.

(b) A person has been issued a Search Warrant relating to military property or equipment, a Military Seizure Order or Military Arrest Order by the courts and is evading Military Police.

(c) A crime or Defense Policy violation was committed by an on-duty guardsmen and said guardsmen are evading Military Police.

(d) A vehicle pursuit is initiated in or passes through a MEZ.

The Military Police shall have the power to freely search any Military Home, as defined in Title 4, Subtitle I of the Mayflower State Code, in accordance to regulations set by the Adjutant General or his designee.

Military Police may only have jurisdiction stipulated in this if they are clearly identifiable as a member of the Military Police.

The Military Police shall hold the exclusive jurisdiction to serve and execute Search Warrants relating to or involving military equipment/property, Military Seizure Orders and Military Arrest Orders issued by the District Court.

sections.heading: Military Legal Authorities
sections.text:
An “authorized guardsmen” or any variation thereof means a guardsmen who is a legitimate member of the Mayflower National Guard, through proper documentation such as a United Columbian Armed Forces Service Identification Card (U.C. Army ID).

In this section, “Mayflower Army National Guard” means the Mayflower National Guard as recited in earlier sections of this subtitle, as amended.

It is hereby authorized for the Judge Advocate General’s Corps of the Mayflower Army National Guard to engage in all legal activities under state law.

The Judge Advocate General’s Corps of the Mayflower Army National Guard is a staff corps and component of the headquarters of the Mayflower Army National Guard. It shall be organized in accordance with regulations prescribed by the Adjutant General of the Mayflower Army National Guard while it is a state agent, carrying out any obligation and function to the state while in peacetime and unactivated by the federal government.

There is in the headquarters component of the Mayflower Army National Guard a Staff Judge Advocate for the Mayflower Army National Guard. The Staff Judge Advocate shall be appointed directly by the Adjutant General, and serve at his command and pleasure.

The Staff Judge Advocate, under the direction of the Adjutant General, shall:

(a) Perform duties relating to legal matters arising in the Mayflower Army National Guard as may be assigned to him or her;

(b) Establish minimum requirements for prospective candidates to become judge advocates, including pay grade and benefits, with the consent of the Adjutant General;

(c) Either oversee or appoint in his name an officer or officers to oversee the various functions, as given by the Adjutant General, of the Judge Advocate General’s Corps; and

(d) Perform such other duties as may be assigned to him.

There is in the headquarters component of the Mayflower Army National Guard a Deputy Staff Judge Advocate for the Mayflower Army National Guard. The Deputy Staff Judge Advocate shall be appointed by the Adjutant General, with the advice of the Staff Judge Advocate, and serve at the command and pleasure of the Adjutant General.

The Deputy Staff Judge Advocate shall perform any of the duties of the Staff Judge Advocate either in his absence, delegated by the Staff Judge Advocate or under the direction of the Adjutant General from time to time.

All references to “prosecutor” herein shall refer to a judge advocate who is designated a prosecutor with the Judge Advocate General’s Corps unless stated otherwise.

It is authorized for the Judge Advocate General’s Corps to commence prosecutions of criminal offenses in state courts, pursued in the name of the State, against persons engaging in breach of State criminal law who, at the time of the commission of the offense is or was a guardsmen of the Mayflower Army National Guard, and either-

(a) is/was on the Mayflower Army National Guard team in-game; or

(b) is/was on property operated by the Mayflower Army National Guard; or

(c) is/was wearing any uniform also worn by a member of the Mayflower Army National Guard and has been identified as an authorized guardsmen upon inquiry or investigation by any person(s); or

(d) performing the duties of an ordinary guardsmen in the Mayflower Army National Guard; or

(e) is handling material, property, or equipment belonging to or issued by the Mayflower Army National Guard.

It is prohibited for the Judge Advocate General’s Corps to commence prosecutions for breaches of Title 2 of the Mayflower State Code.

The Staff Judge Advocate is authorized to appoint, or delegate to anyone the authority to, in the name and authority of the State, certain military officers as prosecutors within the Judge Advocate General’s Corps (JAGC), including those with authority over a particular prosecution or set of prosecutions; and prescribe or authorize the enactment of a set of rules guiding prosecutions under this section.

A prosecutor for the Judge Advocate General’s Corps shall have the same authority to prosecute as that of an ordinary prosecutor in the Mayflower Department of Justice, and referred to as “trial counsel” in proceedings before the courts of the State of Mayflower. Such prosecutors are authorized, further, to make a decision, in a case, pursuing or dismissing criminal charges against a person, in accordance with the direction of the prosecutor with authority over that case.

The Adjutant General is to prescribe regulations for the referral of criminal incidents, the formulation of cases for prosecution by relevant military authorities and the authority of prosecutors to sign, countersign or authorize applications for a military search or arrest order where required.

The Mayflower Department of Justice, if it is in receipt of reports of criminal activity in the military, shall be authorized to commence criminal investigations into anyone involved in such activities, including guardsmen, unless such criminal activity involves anything covered under 3 M.S.C. 4 § 3302(e), in which case it is required to engage in an investigation with military law enforcement.

(a) Upon an investigation concluding, the Mayflower Department of Justice may elect to refer a case to the Judge Advocate General’s Corps for prosecution if it involved: (1) any of the conditions set in (i) of this section, or (2) military law enforcement in the investigation. The Judge Advocate General’s Corps is authorized to dismiss or pursue the charges after referral and required to submit notice to the Mayflower Department of Justice of its decision.

(b) Where the Mayflower Department of Justice decides against referring a case to the Judge Advocate General’s Corps, it is required to submit notice to the Judge Advocate General’s Corps of its decision to prosecute or dismiss charges.

An individual prosecutor in a case may, with the consent of the prosecutor with authority over that case, elect to refer it to the Mayflower Department of Justice for prosecution. The Mayflower Department of Justice is authorized to dismiss or pursue the charges after referral.

It is authorized for a prosecutor, upon commencement of a criminal prosecution in court, to engage in actions commonly expected of an ordinary prosecutor in the Mayflower Department of Justice and to hold the exact same rights and authority of the same, including the right to submit motions or declarations of nolle prosequi before a court.

A “defense attorney” means a judge advocate who is designated a defense attorney in the Judge Advocate General’s Corps.

It is authorized for the Judge Advocate General’s Corps to facilitate and produce independent legal advice and provide legal representation to current guardsmen of the Mayflower Army National Guard.

A current guardsmen of the Mayflower Army National Guard is eligible for legal advice and legal representation at no cost for criminal defenses if they are involved in criminal proceedings and are not able to afford civilian counsel because of a genuine financial difficulty. The Adjutant General is to prescribe regulations surrounding the determination of financial difficulty of an individual guardsmen.

Similarly, a current guardsmen of the Mayflower Army National Guard is eligible for the same in civil proceedings if:

(a) they are a defendant in an official capacity case and either:

(i) The Mayflower Department of Justice is intending to provide a defense to a civil proceeding concerning the official capacity of a guardsmen in accordance with 5 M.S.C. 1 §§ 3209.3 and 3209.5; and

(ii) The defendant explicitly requests to the Judge Advocate General’s Corps for the aid of a judge advocate, in which case the judge advocate shall be subscribed to the case as a co-counselor, and under the direction of the counsel of record.

For the purposes of paragraph 3404 of this subchapter, a guardsmen involved in civil proceedings loses eligibility if the Solicitor General refuses to certify in accordance with either 5 M.S.C. 1 §§ 3209.6, or for any reasons in 3202.5.

A defense attorney for the Judge Advocate General’s Corps shall have the same rights that are afforded to a civilian attorney, and referred to as “defense counsel” in proceedings before the courts of the State of Mayflower, or another applicable and appropriate title if one exists.

A defense attorney may provide legal representation to guardsmen who are subject to criminal investigations by Military Police or any military investigation body with jurisdiction in the state. They may also provide legal representation to guardsmen, who have an inability to retain civilian counsel, that are subject to any investigation which the possible outcome of it may lead to separation from the Mayflower Army National Guard.

(a) Where this is the case, the defense attorney must not engage in any discussion or disclose any of their work with a judge advocate assigned to provide advice to any law enforcement arm of the Mayflower Army National Guard, except for the Staff Judge Advocate or his deputy.

It is authorized for the Judge Advocate General’s Corps to facilitate and produce independent legal advice, on behalf of the Adjutant General, for legal matters that affect the Guard, its operations, or any matter under military law or state laws affecting military operations.

In accordance with 3 M.S.C. 1 § 8201, it is authorized for the Judge Advocate General’s Corps to solicit a legal opinion, on behalf of the Adjutant General, from the Attorney General on issues under state law. Where it is required to solicit the opinion of the Attorney General, it shall do so in a manner that records the opinion in writing.

No officer, guardsmen or any employee or associated persons to the Mayflower Army National Guard or state agency thereof may interfere with the ability of judge advocates of the Judge Advocate General’s Corps for the Mayflower Army National Guard assigned or attached to, or performing duties with, military units to give independent legal advice to commanders or the ability of the judge advocate who is authorized to provide independent legal advice to the Adjutant General or Command Group.

sections.heading: Selective Service
sections.text:
Any employee of a government agency not serving within the Mayflower National Guard shall be encouraged to register for Selective Service, which, in a time of war, will allow the Governor to conscript them into the ranks of the Mayflower National Guard. However, no individual shall be involuntarily conscripted into service in the Mayflower National Guard; participation shall remain strictly voluntary.

(a) The registration shall include “willingness to serve” question, with the answer as a numerical value between 1-5, with 1 being least willing to be selected and 5 being most willing to be selected for service.

(b) If, during a war, an individual registered for service is selected by the Selective Service Committee, they shall be invited, not obligated, to serve in the Mayflower National Guard for a period not to exceed two months, unless the conscripted individual chooses, without coercion or force, to remain in the National Guard. Individuals shall be permitted to decline the invitation without penalty or consequence.

(i) The State Senate must convene within 24 hours of the draft being published and, through resolution, authorize the conscription as required by the State Constitution.

The Adjutant General shall appoint a Selective Service Committee who shall be responsible for managing the Selective Service Registration and selecting those for service during a time of war.

If, during a time of war, any individual registered for Selective Service is selected to

The Governor and/or his designee shall prescribe regulations on the manner that individuals may be drafted. They shall also ensure that:

(a) The process of being drafted remains impartial and transparent; and

(b) No group or strata of people is included or excluded based on any characteristics such as, but not limited to, social status, gender or race.

(c) The draft process shall be conducted in a manner that respects individual availability, personal circumstances, and consent. No government employee shall face punitive measures, job loss, or demotion for declining to serve after being selected.

sections.heading: Militia Registration
sections.text:
All Militias are required to be registered with the Office of the Adjutant General.

The Adjutant General or his designee are responsible for maintaining a registry of any Militias operating within the State.

Additional requirements may be set and published by the Adjutant General or his designee in a publicly accessible space.

Militias are not obligated to maintain or possess an active business license with the Department of State.

Individuals who have received an honorable discharge from the Mayflower National Guard must be given priority membership status, provided they qualify as eligible members.

The Adjutant General, or his designee are to establish requirements that Militias are to follow to continue active operation.

Militias are to maintain their own publicly available operations policy, as well as maintaining a public database of all qualified members.

(a) Citizens who have four in total or more active misdemeanor records or have an active felony record are not eligible to be qualified for membership.

Militias may be deployed alongside the Mayflower National Guard at the request of the Governor, Adjutant General or his designee, Militias will be subservient to all regulations set forth to the Mayflower National Guard and all members, regardless of their internal Militia rank, will be obligated to follow orders given by a Senior Officer, ranked Major or above, within the Mayflower National Guard.

sections.heading: Military Engineers
sections.text:
The Mayflower National Guard shall establish and maintain a military engineering body known as Engineers. This body shall be subordinate and answerable to Command Group, or any other administrative entity supervising the body, who shall appoint a Senior Officer, hereinafter referred to as "Engineer Commanding Officer," to oversee and direct a military engineering body.

Engineers shall be the military engineering branch of the Mayflower National Guard.

(a) Engineers shall be tasked with the assembly and maintenance of structures, deployment and disposal of explosive ordnance, utilizing explosive ordnance in the protection of the State of Mayflower and providing civil works.

"Engineers" shall be defined as guardsmen who hold the necessary accreditation and have undergone training to perform their duty.

"Engineer Officers" shall be defined as Commissioned Officers who hold the necessary accreditation and have undergone training to perform their duty.

This subchapter shall only apply during peacetime, outside of an activation of the Guard by the Governor as prescribed by the Constitution.

Engineers shall operate in any place where the Mayflower National Guard are operating from or based, including locality surrounding serving members of the Guard.

(a) This shall not be limited to overseas.

Engineers shall be given permanent jurisdiction within the state which their services and assistance for visible civil works missions that include—

(a) planning, designing, building and operating locks and dams, which includes flood control, beach nourishment and dredging for waterway navigation;

(b) design and construct fortifications and peace lines within civilian areas when deemed necessary to ensure public safety;

(c) design and construct checkpoints, roadblocks or any other form of temporary traffic control system at the request of law enforcement officers with the relevant authority to conduct such operations; and

(d) environmental regulation and ecosystem restoration.

Engineers shall reserve the privilege to request Military Police or any other available guardsmen to assist with the physical security of civil work project sites.

Engineers may only have jurisdiction stipulated in this if they are clearly identifiable as members of the Mayflower National Guard

Engineers shall hold the jurisdiction to render inoperable and adequately dispose of all explosive ordnances that have been placed or stockpiled.

sections.heading: General Officer Limitations
sections.text:
There may be no more than four (4) General Officers within the Mayflower National Guard at any given time.

The Governor may not nominate, and the Senate may not confirm, a general officer if such confirmation would result in the total number of general officers exceeding this limit.

Exceptions to this cap may only be made by a resolution of the Senate, approved by a simple majority, citing an active state of emergency or wartime necessity.

No individual may be appointed or promoted to the rank of General Officer in the Mayflower National Guard without the following requirements:

(a) At least six (6) consecutive months of service, with no disciplinary action taken against them.

(b) At least two (2) consecutive months of service as a Senior Officer, at the rank of Major or above.

(c) A letter of recommendation from the Adjutant General to the Governor, endorsing the individual's promotion to the rank of General Officer.

No individual may be appointed or promoted to the rank of General Officer in the Mayflower National Guard without first being nominated by the Governor and subsequently receiving a confirmation by a majority of the State Senate.

In the event of a vacancy requiring temporary assignment, the Governor may designate an acting general officer for a period to not exceed seven (7) days pending Senate review.

(a) The Governor shall not designate the same individual as an acting general officer more than once in any single calendar month.

No individual shall exercise the duties or privileges of a general officer, including operational command authority, access to sensitive command briefings, without Senate confirmation.

Any actions taken in violation of this section shall be deemed null and void.

sections.heading: Military Reporting and Oversight
sections.text:
The Governor or his designee, or the Adjutant General or his designee shall be responsible for notifying the State Legislature, in a timely manner, when:

(a) The National Guard in its entirety or its subordinate units, assets, organizations, groups, battalions, or components is deployed during peacetime.

(b) The National Guard in its entirety or its subordinate units, assets, organizations, groups, battalions, or components has been stood down during peacetime.

(c) There is potential for, or actual, deployment of the Special Forces.

During such a notification, the Governor or his designee, or the Adjutant General or his designee must in a timely manner, provide:

(a) The authority by which the deployment was made.

(b) A reason for the deployment.

(c) An estimated duration of the deployment.

(d) The subordinate units, assets, or organizations being deployed, if not the National Guard as a whole.

At the conclusion of such a deployment, the Governor or his designee, or the Adjutant General or his designee must inform the State Legislature, in a timely manner, of:

(a) The duration of the deployment.

(b) A timeline and summary of events that occurred during the deployment.

(c) New information, understandings, and operational takeaways made as a result of the deployment.

(d) Whether the State Legislature should furnish the Guard with legislative support, and a reason for such.

sections.heading: Emergency Management Definitions
sections.text:
The term 'on-duty operator' for the purposes of this subtitle shall refer to persons that are on the Port Authority team in-game and actively working or representing the Port Authority.

The term ‘Port of Entry’ shall refer to any property listed under 6 M.S.C. 5 § 1101.

The term ‘Emergency Management’ shall refer to the Office of Emergency Management, the subordinate entity to the Port Authority responsible for the immediate response and coordination of emergencies on Port Authority facilities.

The term ‘Port Authority Trans Henry’, or PATH, shall refer to the Port Authority Trans Henry Railroad, the subordinate entity of the Port Authority responsible for the upkeep and oversight of railroads and train operations owned by the Port Authority.

In this subtitle, ‘Port Authority Installation’ refers to any of the properties below:

(a) The Lander Marine Terminal;

(b) The International Commerce Center;

(c) Any bridge and tunnel within the State of Mayflower;

(d) The Standish Tunnel Command.

The Commissioner, or their designee, or in the event there is no Commissioner present; the highest ranking officer, may impose temporary restrictions on the possession or carrying of firearms within Port Authority Installations. Such restrictions shall not exceed a continuous duration of two (2) calendar days.

(a) The Commissioner, or their designee, or in the event there is no Commissioner present; the highest ranking officer, shall be required to issue a written notice detailing any firearm restrictions no less than thirty (30) minutes prior to such restrictions taking effect. The notice must explicitly specify which categories or types of firearms are subject to restriction.

(b) The provisions of this section shall not apply to on-duty law enforcement officers, military personnel, or other individuals or organizations expressly authorized in writing by the Commissioner or their designee. Such written authorization must identify, with specificity, the organizations or classes of individuals exempted under this subtitle.

(c) Individuals who are found in violation of the written notice, as defined in 3 M.S.C. 5 § 1201, can be subject to arrest or prosecution under 1 M.S.C. § 6302.

The Commissioner, or their designee, or in the event there is no Commissioner present; the highest ranking officer, may impose temporary entrance restrictions on any installations, as defined by 3 M.S.C. 5 § 1110, for no longer than two (2) calendar days.

(a) The Commissioner, or their designee, or in the event there is no Commissioner present; the highest ranking officer, may only impose temporary entrance restrictions when notified of a credible threat which compromises the safety of individuals or property within the installation.

(b) The Commissioner, or their designee, or in the event there is no Commissioner present; the highest ranking officer, shall be required to issue a written notice less than thirty (30) minutes prior to such restrictions taking effect.

(c) This statute shall not apply to installations identified under 3 M.S.C. 5 § 1110(a) without the express written consent of the Secretary of Transportation.

No individual shall host any event, public gathering, or similar activity on any Port Authority Installation without the express written authorization of the Commissioner or their designee.

(a) This provision shall not apply to official state functions when expressly designated as such by the Governor.

(b) Individuals who are found in violation of the written notice, as defined in 3 M.S.C. 5 § 1201, can be subject to arrest or prosecution under 1 M.S.C. § 3205.

(c) Individuals found to be in violation of this statute may, at the direction of the Commissioner or their designee, be prohibited from accessing Port Authority Installations, as defined in 3 M.S.C. 5 § 1110(a) and 3 M.S.C. 5 § 1110(b), for a period not to exceed one (1) week.

(i) The Commissioner, or their designee, shall be required to issue written notice of such prohibition no less than one (1) hour prior to its implementation. Said notice must clearly specify the duration of the prohibition and the exact date and time at which it shall expire.

A maximum speed limit of thirty (30) studs per second shall be enforced within the Lander Marine Terminal.

The Port Authority Police Department may serve as Commercial vehicle officers, as defined in 6 M.S.C. 1 § 2201, on any Port Authority Installation.

sections.heading: Business Licensing and Trade
sections.text:
No person shall operate a business without a proper license from the Department of State.

No business entity shall operate in a manner inconsistent with regulations promulgated by the Secretary of State in accordance with this Section.

(a) Regulations applied to any business entity promulgated by the Secretary of State in accordance with this act shall be created and enforced in a manner that ensures they do not unduly obstruct or excessively restrict business operations, thereby maintaining a balance between regulatory compliance and the ability of businesses to operate effectively and efficiently.

The Secretary of State shall ensure that all documents and information prerequisite is provided on the registration.

There shall be a form, known as the “Application for Articles of Organization” that shall be publicly available by the Department of State.

The Secretary of State shall refuse to file an articles of incorporation if it does not meet the following standards:

(a) The name of the corporation is clearly typed and designated as such.

(b) It must contain an initial appointment of the board of directors.

(c) It must contain the number of authorized shares and who the shares are distributed to.

(d) The name of the incorporator is clearly typed and designated as such.

(e) It must contain an attached set of bylaws which shall dictate the appointment of the board of directors and the further apportionment or sale of shares.

The Secretary of State shall refuse to file an articles of general partnership if it does not meet the following standards:

(a) The name of the general partnership is clearly typed and designated as such.

(b) The initial partners.

(c) Authorization for a majority of partners to modify the general partnership including the admittance or expulsion of partners.

(d) The designation and appointment of a managing partner.

The Secretary of State shall examine trademark applications to ensure compliance with the requirements set forth in this act, in addition to any additional requirements that the Secretary of State deems necessary.

Upon determination that a trademark meets all necessary criteria, including distinctiveness and non-conflict with any existing trademarks, the Secretary of State shall approve the registration.

Once a trademark has been registered with the Department of State with the approval of the Secretary of State, no other person or business entity may use the trademark unless permitted by the person or business entity who owns the rights to the trademark.

The Secretary of State is required to maintain a public registry of trademarks in use. This registry shall include information regarding:

(a) The registered trademark;

(b) The owner; and

(c) The goods or services associated with each trademark.

Owners of registered trademarks shall be required to renew their trademark registrations periodically, as prescribed by the Secretary of State.

If a registered trademark is revoked for any reason, including but not limited to non-renewal or infringement, the public shall once again be permitted to use the trademark.

No person or business entity shall use a trademark without the explicit permission, in writing, from the registered owner of the trademark.

(a) Violation of this section shall be a civil tort referred to as as "Civil Trademark Infringement" punishable by declaratory judgement removing the use of said trademarks and punitive damages up to $3000.

Any person or business entity who contravenes any provision of this Section shall, in addition to any other penalty or punishment to which the person or business entity may be liable to, be subject to the following penalties upon conviction:

(a) In the case of a business entity, a fine not exceeding ten thousand dollars.

(b) In the case of an individual, the crime of “Unlawful Operation of a Business”, or a fine not exceeding two thousand dollars, or both.

PURPOSES; RULES OF CONSTRUCTION. The provisions of this part shall be construed liberally to promote the following policies:

(a) To simplify, clarify, and modernize the law governing consumer protection, unfair methods of competition, and unconscionable, deceptive, and unfair trade practices.

(b) To protect the consuming public and legitimate business enterprises from those who engage in unfair methods of competition, or unconscionable, deceptive, or unfair acts or practices in the conduct of any trade or commerce.

DEFINITIONS. As used in this subchapter, unless the context otherwise requires, the term:

(a) "Final judgment" means a judgment, including any supporting opinion, that determines the rights of the parties and concerning which appellate remedies have been exhausted or the time for appeal has expired.

(b) "Enforcing authority" means the Department of Justice.

(c) "Violation of this part" means any violation of this act or the rules adopted under this act, and may be based upon any law, statute, rule, regulation, or ordinance which proscribes unfair methods of competition, or unfair, deceptive, or unconscionable acts or practices.

(d) "Department" means the Department of Justice.

(e) "Order" means a cease and desist order issued by the enforcing authority.

(f) "Interested party or person" means any person affected by a violation of this part or any person affected by an order of the enforcing authority.

(g) "Consumer" means an individual; business; firm; association; joint venture; partnership; trust; business trust; syndicate; fiduciary; corporation; any commercial entity, however denominated; or any other group or combination.

(h) "Trade or commerce" means the advertising, soliciting, providing, offering, or distributing, whether by sale, rental, or otherwise, of any good or service, or any property, whether tangible or intangible, or any other article, commodity, or thing of value, wherever situated. "Trade or commerce" shall include the conduct of any trade or commerce, however denominated, including any nonprofit or not-for-profit person or activity.

(i) "Thing of value" may include, without limitation, any moneys, donation, membership, credential, certificate, prize, award, benefit, license, interest, professional opportunity, or chance of winning.

UNLAWFUL ACTS AND PRACTICES. Unfair methods of competition, unconscionable acts or practices, and unfair or deceptive acts or practices in the conduct of any trade or commerce are hereby declared unlawful.

RULEMAKING AUTHORITY. The department may adopt rules which set forth with specificity acts or practices that violate this part and which prescribe procedural rules for the administration of this part.

INVESTIGATIVE POWERS OF ENFORCING AUTHORITY. If, by his or her own inquiry or as a result of complaints, the enforcing authority has reason to believe that a person has engaged in, or is engaging in, an act or practice that violates this part, he or she may administer oaths and affirmations, subpoena witnesses or matter, and collect evidence. Within 3 days after the service of a subpoena or at any time before the return date specified therein, whichever is longer, the party served may file in the district court and serve upon the enforcing authority a petition for an order modifying or setting aside the subpoena. The petitioner may raise any objection or privilege which would be available under this subchapter or upon service of such subpoena in a civil action. The subpoena shall inform the party served of his or her rights under this subsection.

(a) Upon failure of a person without lawful excuse to obey a subpoena and upon reasonable notice to all persons affected, the enforcing authority may apply to the district court for an order compelling compliance.

(b) The enforcing authority may request that an individual who refuses to comply with a subpoena on the ground that testimony or matter may incriminate him or her be ordered by the court to provide the testimony or matter. Except in a prosecution for perjury, an individual who complies with a court order to provide testimony or matter after asserting a privilege against self-incrimination to which he or she is entitled by law shall not have the testimony or matter so provided, or evidence derived therefrom, received against him or her in any criminal investigation or proceeding.

(c) Any person upon whom a subpoena is served pursuant to this section shall comply with the terms thereof unless otherwise provided by order of the court. Any person who fails to appear with the intent to avoid, evade, or prevent compliance in whole or in part with any investigation under this part or who removes from any place, conceals, withholds, mutilates, alters, or destroys, or by any other means falsifies any documentary material in the possession, custody, or control of any person subject to any such subpoena, or knowingly conceals any relevant information with the intent to avoid, evade, or prevent compliance shall be liable for a civil penalty of not more than $5,000, reasonable attorney’s fees, and costs.

REMEDIES OF ENFORCING AUTHORITY. The enforcing authority may bring:

(a) An action to obtain a declaratory judgment that an act or practice violates this part.

(b) An action to enjoin any person who has violated, is violating, or is otherwise likely to violate, this part.

(c) An action on behalf of one or more consumers or governmental entities for the actual damages caused by an act or practice in violation of this part.

The enforcing authority may terminate an investigation or an action upon acceptance of a person’s written assurance of voluntary compliance with this part. Acceptance of an assurance may be conditioned on a commitment to reimburse consumers or governmental entities, make contributions, pay civil penalties, pay attorney’s fees and costs, or take other appropriate corrective action. An assurance is not evidence of a prior violation of this part. However, unless an assurance has been rescinded by agreement of the parties or voided by a court for good cause, subsequent failure to comply with the terms of an assurance is prima facie evidence of a violation of this part. Such assurance is not a limitation upon any action or remedy available to a person aggrieved by a violation of this part.

CIVIL PENALTY. Any person, firm, corporation, association, or entity, or any agent or employee of the foregoing, who is willfully using, or has willfully used, a method, act, or practice declared unlawful, or who is willfully violating any of the rules of the department adopted under this part, is liable for a civil penalty of not more than $10,000 for each such violation. Willful violations occur when the person knew or should have known that his or her conduct was unfair or deceptive or prohibited by rule. This civil penalty may be recovered in any action brought under this part by the enforcing authority; or the enforcing authority may terminate any investigation or action upon agreement by the person, firm, corporation, association, or entity, or the agent or employee of the foregoing, to pay a stipulated civil penalty. The department or the court may waive any such civil penalty if the person, firm, corporation, association, or entity, or the agent or employee of the foregoing, has previously made full restitution or reimbursement or has paid actual damages to the consumers or governmental entities who have been injured by the unlawful act or practice or rule violation. If civil penalties are assessed in any litigation, the enforcing authority is entitled to reasonable attorney’s fees and costs.

CEASE AND DESIST ORDER; PROCEDURES. Whenever the Department of Justice has reason to believe that a person has been, or is, violating this part, and if it appears to the department that a cease and desist order against such violation would be in the interest of the public, it shall issue and serve upon such person a complaint and order stating its charges in that respect and containing a notice of a hearing upon a day and at the place therein fixed at least 5 days after the service of said complaint. No cease and desist order shall act as a limitation upon any other action or remedy available to a person aggrieved by a violation of this act.

Any person who violates a cease and desist order of the department after it has become final and while such order is in effect shall forfeit and pay to the state a civil penalty of not more than $5,000 for each violation which shall accrue to the state and may be recovered in a civil action brought by the state. Each separate violation of such an order shall be a separate offense, except that in the case of a violation through continuing failure or neglect to obey a final order of the department, each day of continuance of such failure or neglect shall be deemed a separate offense.

The department may modify or set aside its order at any time by rehearing upon its own motion when such rehearing is in the interest of the public welfare.

OTHER INDIVIDUAL REMEDIES. Without regard to any other remedy or relief to which a person is entitled, anyone aggrieved by a violation of this part may bring an action to obtain a declaratory judgment that an act or practice violates this part and to enjoin a person who has violated, is violating, or is otherwise likely to violate this part.

(a) In any action brought by a person who has suffered a loss as a result of a violation of this part, such person may recover actual damages, plus attorney’s fees and court costs.

(b) The remedies of this act are in addition to remedies otherwise available for the same conduct under state or local law.

Willful violations occur when the person knew or should have known that his or her conduct was unfair or deceptive or prohibited by rule. This civil penalty may be recovered in any action brought under this part by the enforcing authority; or the enforcing authority may terminate any investigation or action upon agreement by the person, firm, corporation, association, or entity, or the agent or employee of the foregoing, to pay a stipulated civil penalty. The department or the court may waive any such civil penalty if the person, firm, corporation, association, or entity, or the agent or employee of the foregoing, has previously made full restitution or reimbursement or has paid actual damages to the consumers or governmental entities who have been injured by the unlawful act or practice or rule violation. If civil penalties are assessed in any litigation, the enforcing authority is entitled to reasonable attorney’s fees and costs.

CEASE AND DESIST ORDER; PROCEDURES. Whenever the Department of Justice has reason to believe that a person has been, or is, violating this part, and if it appears to the department that a cease and desist order against such violation would be in the interest of the public, it shall issue and serve upon such person a complaint and order stating its charges in that respect and containing a notice of a hearing upon a day and at the place therein fixed at least 5 days after the service of said complaint. No cease and desist order shall act as a limitation upon any other action or remedy available to a person aggrieved by a violation of this act.

Any person who violates a cease and desist order of the department after it has become final and while such order is in effect shall forfeit and pay to the state a civil penalty of not more than $5,000 for each violation which shall accrue to the state and may be recovered in a civil action brought by the state. Each separate violation of such an order shall be a separate offense, except that in the case of a violation through continuing failure or neglect to obey a final order of the department, each day of continuance of such failure or neglect shall be deemed a separate offense.

The department may modify or set aside its order at any time by rehearing upon its own motion when such rehearing is in the interest of the public welfare.

OTHER INDIVIDUAL REMEDIES. Without regard to any other remedy or relief to which a person is entitled, anyone aggrieved by a violation of this part may bring an action to obtain a declaratory judgment that an act or practice violates this part and to enjoin a person who has violated, is violating, or is otherwise likely to violate this part.

(a) In any action brought by a person who has suffered a loss as a result of a violation of this part, such person may recover actual damages, plus attorney’s fees and court costs.

(b) The remedies of this act are in addition to remedies otherwise available for the same conduct under state or local law.

sections.heading: Classification of Government Information
sections.text:
The term “classified information” shall refer to:

(a) Information regulated by the provisions of this act to be confidential; specifically designated by a State Government Agency for limited or restricted dissemination or distribution.

The term “department head” shall refer to:

(a) The first-in-command of an agency under the executive cabinet, or the head of a law enforcement agency within the State of Mayflower.

The term “security clearance” shall refer to:

(a) An official authorization to access classified information designated by the provisions of this act.

Information may be classified at one of the following four levels upon meeting its’ criteria:

(a) “Top Secret” shall be applied to information, the unauthorized disclosure of which reasonably could be expected to cause exceptionally grave damage to the state security or impede ongoing criminal investigations or judicial processes that the original classification authority is able to identify or describe.

(b) “Secret” shall be applied to information, the unauthorized disclosure of which reasonably could be expected to cause serious damage to the state security or impede ongoing criminal investigations or judicial processes.

(c) “Confidential” shall be applied to information, the unauthorized disclosure of which reasonably could be expected to cause damage to the state security or impede ongoing criminal investigations or judicial processes.

(d) "O" shall be applied to information of the highest sensitivity, accessible only to the Governor, the State Intelligence Director, and individuals explicitly cleared by both.

At the time of original classification, the following shall appear on the face of each classified document, or shall be applied to other classified media in an appropriate manner in order to be considered classified information:

One of the three classification levels defined in Subchapter II of this Chapter.

The date of classification

The username of the individual with classification authority.

The date that is no more than 1 year from the date of original classification pursuant to paragraph (a)(ii) of this section.

Classified material shall remain protected under its classification for no more than one (1) year.

(a) An original classification authority may extend the duration of classification, change the level of classification, or reclassify specific information only when the standards and procedures for classifying information under this act, and by authority of the Governor to classify information.

The Governor shall have the authority to issue orders on the handling, procedure, criteria, or any otherwise necessary provisions for classifying information.

Categories for the classification of information must serve a reasonable and objective purpose of securing information that if disclosed, would be either damaging to state security, public safety, criminal investigations, defense, or life-threatening harm to individuals.

The authority to classify information originally shall only be exercised by:

The Governor of the State of Mayflower, in the performance of executive duties, the Lieutenant Governor;

Department heads and officials designated by the Governor through executive decree.

State government officials delegated this authority by paragraph (b) of this section.

State government officials delegated this authority by paragraph (b) of this section.

(i) Material which is classified by the Adjutant General, his deputy or any authorised officials thereof to which he delegates his authority may be subject to review, reclassification or reversal of their original classification status by the Director of State Intelligence which must be provided in writing. No material of the same (or inherently similar) nature may be reclassified without the approval of the Director of State Intelligence or the Governor in writing so as to subvert this clause.

“Confidential,” “Secret” or “Top Secret” may be delegated by the Governor; in the performance of executive duties, the Lieutenant Governor; or a department head or official designated pursuant to paragraph 1401 of this section; or a subordinate designated by a department head to classify information.

All Commissioned Officers of the Mayflower National Guard shall be issued the Security Clearance of Secret as defined by 4 M.S.C. 3 § 1201(b) upon completing Officer Candidate School or its equivalent.

All Senators appointed to the Senate Standing Committee on State Security, who have been vetted by the Office of State Intelligence, shall be issued a "Top Secret" security clearance, as defined in 4 M.S.C. 3 § 1201(a).

All Senators appointed to the Senate Standing Committee on State Security shall be vetted for the following criteria:

(a) Whether the Senator has alternate accounts, registered and unregistered, and reasonably determine if said accounts are connected to declared Street Gangs, Criminal Organizations, or Terrorist Organizations.

(b) Whether the Senator's inventory is open.

(c) Whether the Senator is involved with a street gang, criminal or terrorist organization which has been declared by the Attorney General.

(d) Whether the Senator has a criminal conviction of: any offence under Title 1, Subtitle 1, Chapter 1; Title 1, Subtitle 1, Chapter 6; Title 1, Subtitle 1, Chapter 9; Title 1, Subtitle 5, Chapter 1; Title 1, Subtitle 5, Chapter 2; any form of misconduct; 1 M.S.C. § 1201 "Concealing/destroying evidence;" 1 M.S.C. § 1401 "Unauthorized Disclosure of Trade Secrets;" or 1 M.S.C. § 1410 "Corporate Espionage."

The Office of State Intelligence shall have the sole authority to issue, revoke, and regulate security clearances within the State of Mayflower. The Director of State Intelligence may designate officials who hold the authority to issue, revoke, and regulate security clearances.

(a) This power shall not extend to Commissioned Officers of the Mayflower National Guard, although the Director of State Intelligence shall retain the power to petition in writing, to the Governor, for the suspension, revocation or regulation of security clearances for members of Commissioned Officers of the Mayflower National Guard.

(b) This power shall not extend to vetted Senators of the Senate Standing Committee on State Security, although the Director of State Intelligence shall retain the power to petition in writing, to the Governor, for the temporary suspension of members of the Senate Standing Committee on State Security for such actions regarding committee members, providing a detailed justification based on conflicts of interests or misconduct.

No individual may view classified information without a security clearance of the same classification level.

(a) The Governor, Lieutenant Governor, and Director of State Intelligence shall be exempt from this provision.

Whoever knowingly and willfully communicates, furnishes, transmits, or otherwise makes available to an unauthorized person, or publishes, or uses in any manner prejudicial to the safety or interest of the State or for the benefit of any foreign government to the detriment of the State of Mayflower any classified information shall be guilty of “Unauthorized distribution of classified information” as defined in 1 M.S.C. 1 § 1101, which shall be considered a capital felony.

Any person who distributes, or attempt to distribute, information classified by an authorized entity of the State of Mayflower to agents or subjects of foreign governments, with intent or reason to believe that it is to be used to the injury of the State of Mayflower or to the advantage of a foreign government shall be guilty of “Espionage” as defined in 1 M.S.C. 1 § 1102, which shall be considered a capital felony.

Any person that violates 4 M.S.C. 3 § 1602 in time of war shall be punished by death or imprisonment for no more than seven (7) days.

Any person that violates 4 M.S.C. 3 § 1602 shall be punished by death or imprisonment for no more than five (5) days.

sections.heading: Public Meetings and Sunshine Rules
sections.text:
The term "Lucas" shall refer to:

(a) columbianethos, the Inaugural Attorney General and a Founding Father of the State of Mayflower.

The term “legistlative body” shall refer to:

(a) The governing body of a municipality or county.

(b) A commission, committee, board, or other body of a municipality or county, whether permanent or temporary, decisionmaking or advisory, created by charter, ordinance, resolution, or formal action of a legislative body. However, advisory committees, composed solely of the members of the legislative body that are less than a quorum of the legislative body are not legislative bodies, except that standing committees of a legislative body, irrespective of their composition, which have a continuing subject matter jurisdiction, or a meeting schedule fixed by charter, ordinance, resolution, or formal action of a legislative body are legislative bodies for purposes of this chapter.

The term “meeting” shall refer to:

(a) Any congregation of a majority of the members of a legislative body at the same time and location, including teleconference location, to hear, discuss, deliberate, or take action on any item that is within the subject matter jurisdiction of the legislative body.

All meetings of the legislative body of a municipality or county shall be open and public, and all persons shall be permitted to attend any meeting of the legislative body of a local agency, except as otherwise provided in this chapter.

No legislative body shall take action by secret ballot, whether preliminary or final.

(a) The legislative body of a municipality or county shall publicly report any action taken and the vote or abstention on that action of each member present for the action.

No legislative body shall require public comments to be submitted in advance of a meeting and must provide an opportunity for the public to address the legislative body and offer comment in real time.

A legislative body of a municipality of county must publish the date, time, and location of all meetings in a place viewable and accessible to the general public no later then one hour before the time of any meeting.

(a) The Clerk or Presiding Officer of such legislative body must advise the public of any changes to the date, time, and location of published meetings as described in this subchapter.

No legislative body of a local agency shall prohibit or otherwise restrict the broadcast of its open and public meetings in the absence of a reasonable finding that the broadcast cannot be accomplished without noise, or obstruction of view that would constitute a persistent disruption of the proceedings.

A legislative body must maintain and publish for public access all agendas, proposed resolutions, bills, or acts of the body, a record of attendance, the minutes of any held meeting, and the voting record of any member of the legislative body.

The Clerk or Presiding Officer must furnish to any person who so requests a record of any business before the legislative body for which they clerk or preside over.

A legislative body may hold an emergency session in the event of an emergency, which shall be defined as a crippling disaster, mass destruction, terrorist act, or threatened terrorist activity that poses peril so immediate and significant that requiring a legislative body to provide one-hour notice before holding an emergency meeting under this section may endanger the public health, safety, or both, as determined by a majority of the members of the legislative body. In such circumstance, the one-hour requirement is waived.

sections.heading: Public Disclosures
sections.text:
The term "employee" shall refer to:

(a) Any individual employed by, or contracted to work in, any agency, department, office, division, or body of the State of Mayflower or political subdivisions thereof within the Executive Branch, including all law enforcement officers of the State.

No state employee shall:

(a) Engage in political activity while on-duty, or while clearly identifiable as a member as an employee of the State or any political subdivisions thereof, or within any property of the State or any political subdivisions thereof.

(b) Invite subordinate employees to political events, or otherwise encourage or suggest that they engage in political activity of any form.

(c) Solicit or discourage the political activity of any person with business before the agency, department, division, office, or body of the State or any political subdivison thereof that they are employed within.

(i) This includes any individiual a law enforcement officer makes contact with whilst on-duty.

(d) Solicit, accept, or recieve political donations or contributions.

(e) Use official authority to interfere with an election, or use official authority in any way while engaged in political activity.

Nothing in this subchapter shall be construed to prohibit a state employee or restricted state employee from attending political rallies, meetings, or fundraisers, or from being a non-partisan candidate in an election, or expressing opinions about partisan groups and candidates in partisan elections while not at work or using official authority, or express opinions about political issues, or joining partisan political groups, or sign nominating petitions, or vote as they choose.

The Attorney General or his designee shall receive any allegation of a violation of this Chapter and shall investigate the allegation to the extent necessary to determine whether there are reasonable grounds to believe that a violation of this Chapter has occurred.

The Attorney General or his designee shall fully investigate any alleged violations.

The Attorney General or his designee, upon conclusion of the investigation, shall either determine no violation was made, or submit a notice to the violator of the violations under this Chapter they sustained. Such notice will include a full description of the violation, and the corrective action taken, which may include:

(a) referral to the internal investigative unit of the agency which the violator is a member of;

(b) a fine of no more than $10,000; or

(c) removal from state service or a reduction in grade or rank;

(i) removal or reduction may only take place after the filing of an administrative action on behalf of the State against the violator.
