sections.heading: Records and Public Access
sections.text:
“Political Party” shall refer to any political organization registered with the Mayflower Elections Commission as a political party.

“Espionage” shall refer to the act of using informants or illicit and clandestine methods in order to obtain secret information from an organization, information which is not made readily accessible to the public and is not intended for public awareness.

“Secret Police” shall refer to an organization that carries out illicit and clandestine methods of intelligence gathering regarding communication between their targets.

“Paramilitary” shall refer to an organization, not associated with the Federal or State government, that carries out military activities through the employment of armed personnel and utilization of firearms, explosives and other weaponry.

“Security Contractor” shall refer to a business registered with the Department of State as a security company and have a license to offer security contracting services to the public.

Political parties shall be prohibited from carrying out espionage on other political parties.

Political parties shall be prohibited from having a paramilitary or other non-government militia as a direct subdivision of their party organization.

Political parties shall be prohibited from having a secret police or clandestine intelligence bureau as a direct subdivision of their party organization.

Political parties shall be allowed to contract a security contractor business for protection of events, buildings and any other needs.

Any political party that knowingly takes part in any prohibited activities outlined in this act, shall be unregistered as a political party by the Mayflower Elections Commission.

The registered leader of a political party found to have taken part in prohibited activities shall be suspended from establishing any political party for 3 (three) months.

Should a party be found to have taken part in prohibited activities and be shut down by the Mayflower Elections Commission, no individual shall be allowed to establish a political party under the previous party name for 3 (three) months.

parts.heading: Subchapter II — PROHIBITED ACTIVITIES
parts.text:
Political parties shall be prohibited from carrying out espionage on other political parties.

Political parties shall be prohibited from having a paramilitary or other non-government militia as a direct subdivision of their party organization.

Political parties shall be prohibited from having a secret police or clandestine intelligence bureau as a direct subdivision of their party organization.

Political parties shall be allowed to contract a security contractor business for protection of events, buildings and any other needs.

parts.heading: Subchapter III — ENFORCEMENT
parts.text:
Any political party that knowingly takes part in any prohibited activities outlined in this act, shall be unregistered as a political party by the Mayflower Elections Commission.

The registered leader of a political party found to have taken part in prohibited activities shall be suspended from establishing any political party for 3 (three) months.

Should a party be found to have taken part in prohibited activities and be shut down by the Mayflower Elections Commission, no individual shall be allowed to establish a political party under the previous party name for 3 (three) months.

sections.heading: Public Institutions and Education
sections.text:
The term “Academic unit” shall refer to:

(a) any University, faculty, school, institute, department, or other academic division of the University so designated by the Governing Council.

The term “Administrative staff” shall refer to:

(a) the employees of the University.

The term “Alumni” shall refer to:

(a) persons who have received certificates of completion, post-secondary diplomas or degrees from the University, or equivalent thereof as determined by the Governing Council, towards such a certificate of completion, post-secondary diploma or degree and are no longer registered at the University.

The term "Chancellor" shall refer to:

(a) the Chancellor of the University.

The term "Council" shall refer to:

(a) the governing body of an academic unit.

The term "Governing Council" shall refer to:

(a) the Governing Council of the University.

The term "Property" shall refer to:

(a) property of any kind, real or personal owned or leased by the University.

The term "Real property" shall be defined as:

(a) land and any permanent structures or improvements attached to the land owned or leased by the University.

The term "Student" shall refer to:

(a) any person registered at the University for full-time or part-time study in a program that leads to a certificate of completion, post-secondary diploma or degree of the University or in a program designated by the Governing Council as a program of post-secondary study at the University.

The term "Teaching staff" shall refer to:

(a) the employees of the University who hold the academic rank of professor, associate professor, assistant professor, full-time lecturer, part-time lecturer or who hold any other rank created by the Governing Council and designated by it as an academic rank for the purposes of this clause.

The term "University" shall refer to:

(a) Mayflower State University.

The term "Policy" shall refer to:

(a) A formal directive or guideline established by the University and ratified by the Governing Council delineating rules, standards, procedures, or expectations pertaining to academic, administrative, or operational matters within the University.

The Governing Council shall be composed of:

(a) the Chancellor, who shall be an ex officio member;

(b) one member appointed by the Chancellor among the alumni;

(c) two members, none of whom shall be students, members of the administrative staff or members of the teaching staff, appointed by the Governor; and

(d) three members elected by the administrative staff among the administrative staff.

Members of the Governing Council shall act with diligence, honesty, and with good faith in the best interests of the University.

No person shall serve as a member of the Governing Council unless they are a resident of the State.

The Governor, with the advice and consent of the Senate, shall appoint the Chancellor.

The Chancellor and each member of the Governing council shall serve for one hundred and eighty days, with each term commencing upon the commencement of the Chancellor’s term.

Where a vacancy occurs for any reason among the Governing Council, the Chancellor shall appoint a person to fill the vacancy for the remainder of the Governing Council’s term.

Four members shall constitute a quorum of the Governing Council.

(a) In times where the Governing Council does not have enough members to constitute a quorum, the Chancellor shall assume all rights and responsibilities normally assigned to the Governing Council for the duration of the Governing Council’s term.

The government, management and control of the University, and of the property, revenues, business and affairs thereof, are vested in the Governing Council, and, without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the Governing Council has power to:

(a) appoint, promote, suspend and remove members of the teaching and administrative staffs of the University, as the Governing Council considers necessary, but no member of the teaching staff shall be appointed, promoted, suspended or removed unless recommended by the Chancellor or such other employee of the University designated therefor by the Chancellor under this section;

(b) fix the number, the duties and the salaries of the University;

(c) delegate such of its powers under clauses i and ii to the Chancellor as it considers necessary;

(d) provide for the granting of and grant degrees, including honorary degrees, diplomas and certificates;

(i) the Chancellor shall be provided the privilege of granting or revoking degrees to any resident of the State;

(e) borrow from time to time real property for the use of the University, and give such security against the assets of the University by way of mortgage or otherwise, as it determines;

(f) determine and regulate the standards for the admission of students to the University, the contents and curricula of all programs and courses of study and the requirements for graduation;

(g) delegate such of its powers under clauses iv, v and vi as it considers proper to the Chancellor; and

(h) do all such acts and things as are necessary or expedient for the conduct of its affairs and the affairs of the University.

The City University of Lander and the Winchester Community College shall be consolidated into the Mayflower State University.

For the purposes of this section and all other sections that relate to employment, tenureship shall be defined as:

(a) the statutory designation granted to teaching staff entailing a secure employment status governed by specified criteria and procedures as promulgated by the Governing Council and this act.

Within no more than one hundred and eighty days after this act comes into effect shall the Governing Council create and approve an internal policy on the appointment and revocation of tenureship for teaching staff of the University.

(a) Any University policy regarding tenureship shall ensure that, upon appointment, teaching staff shall gain tenureship status within no more than sixty days of satisfactory employment.

Tenureship may be revoked if one of the following criteria is met:

(a) the member of the teaching staff is convicted of a felony;

(b) the department’s budget is insufficient to cover the expenses associated with the employment of the member of the teaching staff; or

(c) there is a concurrent assent from a supermajority, exceeding three-fourths, of the administrative staff, and a supermajority, exceeding three-fourths, of the governing council, along with the endorsement of a majority, exceeding one-half, of the alumni, and explicit approval from the incumbent Chancellor of the University.

All property heretofore or hereafter granted, conveyed, devised or bequeathed to any person in trust for or for the benefit of the University or of any college, faculty, school or department thereof or otherwise in connection therewith, subject to any trust affecting the property, is vested in the Governing Council.

All real property vested in the Governing Council shall, as far as the application thereto of any statute of limitation is concerned, be deemed to have been and to be real property vested in the State for the public uses of the State.

The Mayflower Vehicle Code shall not apply on University property for the purposes of classroom instruction as designated by policy in writing by the Governing Council.

For the purposes of this section, the term “firearm” shall be defined as:

(a) an object designed to fire a projectile at high velocity through the use of explosive force.

Any individual who possesses on their person a firearm on University property shall be guilty of “Carrying a firearm within a firearm-free zone.”

(a) this shall not extend to administrative staff of the University.

(b) this shall not extend to students of the University.

(c) this shall not extend to state certified peace officers, national guardsmen, firefighters, park rangers, and transportation authority operators, whether on or off duty.

(d) this shall not extend to persons who have been exempted by the Chancellor in writing and upon request by any law enforcement entity has provided evidence of such exemption within a reasonable amount of time.

Upon reception of funds from the Secretary of Treasury for the Union of Columbia, the Chancellor shall establish a schedule to increase wages in the form of multipliers to good-standing degree holders from the University.

(a) The Chancellor shall, in consultation with the Governing Council, ensure that the schedule does not disrupt or have the possibility to disrupt the stability of the Union of Columbia's consumer price index.

The University shall not be subject to any provision of the Department of State Act.

(a) Subject to regulations and rights as a State-owned venture, the Chancellor may, in representation of the Governing Council, choose to represent the University as a business entity to regulatory bodies.

sections.heading: Police Services and Community Safety
sections.text:
This chapter may be cited as the "Police Services and Community Safety Act."

The term “political subdivision" shall refer to:

(a) Regional jurisdictions generally include but are not limited to the State, County or Municipal governments residing within the boundaries of the State of Mayflower.

The term “county law enforcement” shall refer to:

(a) Any government agency within the jurisdiction of a county political subdivision within the State of Mayflower that enforces the law.

The term “municipal law enforcement” shall refer to:

(a) Any government agency within the jurisdiction of a municipal political subdivision that enforces the law.

The term “budget” shall refer to:

(a) The limitations on employment and membership within a government agency as afforded by law.

(b) The provisions of other relevant expenditures of a government agency as afforded by law.

The term “department” or “agency” shall refer to:

(a) Any public department, law enforcement agency, or office within the State of Mayflower.

(b) A governmental or quasi-governmental entity established by statute or through intergovernmental agreement.

The term “M.S.C.”, “MSC”, or “M.S.C” shall refer to:

(a) The Mayflower Code of Statutes.

The term “detain” shall refer to:

(a) A situation in which a peace officer, possessing reasonable suspicion that a crime has been committed, legally orders an individual under investigation to remain within the peace officer's immediate presence and not to leave.

The term “arrest” shall refer to:

(a) The act in which a peace officer, having probable cause to believe that a crime has been committed, takes a suspect into custody.

The term “book” shall refer to:

(a) The act in which a peace officer sends a person to a local, county or state jail using a booking terminal.

The term “second” shall refer to:

(a) The duration of approximately 9,192,631,770 periods of the radiation corresponding to the transition between two hyperfine levels of the ground state of the Cesium-133 atom.

The term “warrant” shall refer to:

(a) A written order issued by a judge, authorized by law, directing a law enforcement officer to perform a specific act, such as the arrest of a person, the search and seizure of property, or the execution of a judicial order.

The term “police officer” or “peace officer” shall refer to:

(a) Any person who is a sworn member of a law enforcement agency and is authorized by the State to enforce laws, maintain public order, prevent and investigate crimes, and protect life and property. This definition includes any federal peace officer, and any fire marshal of a political subdivision.

The term “department head” shall refer to:

(a) The first-in-command of an agency under the executive cabinet, or the head of a law enforcement agency within the State of Mayflower.

The term “force” shall refer to:

(a) Any physical effort used by a peace officer to compel compliance by an unwilling subject. This includes, but is not limited to, physical restraint, physical strikes, use of chemical agents, use of electronic control devices, and use of firearms.

The term “law enforcement training institute” shall refer to:

(a) The Mayflower Law Enforcement Training Institute.

(b) Any state-operated entity established to provide training and certification for individuals preparing to fulfill the duties of a peace officer.

The term “sheriff” shall refer to:

(a) The department head of a county law enforcement agency.

The term “railroad police officer” has the same meaning as defined in 6 M.S.C. 2 § 1102(a).

The term “police operation" shall refer to:

(a) A coordinated effort carried out by one or more peace officers with a clearly defined objective, which may include but is not limited to surveillance, investigation, apprehension, or enforcement actions.

The term “firefighter" shall refer to:

(a) A fire chief and any other person employed in, or appointed to, a fire department and assigned to undertake fire protection services, and includes a volunteer firefighter.

The term “fire protection services" shall refer to:

(a) A range of services including fire suppression, fire prevention, fire safety education, rescue operations, emergency medical services, and related health services. This also includes the training of individuals involved in any of these areas, and the provision of any single service or a combination thereof, as performed by qualified personnel such as firefighters, paramedics, or other emergency responders.

The term “fire department" shall refer to:

(a) A group of firefighters authorized to provide fire protection services by a political subdivision.

The term “parking enforcement agent” or “parking enforcement officer” or “traffic warden” or “traffic infraction enforcement officer” shall refer to:

(a) Any person who is not a peace officer that is employed with a municipal law enforcement agency or the Parks and Wildlife department and is authorized to enforce certain parking and traffic laws and aid peace officers in traffic operations.

The term “special police” or “special officer” shall refer to:

(a) Any peace officer limited to special jurisdiction, provided this term shall not apply to regularly appointed peace officers of Mayflower or its cities or to any sheriff or deputy sheriff of the counties of Mayflower.

(b) Special jurisdiction shall be defined as, “Specific public or private properties or persons.

(i) Special police shall possess all the common law and statutory powers of a regularly appointed peace officer only inside of or within 25 studs of their special jurisdiction and immediately adjoining streets and pathways, or when called out of jurisdiction or deputized for mutual aid or emergency situations.

The duties of a peace officer shall include the following but is not limited to:

(a) preserving the peace;

(b) preventing crimes and other offenses;

(c) assisting victims of crime;

(d) apprehending criminals and other offenders who may lawfully be taken into custody;

(e) participating in prosecutions;

(f) executing warrants that are to be executed by peace officers and performing related duties;

(g) performing lawful duties as promulgated by their respective department head or the Attorney General;

(h) completing training required by this act, the peace officer’s respective department, or a law enforcement training institute; and

(i) performing such other duties as assigned to the peace officer by this act or any other Act, including any prescribed duties.

A peace officer shall not, in the course of their duties, treat any person in a manner that contravenes the Constitution of the State of Mayflower.

A peace officer shall not, by act or omission, do anything that the peace officer, at the time, knows or reasonably ought to know would infringe or deny a person’s rights or freedoms listed in the Constitution of the State of Mayflower.

A peace officer shall not make an arrest if, at the time of the arrest, the peace officer knows or reasonably ought to know that the arrest is unlawful.

A peace officer shall not authorize or make a physical or psychological detention if, at the time of the detention, the peace officer knows or reasonably ought to know that the detention is unlawful.

A peace officer shall not neglect the health or safety of any person who is in their custody as a result of the peace officer’s duties.

A peace officer shall not use force unless:

(a) the force is used for the purpose of carrying out a lawful duty;

(b) the peace officer is entitled by statute or common law to use force for the purpose of carrying out that duty;

(c) the peace officer is acting on reasonable grounds; and

(d) the force used is no more than is necessary given the circumstances.

A peace officer shall not solicit, offer or take a bribe.

A peace officer shall not use their position as a peace officer to do any of the following:

(a) Use any information obtained through their position as a peace officer for personal advantage.

(b) Willingly and knowingly interfere with the administration of justice.

(c) Use departmental property or resources for personal or financial benefit.

A peace officer has the authority to act as such throughout the state but is bound by provisions of the state code that stipulate restrictions.

(a) No county charter or municipal charter shall limit the authority of a peace officer to act as such throughout the State.

If a law enforcement agency is specifically established to serve a particular subdivision, the respective department head is responsible for ensuring that their law enforcement agency’s policies maintain peace officers in areas in or around that political subdivision.

(a) This code does not apply to postal inspectors.

If a law enforcement agency is specifically established as a governmental or quasi-governmental entity established by statute or through intergovernmental agreement, the respective department head is responsible for ensuring that their law enforcement agency’s policies maintain peace officers in areas or around the property managed by the entity, with a focus to the protection of properties that the entity owns, possesses or administers and the persons upon those properties.

(a) This code does not apply to postal inspectors.

The department head of the Mayflower Parks and Wildlife Department may designate an employee as a peace officer for the purposes of this act, subject to the following restrictions:

(a) The maximum number of employees that may be designated as peace officers by the department head of the Mayflower Parks and Wildlife Department shall be calculated by the following steps in order:

(i) Multiply the respective department budget by zero point five (0.5).

(ii) The floor of the resulting product shall be taken.

(iii) Two (2) shall be added to the floored value to determine the final number of employees that may be designated as peace officers.

(b) A publicly accessible registry shall be available listing employees of the Mayflower Parks and Wildlife Department who are appointed as peace officers under this subchapter.

(c) Any restrictions or requirements listed in this act.

No person shall be hired, carry out the duties, or act in the capacity of a peace officer unless he or she:

(b) is physically and mentally able to perform the duties of the position;

(c) does not have any pending criminal matter before any court of the State or the Union of Columbia in which the person is named as the defendant and has been reasonably notified of such matter;

(d) has not been convicted of any degree of misconduct within the last fifty (50) days;

(e) holds an active certification by a recognized law enforcement training institute; and

(f) is actively employed by a recognized law enforcement entity within the State for the purposes of keeping the peace.

If a person is convicted of any degree of misconduct, the sentencing judge may grant an exemption from compliance with 4 M.S.C. 5 § 1601(d), either in full or for a period of up to fifty (50) days.

Every department or railroad company that employs at least one peace officer is required to establish an internal investigation unit that is staffed with at least one peace officer who shall not be in any other division or department office. The duties of this unit shall include, but are not limited to, the following:

(a) Primary duties include, but are not limited to:

(i) ensuring employed peace officers are compliant with department policies;

(ii) ensuring employed peace officers are compliant with regulations issued by the Attorney General;

(iii) maintaining confidentiality where appropriate;

(iv) conducting impartial investigations regarding contraventions of department policies, this act, and any regulations prescribed under this act; and

(v) recommend re-education training or disciplinary measures to the department head.

(b) From time to time, issue a publicly accessible document or message regarding disciplinary measures taken within the respective department since the last publication.

(c) Forward the result and any relevant documentation to the Attorney General upon conclusion of any investigation.

(d) Ensure that an accessible method for reporting police misconduct is available to the public.

In the event that a complaint regarding a department head is received, the internal investigation unit shall notify the Attorney General upon receiving the complaint.

The department head of a law enforcement agency shall have the authority to:

(a) establish or amend written procedures regarding the administration of their respective department;

(b) approve re-education training or disciplinary measures suggested by their respective department’s internal investigation unit; and

(c) delegate in writing any powers and duties in this act, or its regulations, to a member or office of their respective department, subject to any limitations, conditions or requirements set out in the delegation.

The department head of a law enforcement agency is responsible for:

(a) ensuring department policies and procedures are in compliance with all applicable laws and regulations;

(b) overseeing and managing all activities of their respective department;

(c) in writing, authorizing police operations in their respective department; and

(d) approving all offers of employment of their respective department.

This chapter applies to postal inspectors, peace officers employed and acting under a port authority, and any other law enforcement agency not established directly by the State or by State law.

(a) Notwithstanding subchapter (IV), peace officers that fall under this subchapter only receive the authority to enforce the M.S.C. if:

(i) the department is in full compliance with this act and its regulations;

(ii) the peace officer is in full compliance with this act and its regulations; and

(iii) if applicable, the department is in full compliance with their respective budget.

(b) This act applies to railroad police officers.

(i) In the event of a conflict between the Railroad Safety Act and this act, the provisions of the Railroad Safety Act shall prevail.

(c) This chapter shall not apply to peace officers employed by and acting under the Mayflower National Guard (hereinafter “military police officers”); however, any law governing military police officers may incorporate by reference the provisions of this act, or any part thereof, to establish or enforce requirements upon military police officers.

(a) Any peace officer limited to special jurisdiction, provided this term shall not apply to regularly appointed peace officers of Mayflower or its cities or to any sheriff or deputy sheriff of the counties of Mayflower.

(b) Special jurisdiction shall be defined as, “Specific public or private properties or persons.

(i) Special police shall possess all the common law and statutory powers of a regularly appointed peace officer only inside of or within 25 studs of their special jurisdiction and immediately adjoining streets and pathways, or when called out of jurisdiction or deputized for mutual aid or emergency situations.

parts.heading: Subchapter III — DUTIES AND CONDUCT OF A PEACE OFFICER
Subchapter IV — JURISDICTION OF A PEACE OFFICER
parts.text:
A peace officer has the authority to act as such throughout the state but is bound by provisions of the state code that stipulate restrictions.

(a) No county charter or municipal charter shall limit the authority of a peace officer to act as such throughout the State.

If a law enforcement agency is specifically established to serve a particular subdivision, the respective department head is responsible for ensuring that their law enforcement agency’s policies maintain peace officers in areas in or around that political subdivision.

(a) This code does not apply to postal inspectors.

If a law enforcement agency is specifically established as a governmental or quasi-governmental entity established by statute or through intergovernmental agreement, the respective department head is responsible for ensuring that their law enforcement agency’s policies maintain peace officers in areas or around the property managed by the entity, with a focus to the protection of properties that the entity owns, possesses or administers and the persons upon those properties.

(a) This code does not apply to postal inspectors.

parts.heading: Subchapter V — PARKS AND WILDLIFE LAW ENFORCEMENT
parts.text:
The department head of the Mayflower Parks and Wildlife Department may designate an employee as a peace officer for the purposes of this act, subject to the following restrictions:

(a) The maximum number of employees that may be designated as peace officers by the department head of the Mayflower Parks and Wildlife Department shall be calculated by the following steps in order:

(i) Multiply the respective department budget by zero point five (0.5).

(ii) The floor of the resulting product shall be taken.

(iii) Two (2) shall be added to the floored value to determine the final number of employees that may be designated as peace officers.

(b) A publicly accessible registry shall be available listing employees of the Mayflower Parks and Wildlife Department who are appointed as peace officers under this subchapter.

(c) Any restrictions or requirements listed in this act.

parts.heading: Subchapter VI — ELIGIBILITY TO GAIN AND MAINTAIN PEACE OFFICER STATUS
Subchapter VII — INTERNAL INVESTIGATIONS UNITS
parts.text:
Every department or railroad company that employs at least one peace officer is required to establish an internal investigation unit that is staffed with at least one peace officer who shall not be in any other division or department office. The duties of this unit shall include, but are not limited to, the following:

(a) Primary duties include, but are not limited to:

(i) ensuring employed peace officers are compliant with department policies;

(ii) ensuring employed peace officers are compliant with regulations issued by the Attorney General;

(iii) maintaining confidentiality where appropriate;

(iv) conducting impartial investigations regarding contraventions of department policies, this act, and any regulations prescribed under this act; and

(v) recommend re-education training or disciplinary measures to the department head.

(b) From time to time, issue a publicly accessible document or message regarding disciplinary measures taken within the respective department since the last publication.

(c) Forward the result and any relevant documentation to the Attorney General upon conclusion of any investigation.

(d) Ensure that an accessible method for reporting police misconduct is available to the public.

In the event that a complaint regarding a department head is received, the internal investigation unit shall notify the Attorney General upon receiving the complaint.

parts.heading: Subchapter VIII — DEPARTMENT HEAD CONDUCT
Subchapter IX — APPLICATION TO SPECIAL ENTITIES
parts.text:
This chapter applies to postal inspectors, peace officers employed and acting under a port authority, and any other law enforcement agency not established directly by the State or by State law.

(a) Notwithstanding subchapter (IV), peace officers that fall under this subchapter only receive the authority to enforce the M.S.C. if:

(i) the department is in full compliance with this act and its regulations;

(ii) the peace officer is in full compliance with this act and its regulations; and

(iii) if applicable, the department is in full compliance with their respective budget.

(b) This act applies to railroad police officers.

(i) In the event of a conflict between the Railroad Safety Act and this act, the provisions of the Railroad Safety Act shall prevail.

(c) This chapter shall not apply to peace officers employed by and acting under the Mayflower National Guard (hereinafter “military police officers”); however, any law governing military police officers may incorporate by reference the provisions of this act, or any part thereof, to establish or enforce requirements upon military police officers.

sections.heading: Parking Enforcement
sections.text:
The department head of a municipal law enforcement agency, or the Mayflower Parks and Wildlife Department, or the Mayflower Department of Transportation may designate an employee as a parking enforcement agent, subject to the following restrictions:

(a) Parking Enforcement Agents have the authority to issue citations for the following offenses of the M.S.C.:

(i) 2 M.S.C. § 1105 “Idling”

(ii) 2 M.S.C. § 1207 “Illegal Parking”

(iii) 2 M.S.C. § 1211 “Obstruction of Traffic”

(iv) 2 M.S.C. § 1218 “Interference with a Traffic Control Sign”

(v) 2 M.S.C. § 1219 “Interference with a Traffic Control Device”

(vi) 2 M.S.C. § 1220 “Noise Pollution”

(vii) 2 M.S.C. § 1221 “Disabled Vehicles Obstructing Traffic”

(viii) 7 M.S.C. 2 § 1105 “Unlawful disposure of a motor vehicle into a fishing habitat”

(ix) 1 M.S.C. § 1305 “Failure to Comply”

(x) 1 M.S.C. § 1306 “Failure to Identify”

(xi) Any other Title 2 offense when ordered to do so by a peace officer. Such citations shall be issued on behalf of the peace officer rather than the parking enforcement agent.

(b) Departments may permit their parking enforcement agents to carry equipment accessible by the department, but must always require parking enforcement agents to wear a uniform when on duty that bears at least one patch related to the department.

(c) Parking enforcement agents may participate in the enforcement of road closures and checkpoints, directing traffic, and other traffic related operations when requested by a peace officer or emergency service provider.

sections.heading: Police Powers and Firearms
sections.text:
This chapter may be cited as the "Police Services and Community Safety Act."

This chapter uses the same definitions as chapter (1) of this subtitle, and shall be viewed as a continuiation of chapter (1).

For the purposes of this subchapter, the term “pistol” shall be defined as:

(a) a weapon originally designed, made, and intended to fire a projectile (bullet) from one or more barrels when held in one hand, and having:

(i) a chamber(s) as an integral part(s) of, or permanently aligned with, the bore(s); and

(ii) a short stock designed to be gripped by one hand at an angle to and extending below the line of the bore(s).

(b) This definition includes any ammunition compatible and intended for use with the pistol.

A department head of a law enforcement agency must include a provision in their respective department’s policies regarding the privilege to use a pistol issued by the department when not acting in the capacity of the respective law enforcement agency.

1 M.S.C. § 1403 “Unlicensed possession of non-civilian equipment” shall not extend to peace officers who are permitted under their respective department’s policies to use a pistol issued by the department when not acting in the capacity of their respective law enforcement agency.

(a) This subchapter only applies when the pistol is physically present on the person, and does not extend to:

(i) a vehicle;

(ii) a dwelling; or

(iii) any other method of storage where the pistol would not be present on the person.

(b) This subchapter does not exempt any person from any requirements or responsibilities normally required when carrying a firearm.

Any peace officer who carries a pistol off duty under this subchapter is required to identify themselves to any peace officer upon request, in addition to stating any departments they are employed by.

The authorized driver of a vehicle displaying emergency lights authorized under 6 M.S.C. 4 § 3202 is exempt from the provisions of Title 2 of the M.S.C., provided that the authorized driver operates the vehicle with due care in the lawful performance of their duties.

(a) Any individual or organization operating a vehicle pursuant to a valid and active emergency light permit issued under 6 M.S.C. 4 § 3401 shall enjoy the same exemption from Title 2 of the M.S.C., provided the vehicle is operated with due care and in the performance of official duties.

Notwithstanding 4 M.S.C. 5 § 2301, a peace officer operating a vehicle that is authorized to display emergency lights pursuant to 6 M.S.C. 4 § 3202(a) shall be exempt from Title 2 of the M.S.C., provided the officer operates said vehicle with due care in the lawful performance of their duties.

(a) This code applies regardless if the emergency light is active or not.

An authorized driver operating a vehicle in accordance with 4 M.S.C. 5 §§ 2301-2302 shall not be held civilly liable in the event a pedestrian is struck, provided that the driver was acting with due regard, unless negligence or misconduct is demonstrated.

(a) This immunity extends to the employer of the authorized driver, unless negligence or misconduct is demonstrated.

Presumption of non-liability shall apply where evidence indicates the pedestrian intentionally or neglectfully entered or remained in the path of a vehicle where the authorized driver is operating with due regard and care.

(a) Where the authorized vehicle is operating in response to an emergency and has active emergency lighting systems as required by 6 M.S.C. § 3102, a presumption of negligence or a wilful act unless evidence clearly contradicts that presumption.

Pedestrians must yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles as described in 4 M.S.C. 5 §§ 2301-2302.

Liability stipulated in 4 M.S.C. 5 §§ 2303-2304 shall not apply in cases where pedestrians are partaking in a lawful assembly or approved event.

No monetary damages shall be awarded in a civil court under this Subchapter unless negligence or misconduct is demonstrated.

Nothing in this Subchapter shall be construed to permit reckless operation of emergency vehicles or to diminish the standard of due regard required.

“Due regard” for the purpose of this Subchapter shall hold the definition that an authorized driver acted within the constitutional rights of themselves and other road users and within the laws they are not exempted from promulgated by the Mayflower State Code.

When it is reasonably safe for a peace officer, every peace officer upon request from any person is required to:

(a) show their identification card;

(b) state the department they are acting in the capacity of; and

(c) if applicable, state their callsign.

A peace officer is not required to identify themselves if:

(a) it is not reasonably safe for the peace officer;

(b) the peace officer is operating an emergency service vehicle;

(c) the peace officer has already identified themselves to the same person within the last sixty (60) minutes;

(d) the peace officer has declared themselves out of service; or

(e) the peace officer is engaged in or participating in an authorized police operation where the act of providing identification would compromise the objective(s) of the operation.

The Attorney General may make regulations towards any law enforcement agency, personnel, or leadership, in the interest of ensuring that the law is enforced properly, ethical pratices are maintained, and the safety of the State is prioritized.

(a) Any public employee who violates a published law enforcement memorandum unintentionally as a result of negligence shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1304 "Misconduct."

(b) Any public employee who violates a published law enforcement memorandum knowingly or intentionally shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1303 "Gross Misconduct."

(c) All departments who employ law enforcement officers shall develop policies governing requirements for compliance with published memorandums, and punishment for disobedience from employees.

(d) The Attorney General may, at their discretion, may choose to outline certain instances in which there is individual liability of an officer rather than official liability in instances of failure to execute such memorandums.

The Attorney General shall notify the head of any department effected of any creation, amendment, revocation, or any other alteration of a regulation prescribed under this subchapter.

The provisions of any regulation prescribed by the Attorney General under this subchapter shall be interpreted as being in addition to, and not in derogation or restriction of, any power, jurisdiction or authority that may be exercised under this Chapter, the Constitution, or any other Chapter.

Any person who contravenes 4 M.S.C. 5 §§ 1302-1309, 4 M.S.C. 5 § 1601, 4 M.S.C. 5 § 2204, or 4 M.S.C. 5 § 2401 is guilty of an offense and is liable on conviction, in addition to any other penalty or punishment to which the person may be guilty, is guilty:

(a) in the case of an unintentional action that does not result in a threat to life, to misconduct;

(b) in the case of an intentional action that does not result in a threat to life, to gross misconduct; or

(c) in the case of an action that results in a threat to life, to felony misconduct.

The Governor may, for a renewable period of up to one hundred twenty (120) days, appoint a person as a peace officer for the purposes of this act, subject to the following conditions and limitations:

(a) The person is a certified and commissioned peace officer in another State within the Union of Columbia.

(i) Persons who meet this requirement and are appointed under this subchapter shall be considered certified for the purposes of Article VIII, Section 3 of the Constitution for the duration of their appointment.

(b) The person shall have the same responsibilities as any other peace officer normally employed directly or indirectly by a law enforcement agency in the State of Mayflower.

(c) Any other conditions, limitations, stipuplations, or requirements listed in the appointment.

The Colonel of the Mayflower State Police shall ensure that persons appointed as peace officers under this subchapter are provided access to equipment and facilities normally given to peace officers employed under the Mayflower State Police.

(a) The internal investigation unit of the Mayflower State Police shall handle all complaints regarding persons appointed as peace officers under this subchapter.

In this Subtitle, any reference to a pronoun shall be interpreted to include all respective pronouns, regardless of gender. Terms such as 'he,' 'him,' or 'his' shall be deemed to include 'she,' 'her,' 'hers,' 'they,' 'them,' 'theirs,' or any other pronoun as applicable. This inclusive interpretation applies to all provisions, ensuring gender neutrality and inclusivity throughout this act.

sections.heading: Investigatory Stops and Detention
sections.text:
This chapter may be cited as the "Police Detainment Act."

(a) This chapter shall dictate the powers and limitations of detainment by state certified peace officers, which shall extend to Conservation Officers established under Title 7 when acting in their official capacity.

(i) This section shall not apply to members of the National Guard serving in their official capacity, except state certified peace officers acting as Military Police.

The term "supervisor" shall refer to:

(a) Any employee tasked with supervisory roles by their respective department's policies, or as designated by the respective department head, or both.

The term "traffic stop" shall refer to:

(a) A temporary detention of a motor vehicle and its operator by a peace officer on a highway to investigate any motor vehicle infraction, or any other violation of State law. A traffic stop starts when the peace officer and the motor vehicle being pulled over come to a full stop at any reasonable place.

The term "interrogation" shall refer to:

(a) A temporary detention of a person by a peace officer where the person is informed of any relevant rights and is asked a series of questions by the peace officer. An interrogation starts when the peace officer finishes reading the detained person their relevant rights.

A traffic stop may not last more than twelve (12) minutes.

(a) After twelve (12) minutes have passed since the commencement of the traffic stop, all charges on the operator of the motor vehicle shall be void.

An interrogation may not last for more than forty-five (45) minutes.

(a) After forty-five (45) minutes have passed since the start of the interrogation, or the peace officer conducting the interrogation has terminated the interrogation, the peace officer has an additional fifteen (15) minutes to charge the detained person with a crime.

(b) If the peace officer conducting the interrogation takes longer than forty-five (45) minutes, no more questions may be asked and the interrogation shall conclude. The detained person shall be free to leave.

(i) This does not apply if the detained person willingly continues the interrogation. If the detained person willingly continues the interrogation, they shall be free to leave at any time unless the peace officer conducting the interrogation decides to charge the detained person with a crime, to which 4 M.S.C. 5 § 3202(a) shall take effect.

(c) Proceeding the termination of the interrogation, if the peace officer that was conducting the interrogation takes longer than the additional fifteen (15) minutes allocated to book the detained person, the charges against the detained person shall be void.

Any other detainment in any other setting shall not exceed more than twelve (12) minutes. For the purposes of this code, the detainment commences whenever the peace officer verbally informs the person that they are being detained, or places handcuffs on the person, or both.

(a) After twelve (12) minutes have passed since the commencement of the detainment, all charges against the detained person shall be void.

If a detained person requests a bar certified attorney, any timer relevant to the detainment shall be halted. Upon the arrival of the detained person's bar certified attorney, or the detained person has informed the peace officer that their bar ceritifed attorney is no longer coming, the relevant detainment timer shall resume.

Notwithstanding 4 M.S.C. 5 § 3202, an interrogation may last for up ninety (90) minutes provided the following conditions are met:

(a) the peace officer conducting the interrogation is employed by the same department as the detained person;

(b) the peace officer is a higher rank than the detained person in the department, or the peace officer is a member of that department's internal investigation unit formed under 4 M.S.C. 5 § 1701; and

(c) the detained person has not been interrogated within the past twelve (12) hours under 4 M.S.C. 5 § 3202.

(a) After ninety (90) minutes have passed since the start of the interrogation, or the peace officer conducting the interrogation has terminated the interrogation, the peace officer has an additional fifteen (15) minutes to charge the detained person with a crime. After the additional fifteen (15) minutes, all charges against the detained person shall be void.

If any detained person requests a supervisor, any relevant detainment timer shall halt, provided that the peace officer detaining the detained person is not a supervisor themselves. If the peace officer is considered a supervisor, they may act in the capacity of a supervisor for the purposes of the request.

(a) Upon the supervisor concluding the supervisor request, the relevant detainment timer shall resume.

No detainment timer shall apply if a person is being detained for the purposes of executing a warrant. Upon the warrant being executed, 4 M.S.C. 5 § 3203 shall apply.

No detainment timer shall apply if a person is being detained for the purposes of being transported pursuant to State law.

If a person does not verbally speak or otherwise indicate their presence for more than five (5) minutes, any relevant detainment shall end and the peace officer conducting the detainment shall either arrest or release the detained person.

Any contravention of this Chapter by any peace officer is considered a contravention of 4 M.S.C. 5 § 1305, for the purposes of 4 M.S.C. 5 § 2601.

sections.heading: Firearms Regulation
sections.text:
This chapter may be cited as the "Arms, Control, and Knowledge Act" or the "ACK ACT."

The term “firearm” shall refer to the definition prescribed by 4 M.S.C. 5 § 6101(a).

“Dispense” shall be defined as:

(a) Any firearm which is made available to a person through an equipment dispenser device of which the ability to dispense such a firearm is made available through employment or otherwise similar status within an authorized organization. This definition shall include though not be limited to firearms provided by government departments, agencies, or otherwise authorized authorities.

The term “automatic firearm” shall be defined as;

(a) Any self-loading firearm capable of continuously firing projectiles when the trigger mechanism is activated.

(b) Any self-loading firearm capable of firing multiple projectiles per a single activation of the trigger mechanism.

The term “firearm modification” shall be defined as;

(a) Any component, attachment, or accessory designed or used to alter or enhance the functionality, performance, or characteristics of a weapon from its original manufactured state, including but not limited to devices affecting rate of fire, accuracy, caliber, or concealability.

(b) Any physical modification of the mechanical or external components of a firearm from its original manufactured state.

(c) This definition shall include though not be limited to removable devices such as weapon optics, barrel attachments, and otherwise similar devices.

The term “Licensed Vendor” shall be defined as;

(a) Any individual person(s), organizations, private institutions or otherwise stores licensed to operate and participate in the trade and or sale of firearms,

The term “Illicit Vendor” shall be defined as;

(a) Any individual person(s), organizations, private institutions or otherwise stores which participate in the trade and or sale of firearms without being licensed to do so.

No individual shall be permitted to have within their possession a firearm in any capacity without having within their name a valid state issued firearms license.

(a) Any individual found to be in contravention of 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4401 shall be guilty 1 M.S.C. § 6102 Unlicensed Possession of a Firearm.

No individual shall be permitted to have within their possession a restricted-grade firearm in any capacity unless they are employed by, or otherwise affiliated with, an organization able to dispense, or are authorized by law to grant designated individuals permission to carry, such firearms as part of their official duties, and the organization has authorized the individual to carry such a firearm in the performance of their duties or otherwise lawful authorized environments.

(a) An individual authorized under 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4402 to carry a dispense firearm must be in compliance with all provisions of legislation related to the possession of such a firearm.

(b) A peace officer shall be temporarily authorized to possess a restricted-grade firearm which they are not otherwise authorized to possess under 4 M.S.C. § 4402 for the purposes of seizure and destruction, but must place the restricted-grade firearm in the trunk of a department-issued vehicle as soon as is practicably possible.

No individual shall be permitted to have within their possession any firearm sourced from an illicit vendor.

(a) Any individual found to be in contravention of 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4404 shall be guilty 1 M.S.C. § 6102 Unlicensed Possession of a Firearm.

A prospective Licensed Vendor must apply for a Firearm Trade Permit from the Commerce Office.

(a) The Commerce Office may create requirements to obtain a Firearm Trade Permit.

A Firearm Trade Permit may only be given out with the consent of the Lee County Sheriff.

The Commerce Office shall maintain a database of all active Firearm Trade Permits.

No individual or organization that fails to meet the definition of a Licensed Vendor shall engage in the trade of firearms of any designation.

(a) Any individual or organization found to be in contravention of 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4501 shall be guilty 1 M.S.C. § 6201 Unlawful dealing of a firearm.

A Licensed Vendor shall be permitted only to participate in the trade and or sale of firearms of which the possession of is not regulated by the provisions of this act (not including 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4301), provided both parties participating in the trade have within their name a valid state firearms license.

(a) Any individual or organization found to be in contravention of 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4502 shall be guilty 1 M.S.C. § 6201 Unlawful dealing of a firearm.

Any individual in possession of a firearm with a modification made to, affixed to, or installed on that serves any of the following purposes shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 6102: Unlicensed Possession of a Firearm;

(a) Barrel attachments or other modifications which suppress or otherwise silence the audible noise generated by the process of discharging a projectile.

(b) Modification to reduce the length of a firearms barrel to be less than three (3) studs in length, or to reduce the length of the firearm entirely to be less than six (6) studs.

No individual shall be permitted to have within their possession any form of firearm ammunition in any capacity without having within their name a valid state issued firearms license.

(a) Any individual found to be in contravention of 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4701 shall be guilty 1 M.S.C. § 6104 Unlicensed Possession of ammunition.

No individual shall be permitted to have within their possession any form of firearm ammunition sourced from an illicit vendor.

(a) Any individual found to be in contravention of 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4702 shall be guilty 1 M.S.C. § 6104 Unlicensed Possession of ammunition.

No individual who is not defined as a peace officer or active member of the armed services shall be permitted to have within their possession any form of firearm magazine which physically can service a surplus of twenty (20) rounds of ammunition.

(a) Any individual found to be in contravention of 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4703 shall be guilty 1 M.S.C. § 6103 Unauthorized possession of a high-capacity magazine.

No individual or organization that fails to meet the definition of a Licensed Vendor shall engage in the trade of ammunition in excess of more than five (5) magazines, boxes, clips or otherwise devices within a twelve (12) hour period.

(a) Any individual found to be in contravention of 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4704 shall be guilty 1 M.S.C. § 6104 Unlicensed Possession of ammunition.

(b) Any individual or organization which partakes in the trade of ammunition when both parties do not have within their possession a valid state firearms license shall be guilty 1 M.S.C. § 6202 Unlawful dealing of ammunition.

A Licensed Vendor shall be permitted only to participate in the trade and or sale of ammunition of which the possession of is not regulated by the provisions of this act (not including 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4201), provided both parties participating in the trade have within their name a valid state firearms license.

(a) Any individual found to be in contravention of 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4705 shall be guilty 1 M.S.C. § 6202 Unlawful dealing of ammunition.

A state issued firearm license shall only be issued to individuals who are lawful residents of the State of Mayflower.

A state issued firearm license shall be revoked by law enforcement officers if the holder of the license:

(a) Commits a crime involving the use, carriage, discharge or possession of a firearm, ammunition, or non-civilian equipment.

(b) Is a member of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization.

(c) Is deported from the State, or otherwise loses their residency.

A state issued firearm license shall be revoked for only 24 hours, unless otherwise specified by a court order.

Law enforcement officers who revoke a state issued firearm license must appropriately log the revocation in a manner deemed appropriate by the Attorney General.

If an individual with a firearm license is found in violation of a crime that would result in their firearm license being revoked, then any firearm or ammunition in their possession may be seized.

sections.heading: Public Safety Information and Whistleblowers
sections.text:
All Government run departments and agencies under the executive branch(es) of government, including law enforcement agencies, within the state shall be obligated to create and publish a public database, that is easily accessible within a separate public documents or similarly titled channel within a department’s communication server, and has:

(a) a registry of employees and each employees:

(i) assigned unit/division;

(ii) current position;

(iii) rank;

(iv) callsign/badge number; and

(v) complete disciplinary history;

(b) a code of conduct with all punitive titles as defined by 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1003;

(c) a list of all discharges; and

(d) a list of all administrative actions.

Any department or agency head who fails to comply with this subchapter shall be liable for Gross Misconduct and shall be prosecuted by the Department of Justice.

A “Whistleblower” shall be defined as a person who discloses information protected by a court order, nondisclosure agreement, state secrecy, or otherwise protected as permitted under this subchapter.

WHISTLEBLOWER PROTECTION. A whistleblower shall have the right to disclose information that is not otherwise publicly accessible, without threat of legal action, retaliation, or penalty, if the disclosure is made in good faith and based on a reasonable belief that one or more of the following conditions exists:

(a) A reasonable threat to public security or safety.

(b) Abuse by an authority.

(c) Violation of any law or regulation.

(d) Gross mismanagement.

A State Agency may not retaliate against a whistleblower in a manner including but not limited to:

(a) Threats.

(b) Demotion.

(c) Termination of employment.

(d) Legal action.

A whistleblower shall be guaranteed a return to their position of employment should a State Agency be found to have retaliated against the whistleblower.

A whistleblower's identity shall be kept confidential unless they consent to be revealed.

The protections of this subchapter shall apply regardless of whether the allegation is later substantiated, provided the whistleblower had a reasonable and honest belief at the time of disclosure.

No State Agency or official may require, as a condition of employment, any waiver or nondisclosure agreement that would limit or prohibit disclosures protected under this subchapter.

WHISTLEBLOWER PROTECTION; ENFORCEMENT. Should a whistleblower be retaliated against by a State Agency for the action of whistleblowing, then the State Agency will be liable to be subjected to various civil penalties as outlined by the Mayflower Tort Claims Act.

Any player that retaliates against a whistleblower for personal gain shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1302 “Felony Misconduct”.

Any player that retaliates against a whistleblower shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1303 “Gross Misconduct."

Any peace officer who has knowledge of retaliation but fails to report it shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 4202 “Attempt to commit a crime."

DEFINITIONS. A “State Agency” shall be defined as any government agency or department in the executive, legislative or judicial branch of the government.

A “FOIA requester” shall be defined as a resident of the State of Mayflower who is requesting materials as permitted under this act.

A “FOIA officer” or “Freedom of Information Access Officer” shall be defined as an employee of a State Agency who is responsible for responding to FOIA requests.

A “Whistleblower” shall be defined as a person who discloses information protected by a court order, nondisclosure agreement or state secrecy as permitted under this act.

FREEDOM OF INFORMATION REQUESTS. Residents of the State of Mayflower have the right to request access to any record or information of a state agency, except where it is exempted as:

(a) The file(s) are classified for the defence, security, or foreign policy of the state and the file(s) as a whole fall under a classification level as designated under Title 4, Chapter I, Subchapter II of the Mayflower State Code.

(b) The file(s) are trade secrets or confidential business records.

(c) The file(s) relate to personnel records, unless it is the personnel records of the FOIA requester.

(d) The file(s) relates to law enforcement records, operations, processes, information, techniques, or would deprive a person of the right to a fair trial, or reveal the identity of a confidential informant.

(e) The file(s) relate to a State Agency academy or education.

(f) The file(s) relate to foreign or domestic intelligence or counterintelligence.

(g) The file(s) relate to the identity of a witness.

If the file(s) that a FOIA requester is asking for does not exist, then the FOIA officer must notify the FOIA requester of such.

If the request submitted by the FOIA requester is too broad, then the FOIA officer may deny the request and notify the FOIA requester of such.

If file(s) requested by a FOIA requester contains lines, pages, portions, or media which is deemed to fall under a classification level as designated under Title 4, Chapter I, Subchapter II of the Mayflower State Code, then the FOIA officer must make a copy of the original file(s) and redact such information from the file(s), but not delete it, before submitting it to the FOIA requester where the reason for the redactions are clearly labelled.

When submitting a FOIA, the FOIA requester must ensure that they:

(a) Describe in as much detail as possible the file(s) being requested.

(b) Inform the State Agency of the purpose of the request.

Every state agency shall employ a Freedom of Information Access Officer.

(a) This employee may be a civilian employee.

(b) The department head of a State Agency shall be assumed to be the FOIA Officer should the role not be delegated to another individual.

The FOIA Officer shall be responsible for:

(a) Handling FOIA requests.

(b) Managing and publishing a publicly accessible FOIA request form for the state agency for which they are employed.

(c) Managing a database that contains all file(s) related to the State Agency for which they are employed.

(d) Further redacting file(s) which are requested by a FOIA requester so that it may be publicly viewable.

The Freedom of Information Access Officer must respond to a FOIA Requester within 4 days of a FOIA request and:

(a) Provide the FOIA requester with the requested information.

(b) Partially provide the FOIA requester with the requested information, and inform the FOIA requester that the remainder of the request is exempted from the request, and cite the exemption.

(c) Inform the FOIA requester that their request will not be fulfilled due to falling under an exemption, and cite the exemption.

(d) Inform the FOIA requester that the Freedom of Information Access Officer requires additional time to fulfil the request, and that it will be fulfilled within the next 3 days.

(e) Request that the FOIA requester further clarifies their request. Should this need arise, the time requirement shall reset upon the FOIA requester clarifying their request, or shall be denied should the FOIA requester not respond within 24 hours of the Freedom of Information Access Officer requesting the clarification.

FREEDOM OF INFORMATION ACCESS. Should a State Agency fail to respond to a FOIA request, then the FOIA requester may petition a court to order the release of the file(s) within 24 hours, unless the file(s) fall under an aforementioned exemption.

ENFORCEMENT. Should a State Agency fail to respond to a court order, then the FOIA officer shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1304 “Misconduct”.

sections.heading: Weapon Definitions
sections.text:
The term "firearm" shall refer to:

(a) Any weapon designed to fire a projectile at a high velocity through the use of explosive force.

The term “firearm free zone” shall refer to:

(a) The interior of a building or area that has a proper signature prohibiting the carrying of firearms, or any other area specified in this act where the carrying of a firearm visibly or concealed is prohibited, shall extend to the following areas:

(i) The entire property of the Mayflower State House, Camp McEntree, or any law enforcement headquarters or sub-station, or any county fire station, or any courthouse, municipal or county hall, or administration building.

(ii) Any place where healthcare or medical treatment is administered, such as hospital.

(iii) Any religious place of worship.

(iv) Any place where individuals are taught, such as a school or university.

(b) Any property that has a proper signature prohibiting the carrying of firearms where its use is for an aviation purpose.

The term "melee weapon" shall refer to:

(a) Hand held items which are capable of causing harm when swung.

The term "melee free zone" shall refer to:

(a) The interior of a building or area that has a proper signature prohibiting the carrying of melee weapons, or any other area specified in this act where the carrying of a melee weapon visibly or concealed is prohibited, shall extend to the following areas:

(i) The entire property of the Mayflower State House, or any courthouse, municipal or county hall.

(ii) Subway Terminals, Subway Platforms, or Subway Stations.

It shall be unlawful for any individual to carry a firearm within a firearm free zone, either it being visible or concealed, but shall not extend to the following:

(a) It shall be unlawful for any individual to carry a firearm within a firearm free zone, either it being visibly or concealed, but shall not extend to the following:

(i) Members of law enforcement, emergency services, or the national guard, whether they are on-duty or off-duty, being the said member is in possession of an active and valid state firearms license.

(ii) Members of the state legislature, that being state senators, chief clerks, and assistant clerks, etc., requiring that they are in the Mayflower State House and currently attending a senate session in the senate chambers or executing in their official duties.

(iii) Members of the state executive branch, that being the governor, lieutenant governor, members of the cabinet, and executive staff, requiring they are in the Mayflower State House or on the property of Camp McEntree and currently executing in their official duties, or any other authorized individuals from the governor or lieutenant governor, requiring they are in the Mayflower State House or on the property of Camp McEntree.

(iv) Members of the judicial branch, that being the chief justice, associate justices, chief judge, judges, magistrates, and clerks, or members of the Department of Justice, that being the attorney general, deputy attorney general, assistant attorney general, solicitor general, inspector general, state attorney, and legal staff, etc., requiring that they are in any courthouse and currently executing in their official duties.

It shall be unlawful for any individual to carry a melee weapon within a melee free zone, either it being visibly or concealed, but shall not extend to the following:

sections.heading: Controlled Burns
sections.text:
“Burn Permit” shall mean a certification, issued by the Controlled Burns & Explosives Office, authorizing a law enforcement officer and/or Special Forces member to destroy civilian vehicles that meet the specific requirements prescribed by regulation.

“Burn” shall refer to the action taken by a law enforcement officer in exploding a vehicle in a safe and controlled manner.

“Special Vehicle” shall refer to a vehicle not accessible for purchase by all members of the public, that is issued by Community Oversight for the usage of an organization and is only possible to be spawned by members of such an organization.

The Burn Assessment and Burn Guide shall include but are not limited to including the following information:

(a) All safety regulations ensuring the lack of harm towards others.

(b) All safety regulations ensuring the lack of chain reaction explosions.

(c) Legal premises allowing for a vehicle to be burnt.

(d) Allowed properties for Burns to be carried out on.

All law enforcement officers and Special Forces members who wish to carry out Burns must hold an active Burn Permit Certification, issued by the Controlled Burns & Explosives Office.

All law enforcement officers and Special Forces members without prior history of misconduct relating to Burns shall be eligible for a Burn Permit, and must achieve 85% (eighty five percent) or higher in the Burn Permit Assessment.

Controlled Burns & Explosives Office shall be obliged to open the Burn Permit Assessment indefinitely throughout all times of the year and regularly mark responses, releasing results and issuing Burn Permits every 2 (two) weeks or less.

The Controlled Burns & Explosives Office shall be obliged to release and regularly review a forum for members of the public to report misconduct pertaining to Burns, and shall be obliged to investigate each report to the fullest.

The Controlled Burns & Explosives Office shall reserve the right to blacklist, revoke or suspend Burn Permits from law enforcement officers found to be in violation of the Burn Guide and other regulations clearly set by the Controlled Burns & Explosives Office. The severity of the administrative action shall be based on the severity of the misconduct committed, however shall be to the discretion of the Controlled Burns & Explosives Office.

Whilst the Controlled Burns & Explosives Office shall be entrusted with releasing safety regulations through their Burn Guide, the following details must be met for a vehicle to be eligible to be burnt;

(a) Vehicle contains 10 (ten) or more items defined by State Laws to be illegal for possession by the registered vehicle owner.

A vehicle with less than 10 (ten) items illegal for possession by the registered vehicle owner may be burnt by law enforcement officers only if the vehicle is a special vehicle registered to be owned by a member of a criminal street gang or terrorist organization, as declared by the Attorney General.

“Special Forces” shall be defined as the 19th Special Forces Group (AIRBORNE), an operational unit of the Mayflower National Guard, permanently stationed at Fort Standish.

“Special Forces member” shall be defined as an enlisted soldier or commissioned officer who is a duly assigned and qualified member of the 19th Special Forces Group (AIRBORNE) of the Mayflower National Guard, having completed all requisite training, certification, and assignment criteria as established by applicable military regulations and directives.

sections.heading: Prohibited Goods
sections.text:
Any item within this section shall be known as Prohibited Goods.

It shall be illegal for an individual to be in unlawful possession of any goods listed in this subchapter.

The following items shall collectively be known as ‘Prohibited Goods, Class I’, or any other similar name

(a) Items, kits, or modifications tools that can be used to modify an automatic firearm;

(b) Items, kits, or modification tools which can cause a firearm that is not an automatic firearm to become so;

(c) Law enforcement exclusive equipment.

The following items shall collectively be known as ‘Prohibited Goods, Class II', or any other similar name:

(a) Items, kits, or modifications tools that can be used to modify a firearm;

(b) Crates containing illegal firearms;

(c) Crates containing illegal ammunition.

(d) Gavels; and

(e) Items which show membership, admittance or allegiance to a criminal organization or enterprise.

The following items shall collectively be known as ‘Prohibited Goods, Class III’, or any other similar name:

(a) Gold Bars;

(b) Silver Bars;

(c) Dirty Money;

(d) Encrypted Phone;

(e) Military Encryption Cards; and

(f) File of Military Intelligence.

(g) Underground Firearms Access Card.

(h) Lockpicks.

“Underground Firearms Access Card” shall refer to any physical or digital card, token, pass, code, or other medium designed, issued, or possessed for the primary purpose of granting or facilitating entry to any building, room, or premises where firearms, firearm parts, or firearm modification kits are offered, transferred, or sold in violation of the laws of the State of Mayflower. Possession of such a card shall be unlawful unless by a law-enforcement officer or other person acting under the authority of a law-enforcement agency in the course of official duties.

“Lockpick” shall refer to any device, tool, or instrument designed, adapted, or primarily used for the purpose of unlocking a lock without the use of the key or code intended by the lock’s manufacturer, except when possessed by a duly licensed locksmith, a person acting under the direction of a law-enforcement agency, or a person possessing such tools solely for lawful occupational, educational, or hobbyist purposes unrelated to any unlawful entry.

Any item within this section shall be known as Controlled Substance.

It shall be illegal for an individual to be in possession of:

(a) Nopyfruit, except when in its concentrated form;

(b) Jarniwanus, in any form; or

(c) Gushie, in any form.

The Department of Justice shall maintain a publicly accessible registry containing a list of Prohibited Goods and Controlled Substances found within this chapter.

Any person who is found in possession of an item which is a Prohibited Good, Class I shall be liable for arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 1702 "Possession of Prohibited Goods I."

Any person who is found in possession of an item which is a Prohibited Good, Class II shall be liable for citation or arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 1703 "Possession of Prohibited Goods II."

Any person who is found in possession of an item which is a Prohibited Good, Class III shall be liable for citation or arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 1704 "Possession of Prohibited Goods III."

Any person who is found in possession of an item which is a Controlled Substance which weighs up or equal to 15 weight units shall be liable for citation or arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 1706 "Petty Possession of Controlled Goods."

Any person who is found in possession of an item which is a Controlled Substance, which weighs between or equal to 16 and 30 weight units, shall be liable for citation or arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 1707 "Grand Possession of Controlled Goods."

Any person who is found in possession of a Controlled Substance in a weight greater or equal to 31 weight units shall be liable for arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 1708 "Felony Possession of Controlled Goods."

Gavels shall only be possessed by:

(a) The President of the Senate and their designated Senator(s).

(b) Justices and Judges of the State Judiciary.

sections.heading: Security Officers
sections.text:
“Criminal Organization” shall refer to any organization labelled placed on the Mayflower State Criminal Organization Registry by the Attorney General.

“Street Gang” shall refer to any organization with less than 30 (thirty) active members taking part in crimes against the State Code that do not require a conviction in order to issue prison sentences for.

“Senior Member” shall refer to any member of a Criminal Organization who holds a position of command in such an organization and is capable of directing subordinates to take part in organized criminal activity.

The Attorney General shall have the power to designate any organization as a Criminal Organization as he deems fit and appropriate, however such orders may be overturned by the Governor (with such overturns being open to counter-overturning by the Senate).

The Governor shall wield the power to revoke the residency of any senior member of a Criminal Organization, with the advice of the State Security Council and other such advisors with knowledge as to the capabilities and identities of senior criminals.

The Attorney General shall have the power to designate any organization as a Street Gang as he deems fit and appropriate.

The Attorney General shall maintain an up-to-date, publicly available database displaying information pertaining to Street Gangs, their operations and their known members.

The Governor shall wield the power to revoke the residency of any senior member of a Street Gang, with the advice of the State Security Council and other such advisors with knowledge as to the capabilities and identities of such Street Gang leaders.
