sections.heading: Private Security Services
sections.text:
This chapter is established to provide provisional laws pertaining to the authority, training, and accountability of private security firms and the services which they provide.

This chapter may be cited as the “Security Services Act.”

A proprietary security guard shall be defined as an employee who is employed exclusively by any one employer whose primary duty is to provide security services for his or her employer, whose services are not contracted out to any other entity.

A proprietary private security employer shall be defined as a person who has one or more employees who provide security services for the employer and only the employer. A person who employs proprietary security guards pursuant to this definition at more than one location owned and operated by the employer shall still be considered a single employer

A security guard or security officer shall be defined as an employee of a private patrol operator who is licensed to and performs the duties of a private patrol operator in compliance with the provisions of this Chapter.

A private patrol operator and or any other variation thereof shall be defined as a person and or organization, who, for any consideration whatsoever; agrees to furnish, or furnishes a security officer or guard, or other person to protect persons or property to prevent the theft, loss, embezzlement, or concealment of any goods, merchandise, money, or property of any kind; or performs the service of a security officer or guard for any of these purposes.

The Department of State shall form a commission responsible for the enforcement of the provisions of this Chapter. Furthermore this commission shall be uniquely responsible for the issuance, suspension, and revocation of security licenses in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter.

The Department of State shall draft, maintain and issue an examination of which the passing of shall be required for an individual to acquire a security license from the Department of State.

The Department of State shall be provided a document titled the “Power to Arrest Training Manual,” which shall detail the provisions of this Chapter in an attempt to educate those seeking a security license from the Department of State. Using this document, the State Department shall either be responsible for the administration of the required curriculum. Or, they may permit a registered business to do so on behalf of the State, so long as they meet all the same curriculum requirements the Department of State upholds.

(a) The Department of State shall maintain a roster of businesses that have been given permission to render security training.

(b) The Department of State shall maintain a publicly accessible form for businesses to request a training waiver.

The Commission which the State Department designates to oversee the management of security license shall be permitted to modify license status only in the following situations:

(a) A security license may be issued only if an individual has completed the required training process and passed the required examination, or otherwise has an exemption provided by this Chapter.

(b) A security license may be suspended if the holder has failed to maintain citizenship status, or is the subject of official investigation by the State Department or the investigative unit of any law enforcement agency, or representative of the Department of Justice.

(c) For a security license to be revoked, the specific license holder must meet one the following criteria:

(i) Previous active conviction in a court of law of any criminal offense other than an infraction.

(ii) Four in total or more active misdemeanor records and/or three in total or more active felony records, of which are not actively being disputed or in the process to do so through a court of law.

(iii) Conviction by a court of a felony violation or multiple (or consecutive) violations of state law within twenty-four (24) hours, where such violations are determined by the Commission.

(iv) Repeated, or serious violation of the Security Services Act or any other private security regulation promulgated by the Department of State.

(d) A security license may be suspended as a result of an investigation conducted by the Department of State for a time specified in the investigation report that does not exceed thirty (30) days.

(i) A security license may be suspended for the duration of a criminal trial in which the holder is charged with any criminal offense other than an infraction.

An individual applicant may not be issued a security license by the State Department if the applicant meets one of the criterion found within 4 M.S.C. 6 § 1304(c) that would normally warrant a license revocation.

A license may not be issued to an applicant without active residency.

The State Department shall be permitted to, on an individual basis, exempt an applicant from the required training and examination if the applicant is an active peace officer as defined by the State code, or an otherwise honorably discharged person which previously held such a position.

Training Waiver shall be defined as, “A waiver granted to businesses permitting them to render security training themselves as opposed to through the Department of State.”

Any individual seeking employment as a security officer employed by a private patrol operator, or wishing to incorporate or otherwise establish an organization defined as a private patrol operator shall be required to maintain an active security license from the Department of State.

(a) Proprietary security guards shall be required to maintain an active security license to carry a firearm while acting in the capacity of a proprietary security guard.

Previous to being issued a license the applicant shall complete a course of training in the exercise of the power of arrest, a course in the training of carrying and use of firearms, and the general use of force regarding specialized tools and equipment.

An individual representing the organization of which they are employed and acting in the capacity of a security officer or proprietary security guard shall be required to display a unique uniform compliant with this Chapter designated by their employer.

(a) For the purpose of this code, a uniform shall be considered compliant if it aligns with all of the following components:

(i) A uniform which bears at least one patch, badge, ID, logo, or otherwise emblem visible at all times clearly identifying the employing company.

(ii) Authorized officers may perform duties regulated under this chapter in 'non uniformed' status on a limited special assignment basis, and only when duty circumstances or special requirements of the client necessitate such dress. Licensees who are performing bodyguard or executive protection services may choose to carry their authorized equipment while in non uniformed status as needed in the conduct of such services.

(b) Security officers and or proprietary security guards which fail to comply with the uniform mandate shall not receive any protection or exemption by the provisions of this act.

A licensed private security officer or licensed proprietary security guard which has in their possession a valid firearms license shall be permitted to carry and display in public and/or in a restricted or otherwise firearms freezone, if the aforementioned restricted or otherwise firearms freezone is within the reasonable scope of their duties, a loaded firearm.

A licensed security officer shall be permitted to carry on their person and utilize, when on duty and conducting official security duties, and in accordance with provisions of State law the following articles of equipment and their respective ammunition or otherwise essential components; extendable, fixed and straight batons, stun guns or taser devices, pepper-spray or other similar chemical self-defense items, encrypted handheld radios, fixed or chain connected handcuffs; and the Bennetti 17 pistol.

A private security officer specifically directed to do so by an on-duty peace officer as defined by the State Code may be permitted to assist in the detainment, arrest, or capture of a criminal wrongdoer; however, security officers shall never, under any circumstances, be authorized to engage or assist directly or indirectly, in a vehicular pursuit. Private security officers may be permitted to close or block public roadways if authorized to do so by an on-duty supervisor of a law enforcement agency to ensure public safety during significant emergencies.

A security officer may only protect an asset, property or person when the security entity they are employed by has a contract or signed agreement to protect such asset, property or person and said security officer is authorized by his employer to provide such protective services.

For the purposes of this Subchapter, the term “authorized officer” shall be defined as a security officer, or proprietary security guard.

Peace officers defined by the State code discharging the authority of arrest on behalf of the State involved in the secondary duty of an authorized officer shall be exempt from the provisions of this Subchapter.

An authorized officer shall be permitted to hold an individual within their custody only under the following conditions:

(a) For an codified offense of the State code punishable by arrest committed or attempted within the presence of an authorized officer.

(b) For a codified felony offense of the State code which the authorized officer has evidence of such an offense although not not committed within their presence.

(c) When ordered to do so by a peace officer as defined by the State code. Such a detention shall be considered an action on behalf of the peace officer rather than the authorized officer.

Upon effecting an arrest, an authorized officer shall be required to contact a peace officer within a reasonable timeframe to take custody of the violator and provide the peace officer with evidence of the offense which the individual was arrested for.

An authorized officer shall have the sole authority to conduct an arrest with reasonable and plausible cause to do so. Upon affecting an arrest a authorized officer may not release a violator unless ordered to do so by a peace officer or due to emergent circumstances. Unlike a peace officer, an authorized officer shall not be permitted to detain a person for investigative purposes, and as such may only hold a person within their custody to effect an arrest.

Upon an arrest being effected, an authorized officer must immediately inform the individual which is within their custody of the crime which they are being arrested for, and their authority to do so.

An authorized officer attempting to effect an arrest may utilize handcuffs or similar devices to hold an individual within their custody. Furthermore authorized officers shall be permitted to use a reasonable amount of force to prevent the evasion, or resistance of such an arrest.

An authorized officer may transit an arrested individual within their custody to a holding room or hold them within a marked security vehicle whilst awaiting peace officer arrival.

An authorized officer may search the person of an arrested individual though may only remove weapons, and must transfer seized items to a peace officer upon arrival. Additionally an authorized officer may search the person of any individual which consents to such a search.

The authority granted under 4 M.S.C. 6 § 1603 (a) and (b) shall only be exercised under the following conditions:

(a) The authorized officer is actively engaged in the protection of a contracted property, person, or asset, and is either on, in, or in the immediate vicinity of that property, person, or asset; or

(b) When not in the immediate vicinity of a property, person, or asset they are contracted and authorized to protect, but during exigent circumstances to protect human life. This subsection shall not be construed to allow authorized officers to patrol or seek out criminal wrongdoers not within the scope of their official security duties to protect a contracted property, asset, or person.

Any individual who without a license attempts to, or operates a private patrol operator service shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1406 “Unlawful Operation of a Business” and/or 1 M.S.C. § 1318 “Impersonation of a Private Security Officer” if applicable.

Any private patrol operator which knowingly employs an individual without a security license as a security officer within their organization shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1406 “Unlawful Operation of a Business.“

Any individual which acts in the capacity of a security officer without having in their possession an active security license shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1318 “Impersonation of a Private Security Officer."

A proprietary security guard which carries on their person a firearm whilst representing the proprietary security employer and does not have in their possession an active security license shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 6102 “Unlicensed Possession of a Firearm.”

Any individual which attempts to exercise the exemptions or authority of a security officer, proprietary security guard, or private patrol operator without total compliance with the provisions of this Chapter shall receive no exemption or protection from liability which is found therein.

A private security officer specifically directed to do so by an on-duty peace officer as defined by the State Code may be permitted to assist in the detainment, arrest, or capture of a criminal wrongdoer; however, security officers shall never, under any circumstances, be authorized to engage or assist directly or indirectly, in a vehicular pursuit. Private security officers may be permitted to close or block public roadways if authorized to do so by an on-duty supervisor of a law enforcement agency to ensure public safety during significant emergencies.

A security officer may only protect an asset, property or person when the security entity they are employed by has a contract or signed agreement to protect such asset, property or person and said security officer is authorized by his employer to provide such protective services.

parts.heading: Subchapter VI — POWER TO ARREST; AUTHORITY TO ARREST
parts.text:
For the purposes of this Subchapter, the term “authorized officer” shall be defined as a security officer, or proprietary security guard.

Peace officers defined by the State code discharging the authority of arrest on behalf of the State involved in the secondary duty of an authorized officer shall be exempt from the provisions of this Subchapter.

An authorized officer shall be permitted to hold an individual within their custody only under the following conditions:

(a) For an codified offense of the State code punishable by arrest committed or attempted within the presence of an authorized officer.

(b) For a codified felony offense of the State code which the authorized officer has evidence of such an offense although not not committed within their presence.

(c) When ordered to do so by a peace officer as defined by the State code. Such a detention shall be considered an action on behalf of the peace officer rather than the authorized officer.

Upon effecting an arrest, an authorized officer shall be required to contact a peace officer within a reasonable timeframe to take custody of the violator and provide the peace officer with evidence of the offense which the individual was arrested for.

An authorized officer shall have the sole authority to conduct an arrest with reasonable and plausible cause to do so. Upon affecting an arrest a authorized officer may not release a violator unless ordered to do so by a peace officer or due to emergent circumstances. Unlike a peace officer, an authorized officer shall not be permitted to detain a person for investigative purposes, and as such may only hold a person within their custody to effect an arrest.

Upon an arrest being effected, an authorized officer must immediately inform the individual which is within their custody of the crime which they are being arrested for, and their authority to do so.

An authorized officer attempting to effect an arrest may utilize handcuffs or similar devices to hold an individual within their custody. Furthermore authorized officers shall be permitted to use a reasonable amount of force to prevent the evasion, or resistance of such an arrest.

An authorized officer may transit an arrested individual within their custody to a holding room or hold them within a marked security vehicle whilst awaiting peace officer arrival.

An authorized officer may search the person of an arrested individual though may only remove weapons, and must transfer seized items to a peace officer upon arrival. Additionally an authorized officer may search the person of any individual which consents to such a search.

The authority granted under 4 M.S.C. 6 § 1603 (a) and (b) shall only be exercised under the following conditions:

(a) The authorized officer is actively engaged in the protection of a contracted property, person, or asset, and is either on, in, or in the immediate vicinity of that property, person, or asset; or

(b) When not in the immediate vicinity of a property, person, or asset they are contracted and authorized to protect, but during exigent circumstances to protect human life. This subsection shall not be construed to allow authorized officers to patrol or seek out criminal wrongdoers not within the scope of their official security duties to protect a contracted property, asset, or person.

parts.heading: Subchapter VII — ENFORCEMENT
parts.text:
Any individual who without a license attempts to, or operates a private patrol operator service shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1406 “Unlawful Operation of a Business” and/or 1 M.S.C. § 1318 “Impersonation of a Private Security Officer” if applicable.

Any private patrol operator which knowingly employs an individual without a security license as a security officer within their organization shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1406 “Unlawful Operation of a Business.“

Any individual which acts in the capacity of a security officer without having in their possession an active security license shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1318 “Impersonation of a Private Security Officer."

A proprietary security guard which carries on their person a firearm whilst representing the proprietary security employer and does not have in their possession an active security license shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 6102 “Unlicensed Possession of a Firearm.”

Any individual which attempts to exercise the exemptions or authority of a security officer, proprietary security guard, or private patrol operator without total compliance with the provisions of this Chapter shall receive no exemption or protection from liability which is found therein.

sections.heading: Security Services Regulation
sections.text:
An act to establish regulations around financial reporting for larger companies within the State of Mayflower and implementing financial crimes within the Mayflower Criminal Code.

this act may be cited as "The Second Finance Act."

A fiscal period is a single month, starting on the first of the month and ending the last day of the month.

A fiscal quarter shall be defined as follows, with the quarter starting on the first day of the specified month and ending on the last day of the other specified month:

(a) Quarter 1: October to December.

(b) Quarter 2: January to March.

(c) Quarter 3: April to June.

(d) Quarter 4: July to September.

A fiscal year shall be defined as the 12-month period beginning 1 October and ending 30 September the following year.

References for fiscal years shall be made as “The [fiscal/financial] year of [the calendar year the fiscal year started in]”.

The term "commercial instrument" shall be defined to mean any document or item utilized in the course of commercial transactions or business operations that holds legal or financial significance that evidences, constitutes, or facilitates a business or financial transaction.

All Financial Statements that are required by law must meet requirements adopted by the Governor’s Office.

(a) The Governor shall be obligated to create a position within his office to accommodate this.

All businesses registered with the Department of State that offer stocks, bonds or investment contracts are obligated to prepare and publish the following financial statements every fiscal quarter:

(a) A Statement of Cash Flows

(b) A Balance Sheet

(c) Income Statement

All required Financial Statements must be made public within three (3) days of the end of each fiscal quarter.

All financial statements submitted to the SEC must be complete and accurate.

CASINO FINANCIALS. This chapter/Subchapter of the State Code is established to provide laws pertaining to the oversight, regulation, fairness, transparency, and accountability of Casino and Online Games websites and operations run within, or operating within, the State of Mayflower.

Businesses conducting gambling or casino like operations, herein “Casino” must be responsible for transparency with their financials, and shall be obligated to prepare and publicly announce the following Financial Statements every fiscal quarter:

(a) A Statement of Cash Flows.

(b) A Balance Sheet.

(c) Income Statement.

(d) Ledger of Cash Disbursements.

A Casino may not permit an individual user to withdraw more than $7,000,000 of their deposits/winnings at the casino in a 7 day period.

CONSUMER PROTECTIONS. Businesses conducting casino-like operations must be responsible for listing odds for all games. Whether it is in percentile or fraction format, the odds for all games. The odds must be displayed in a manner that a reasonable person would be able to properly read from a reasonable distance.

Casinos must disclose publicly and visibly any and all games in which the “house” or the business is favored to win the game, or in other words, where the person has a 49% chance or less to win.

Casinos must publicly report changes in odds, gameplay, or any other mechanic that may alter the experience of the casino in any way when the changes are made and in a monthly report. If there is no alteration as described above, a monthly report need not be published.

Any advertisement or promotion for Casinos must provide, in visible font and coloring that a reasonable person can see from a reasonable distance, a support website for chronic gambling addictions.

Should there be discrepancies or inaccuracies the Attorney General or District Attorney should direct an investigative agency to investigate the matter.

The Attorney General or District Attorney may take enforcement through civil and/or criminal court as prescribed by law.

Businesses that fail to comply with the prescribed Financial Reporting requirements will result in the business owner(s) being subject to various civil penalties as outlined by the Mayflower Tort Claims Act.

(a) This shall primarily fall under Negligent and Economic Torts but shall not be limited to such.

Businesses that fail to comply with the prescribed Financial Reporting requirements will result in the business owner(s) being subject to criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 1406 (Unlawful Operation of a Business) if—

(a) The business in question has been non-compliant with Financial Reporting requirements prescribed by law for a cumulative period of twenty one (30) days.

A new Chapter within the Mayflower Criminal Code shall be created: “Financial Crimes."

All crimes within Section IV of the Financial Reporting and Crimes Act shall be classified as Financial Crimes.

The following crimes shall be created and codified within the Mayflower Criminal Code:

“Bank Robbery” shall be created and defined as follows:

(a) Any person whether by force or intimidation, that takes any property or money in the care, custody, control, etc. of any bank, credit union, or savings and loan institution.

(b) Shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 30 minutes in prison.

(c) This statue shall be set to active within the Mayflower Criminal Code.

“Money Laundering” shall be created and defined as follows:

(a) Any person, knowing that the property involved in a financial transaction represents the proceeds of some form of unlawful activity, conducts or attempts to conduct such a financial transaction which in fact involves the proceeds of unlawful activity with the intent to promote the carrying on of specified unlawful activity; or knowing that the transaction is designed in whole or in part;

(i) to conceal or disguise the nature, the location, the source, the ownership, or the control of the proceeds of specified unlawful activity; or

(ii) to avoid a transaction reporting requirement under Local, State or Federal law;

(b) Shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 30 minutes in prison and/or face a fine of not more than $5,000 or twice the value of the property involved in the transaction, whichever is greater.

(c) This statue shall be set to active within the Mayflower Criminal Code.

“Embezzlement” shall be created and defined as follows:

(a) A person who shall, having lawful custody of property not his or her own, appropriate the same to his or her own use, with intent to deprive the owner thereof;

(b) Shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 50 minutes in prison and/or face a fine of not more than $5,000 or twice the value of the property involved in the transaction, whichever is greater.

(c) This statue shall be set to By Conviction within the Mayflower Criminal Code.

“Counterfeiting” shall be created and defined as follows:

(a) Any person, with intent to defraud, falsely makes, forges, counterfeits, or alters any obligation or other security of the State of Mayflower or Union of Columbia;

(b) Shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 120 minutes in prison.

(c) This statue shall be set to By Conviction within the Mayflower Criminal Code.

1 M.S.C. § 1301 “Bribery” shall be reclassified as a Financial Crime.

“Loan Sharking” shall be added and defined as follows: Any Lender who provides a loan not in accordance with Usury Laws or Loan Prohibitions shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 25 minutes in prison and/or face a fine of not more than $20,000 or twice the value of the loan, whichever is greater.

Commercial instrument falsification in the second degree’ shall be defined as follows: Any person who, with intent to defraud, knowingly falsifies, alters, or forges any commercial instrument shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.

sections.heading: Enforcement and Arrest Powers
sections.text:
A “Borrower” shall be defined as a person or business who is loaned money from a Lender.

A “Lender” shall be defined as a business which loans money to a Borrower.

A “loan” shall be defined as a sum of money or other asset provided by a Lender to a Borrower under an agreement that it will be repaid in the future, typically with interest as compensation for the use of the funds.

An “interest rate” shall be defined as “the percentage charged or paid on the principal amount of a loan or deposit, calculated over a specified period, as agreed between the Lender and Borrower or deposit holder and institution.”

A “collateral” shall be defined as an asset or property offered by a Borrower to be given to the Lender should the Borrower fail to repay the loan.

This chapter may be cited as the "Loan Shark Extinction Act."

A Lender must have the loan readily available to the Borrower upon effect of the loan.

The Borrower must repay the loan and in full to the Lender by the conclusion of the loan.

A Lender may request collateral from a Borrower as a security against a loan.

(a) The collateral must be agreed in writing in the same document the loan is signed on.

(b) Should the Borrower fail to repay the loan, the collateral shall automatically be transferred to the ownership of the Lender.

A loan may only be offered by a Lender where the Borrower can repay the loan in whole, or at an agreed rate or repayment of weekly, fortnightly, monthly, once every two months, quarterly, once every 6 months, or yearly.

An interest rate may not be larger than:

(a) 40% of a principle where the loan rate of repayment is of weekly or fortnightly recurrence.

(b) 35% of a principle where the loan rate of repayment is monthly, once every two months, or quarterly.

(c) 30% of a principle where the loan rate of repayment is once every 6 months, or yearly.

A loan may not include:

(a) Hidden fees.

(b) Clauses that waive the rights of a Borrower.

(c) Clauses that unfairly benefit the Lender.

A Lender may not:

(a) Use methods of threats, coercion, harassment or intimidation to collect loan repayments.

(b) Offer a loan where the Borrower has no reasonable method to repay it.

Borrowers that fail to repay a loan as agreed by the Lender shall be liable to be subjected to various civil penalties as outlined by the Mayflower Tort Claims Act.

The Attorney General or District Attorney may take enforcement of Usury Laws through civil and/or criminal court as prescribed by law.

Lenders that fail to comply with the prescribed Usury Laws or Loan Prohibitions will result in the business owners being subject to criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 1606 “Loan Sharking”.

Lenders that use threats, coercion, harassment or intimidation to collect loan repayments shall be subject to criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 2308 “Extortion”.

sections.heading: Administrative Discipline
sections.text:
The term “Insurance Policy” shall refer to an agreement between a Policyholder and Insurance Business where the Insurance Business agrees that they will payout a Policyholder as a result of a successful Claim.

The term “Policyholder” shall refer to a person or organization which is issued an insurance policy by an Insurance Business.

The term “Insurance Business” shall refer to a licensed business which provides insurance to a Policyholder.

The term “Claim” shall refer to when a Policyholder makes a request to the Insurance Business for compensation or coverage as dictated by an insurance policy.

The term “Premium” shall refer to the charge that a Policyholder receives from the Insurance Business to be covered by insurance, typically at a recurring rate.

An Insurance Business owner must satisfy the following requirments to be permitted to conduct business as an Insurance Business:

(a) Have a minimum capital of the result of the following formula:

(i) (n*C)+(C*3);

(ii) Where n is the maximum amount of persons the Insurance Business is going to insure; and

(iii) Where C is the maximum Claim amount that an Insurance Business is going to compensate for.

(b) Provide the Commerce Office a prospective business report that includes, in the order as listed:

(i) The names of all stakeholders in the business;

(ii) The names of any stakeholders in the business that have owned an Insurance Business which has been insolvent.

(iii) The maximum amount of Policyholders the Insurance Business is to insure;

(iv) The maximum Claim the Insurance Business is to insure for;

(v) The total capital the owner of the Insurance Business possesses; and

(vi) Plans on how to pay out Policyholders in case of insolvency.

(c) If an Insurance Business desires to change the maximum Claim or maximum Policyholders after registration, then the Insurance Business must submit a new prospective business report

The Commerce Office must deny any application to be a licensed Insurance Business where:

(a) The Insurance Business owner has been charged with any crime listed under Subtitle 1, Chapter IV of the Mayflower Criminal Code.

(b) The Insurance Business owner has been charged with any crime listed under Subtitle 1, Chapter VI of the Mayflower Criminal Code.

(c) The Insurance Business owner has been charged with any crime listed under Subtitle 5 of the Mayflower State Code.

(d) The Insurance Business owner has failed to properly file a prospective business report.

Insurance Businesses must clearly outline all types of Insurance Policies and its individual rules provided by the Insurance Business in a clear and discernable method, which is publicly accessible, which includes:

(a) How the Insurance Policy applies to the Policyholder;

(b) The Premium of the Insurance Policy;

(c) The term of coverage that the Policyholder receives for the Insurance Policy; and

(d) An example on how the Insurance Policy will compensate the Policyholder.

Every month, if a Policyholder submits a Claim to the Insurance Business, the Insurance Business must publish a summary claims report which is publicly accessible that includes:

(a) The total amount of Claims submitted by Policyholders;

(b) The total amount of Claims accepted by the Insurance Business;

(c) The total amount of Claims rejected by the Insurance Business, with their reason(s) for rejection;

(d) The total amount of Policyholders, including the difference from the previous public report;

(e) Any changes to an Insurance Policy;

(f) Any loans that the Insurance Business has obtained to finance the Insurance Business, and the amount of money the loan is worth;

(g) Any court convictions against the Insurance Business;

(h) Any commercial punishments against the Insurance Business by the Commerce Office; and

(i) A link to the prospective business report.

Every six months an Insurance Business must submit a summary claims report, regardless if a Claim was submitted by a Policyholder that month.

An Insurance Business may not:

(a) Use methods of threats, coercion, harassment or intimidation to collect a premium; and

(b) Offer an Insurance Policy where the Policyholder has no reasonable method to repay it.

An Insurance Business may only change the rules of an Insurance Policy every 30 days.

Such a change must be publicly announced seven days before the change comes into effect.

Should the premium of an Insurance Policy be changed, a Policyholder who is already covered by the Insurance Policy shall not have their premium affected for more or less until they are required to pay their Premium again.

An Insurance Policy may not include:

(a) Hidden fees;

(b) Clauses that waive the right of the Policyholder; and

(c) Clauses that unfairly benefit the Lender.

A premium may not be more than:

(a) 10% of the maximum Claim if the premium is paid at an increment of time that is monthly, or shorter; or

(b) 15% of the maximum Claim if the premium is paid at an increment of time that is longer than monthly.

A Policyholder may not fraudulently submit a Claim to an Insurance Business.

There may not be a “cooldown” period for submitting a Claim.

An Insurance Business may only reject to compensate for a Claim submitted by a Policyholder where:

(a) The Policyholder misrepresents the facts in a Claim;

(b) The Policyholder fails to pay Premiums;

(c) The Policyholder requests the Claim as a result of their involvement in criminal activity;

(d) The Policyholder attempts to submit a Claim for something that is not covered by the Insurance Policy;

Such a denial must be outlined in writing, with reference to the relevant statute.

An Insurance Business which intends to shutdown, which is not a result of financial issues, must:

(a) Notify the Commerce Office seven days before shutting down.

(b) Notify Policyholders fourteen days before shutting down.

(c) Refuse to accept new Policyholders within fourteen days of shutting down.

(d) Refuse to collect any Premiums within seven days of shutting down.

(e) Publicly publish a statement of cash flows.

(f) Publicly publish a balance sheet.

(g) Publicly publish a summary claims report.

If a business owner who no longer meets the requirements prescribed by the Commerce Office to legally own a business, is the owner of an Insurance Business, then:

(a) The ownership of the Insurance Business shall automatically be transferred to the Secretary of State.

(b) The original business owner must transfer the capital of the Insurance Business to the Secretary of State.

(i) The Department of Justice may direct law enforcement to seize assets owned by the original owner and sell them off to recuperate the capital.

(c) The Commerce Office must find a new owner for the business.

(i) The Commerce Office may sell the ownership in whole or in portions.

(d) The Commerce Office must cease the operations of the business until the new owner(s) are decided.

“Insurance Claims Misconduct” shall be defined as:

(a) Any Insurance Business that rejects a Claim by an Policyholder for a reason not outlined in Section VI, or fails to publish a summary claims report where required.

(b) Shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 30 minutes in prison, and/or face a fine of not more than $40,000 or three times the value of the Premium, whichever is greater.

“Insurance Fraud” shall be defined as:

(b) Shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 25 minutes in prison, and/or face a fine of not more than $30,000 or four times the value of the Claim, whichever is greater.

Insurance Businesses that offer Insurance Policies to more than the maximum number of Policyholders as outlined in the prospective business report shall be subject to criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 1406 “Unlawful Operation of a Business”.

Policyholders that fraudulently submits a Claim to an Insurance Business shall be subject to criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 3108 “Insurance Fraud”.

Policyholders that fail to pay a Premium as agreed by the Insurance Business and the Policyholder shall be liable to be subjected to various civil penalties as outlined by the Mayflower Tort Claims Act.

parts.heading: Subchapter I — DEFINITIONS
parts.text:
The term “Insurance Policy” shall refer to an agreement between a Policyholder and Insurance Business where the Insurance Business agrees that they will payout a Policyholder as a result of a successful Claim.

The term “Policyholder” shall refer to a person or organization which is issued an insurance policy by an Insurance Business.

The term “Insurance Business” shall refer to a licensed business which provides insurance to a Policyholder.

The term “Claim” shall refer to when a Policyholder makes a request to the Insurance Business for compensation or coverage as dictated by an insurance policy.

The term “Premium” shall refer to the charge that a Policyholder receives from the Insurance Business to be covered by insurance, typically at a recurring rate.

parts.heading: Subchapter II — INSURANCE BUSINESS REGISTRATION
parts.text:
An Insurance Business owner must satisfy the following requirments to be permitted to conduct business as an Insurance Business:

(a) Have a minimum capital of the result of the following formula:

(i) (n*C)+(C*3);

(ii) Where n is the maximum amount of persons the Insurance Business is going to insure; and

(iii) Where C is the maximum Claim amount that an Insurance Business is going to compensate for.

(b) Provide the Commerce Office a prospective business report that includes, in the order as listed:

(i) The names of all stakeholders in the business;

(ii) The names of any stakeholders in the business that have owned an Insurance Business which has been insolvent.

(iii) The maximum amount of Policyholders the Insurance Business is to insure;

(iv) The maximum Claim the Insurance Business is to insure for;

(v) The total capital the owner of the Insurance Business possesses; and

(vi) Plans on how to pay out Policyholders in case of insolvency.

(c) If an Insurance Business desires to change the maximum Claim or maximum Policyholders after registration, then the Insurance Business must submit a new prospective business report

The Commerce Office must deny any application to be a licensed Insurance Business where:

(a) The Insurance Business owner has been charged with any crime listed under Subtitle 1, Chapter IV of the Mayflower Criminal Code.

(b) The Insurance Business owner has been charged with any crime listed under Subtitle 1, Chapter VI of the Mayflower Criminal Code.

(c) The Insurance Business owner has been charged with any crime listed under Subtitle 5 of the Mayflower State Code.

(d) The Insurance Business owner has failed to properly file a prospective business report.

parts.heading: Subchapter III — INSURANCE BUSINESS REGULATIONS
Subchapter IV — INSURANCE POLICY REGULATIONS
parts.text:
An Insurance Business may only change the rules of an Insurance Policy every 30 days.

Such a change must be publicly announced seven days before the change comes into effect.

Should the premium of an Insurance Policy be changed, a Policyholder who is already covered by the Insurance Policy shall not have their premium affected for more or less until they are required to pay their Premium again.

An Insurance Policy may not include:

(a) Hidden fees;

(b) Clauses that waive the right of the Policyholder; and

(c) Clauses that unfairly benefit the Lender.

A premium may not be more than:

(a) 10% of the maximum Claim if the premium is paid at an increment of time that is monthly, or shorter; or

(b) 15% of the maximum Claim if the premium is paid at an increment of time that is longer than monthly.

A Policyholder may not fraudulently submit a Claim to an Insurance Business.

There may not be a “cooldown” period for submitting a Claim.

parts.heading: Subchapter V — INSURANCE POLICY REJECTION
Subchapter VII — METHODS OF CLOSURE
parts.text:
An Insurance Business which intends to shutdown, which is not a result of financial issues, must:

(a) Notify the Commerce Office seven days before shutting down.

(b) Notify Policyholders fourteen days before shutting down.

(c) Refuse to accept new Policyholders within fourteen days of shutting down.

(d) Refuse to collect any Premiums within seven days of shutting down.

(e) Publicly publish a statement of cash flows.

(f) Publicly publish a balance sheet.

(g) Publicly publish a summary claims report.

If a business owner who no longer meets the requirements prescribed by the Commerce Office to legally own a business, is the owner of an Insurance Business, then:

(a) The ownership of the Insurance Business shall automatically be transferred to the Secretary of State.

(b) The original business owner must transfer the capital of the Insurance Business to the Secretary of State.

(i) The Department of Justice may direct law enforcement to seize assets owned by the original owner and sell them off to recuperate the capital.

(c) The Commerce Office must find a new owner for the business.

(i) The Commerce Office may sell the ownership in whole or in portions.

(d) The Commerce Office must cease the operations of the business until the new owner(s) are decided.

sections.heading: Training and Certification
sections.text:
“Transportation Service Company” or “TSC” shall refer to any business registered with the State Department whose primary service is to offer transportation through the means of employing taxi operators or other private drivers.

“Incorporated Private Driver” or “IPD” shall refer to any individual employed by a Transportation Service Company as a taxi/transportation operator .

“Unincorporated Private Driver” or “UPD” shall refer to any individual that carries out transportation services using their own private vehicle and is not employed by or affiliated with any Transportation Service Company.

“Fare” shall refer to an amount of U.C. Dollars agreed between a private vehicle operator and customer, to be paid to the vehicle operator either before or after successful completion of the requested journey.

Transportation Service Companies shall be required to maintain a publicly accessible database of their drivers, including but not limited to the following:

(a) the driver's Roblox username;

(b) the driver's date of hire;

(c) the driver's position;

(d) the driver's registered vehicle model; and

(e) the license plate of the driver's registered vehicle model.

Transportation Service Companies shall only hire drivers that possess a Mayflower Driving License.

Transportation Service Companies shall be required to temporarily suspend the employment of drivers that have had their Mayflower Driving License revoked, until the repossession of the license by the driver.

Transportation Service Companies shall be obligated to implement policy that details potential administrative action against employees who in any instance have met all of either sections of the following criteria:

(a) the employee had a passenger in the vehicle;

(b) the employee drove recklessly and in a manner that endangered other drivers and pedestrians; or

(c) the employee was arrested for a Misdemeanour or Felony against the Mayflower Vehicle Code, whilst in the commission of his transportation service vehicle.

The liability of Transportation Service Companies over their employees shall depend on the type of business (as detailed and regulated by the Department of State) however TSCs that are not already liable for their employees shall be required to provide legal counsel and/or sufficient legal advice to drivers facing civil suits for actions committed whilst in the operation of their transportation service vehicle [provided that they are on-duty and representing the TSC employed by].

Unincorporated Private Drivers are required to possess a Mayflower Driving License whilst offering their transportation services to the public.

Unincorporated Private Drivers shall temporarily suspend their offering of transportation services to the public, should they have their Mayflower Driving License revoked, however the suspension may be self-lifted once they have repossessed their license.

Unincorporated Private Drivers shall be completely liable for their own actions.

If a UPD becomes employed by a TSC and becomes an IPD, the TSC shall not be required to provide legal counsel or advice if the driver is facing a civil suit regarding actions committed before their employment, whilst they were in a UPD capacity.

This subchapter shall apply to all private drivers offering transportation services, whether incorporated or unincorporated. This section shall not apply to private drivers with overriding contracts with individuals that detail a contractually agreed pay rate (e.g., Personal Limousine Drivers).

All drivers shall be required to charge a minimum fare of $50 (fifty dollars) per ride request.

All drivers must be informed [by the customer] of the location that the customer wishes to be driven to, before the passenger enters the transportation service vehicle.

All drivers shall be required to make the total fare of the requested journey aware to the customer, before embarking on the journey.

All drivers must detail whether the customer is to pay the fare before or after successful completion of the journey.

A driver may only embark on the requested journey once a price and timing of payment has been agreed between the driver and the customer.

sections.heading: Law Enforcement Standards
sections.text:
The term “Security” shall refer to a stock, bond, or investment contract.

The term “Stock Issuer” shall refer to any person or business that issues a security.

The term “Exchange” shall refer to any organized platform which is a place for buying or selling securities.

Any Security must be registered with the Department of State in a method deemed acceptable by the Secretary of State.

It shall be prohibited to buy or sell a security while in possession of non-public price-sensitive information about the security, or tip off another individual about the non-public price-sensitive information who then buys or sells the security.

(a) Any individual that infringes on this provision shall be liable for criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 1607 “Insider Trading.”

(b) They shall be liable for a citation for $50,000 or three times the worth of the security traded or attempted to be traded, whichever is greater.

It shall be prohibited to misrepresent or omit key facts of a business or security to investors.

(a) Any individual that infringes on this provision shall be liable for criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 1608 “Securities Fraud."

(b) They shall be liable for a citation for $80,000 or four times the worth of the security traded or attempted to be traded, whichever is greater.

It shall be prohibited to falsely portray a business to have a security which is actively being bought or sold.

(a) Any individual that infringes on this provision shall be liable for criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 1609 “Market Manipulation.”

(b) They shall be liable for a citation for $70,000 or four times the worth of the security traded or attempted to be traded, whichever is greater.

Any changes to the cost of a security must be logged in an accessible and publicly viewable manner by both the Exchange and Stock Issuer.

(a) Any individual that infringes on this provision shall be liable for criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 1608 “Securities Fraud.

(b) They shall be liable for a citation for $80,000 or four times the worth of the security traded or attempted to be traded, whichever is greater.

sections.heading: Public Safety Operations
sections.text:
It shall be unlawful for an individual without a bar certification to represent another individual in a legal proceeding unless they are supervised by a bar certified individual.

(a) Any individual who infringes on this provision shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1510 “Fraudulent Practice of Law” and liable for up to 60 minutes in prison, a citation up to $45,000, or both.

(b) Where the individual has charged a client for their service, the infringing individual shall be further liable for up to a 120 in prison, a citation up to the greater amount of either $60,000 or four times the amount charged, or both.

It shall be unlawful to advertise an individual as an attorney or as having an active bar certification where that individual does not have an active bar certification.

(a) Any individual who infringes on this provision shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1510 “Fraudulent Practice of Law” and liable for up to 60 minutes in prison, a citation up to $45,000, or both.

sections.heading: Administrative Conduct
sections.text:
All actions listed in this Chapter shall be considered an administrative action.

No action may be administered if it is in violation with the specifications of this section in each type of action.

All departments shall publish clear and unambiguous codes of conduct which explicitly prescribe the degree of punitive action for each offense.

No person shall be held to account for, or bothered with, an ambiguous offense alleged.

Chapters (I) to (V), and (VII), of this Subtitle may be cited as the “Public Servants Act” and shall be construed harmoniously as one act.

No person may be issued administrative action, as described in paragraph 1001 of this subchapter, over Discord messages.

All department employees shall enjoy the right of not being issued administrative action, as described in paragraph 1001 of this subchapter, over Discord messages.

Demotion shall be considered the involuntary reduction of rank or grade.

(a) Transferring into a different unit and taking a reduction in rank shall be considered a voluntary action if the person knew that such reduction was a prerequisite for their transfer.

It is unlawful to arbitrarily, or without due observance of law, demote someone from a non-staff position.

A voluntary general discharge may be issued upon request for resignation by an employee.

(a) For the purposes of this section, a voluntary general discharge is not an administrative action.

(b) Whether or not to give a voluntary general discharge or honorable discharge is up to the due discretion of the agency so long as they prescribe concrete rules and regulations to the degree each set of circumstances warrant.

An involuntary general discharge may be issued to a conditional employee, or to a non-conditional employee following—

(a) an internal affairs investigation, where—

(i) that investigation found wrongdoing; and

(ii) that the wrongdoing was in the form of negligence or recklessness;

(b) an employee’s failure to uphold mandated activity standards—without approved leave—defined within department policy in the form of Activity Check(s) and/or the submission of an Activity Log(s).

It is unlawful to arbitrarily, or without due observance of law, to issue an involuntary general discharge to a non-conditional employee.

Voluntary general discharges may not be reviewed by any administrative court or court of law or court of equity.

Involuntary general discharges issued to conditional employees may not be reviewed by any court.

“Activity check” shall be defined as a review used to measure employee activity where the employee is required to sign a document or form. The employee must be allotted at least 72 hours to complete this form or document.

“Activity log” shall be defined as the act of clocking in/out while performing duties related to a specific department or otherwise measuring contributions and/or completion of duties assigned to an employee

A dishonorable discharge shall serve as a bar of employment from the issuing agency for at most four (4) months after its issuance.

A dishonorable discharge may be issued only following an internal affairs investigation and–

(a) the investigation found wrongdoing; and

(b) a finding of wanton disregard for policy, statute, or regulation; or

(c) a finding of an intentional act.

It is unlawful to arbitrarily, or without due observance of law, issue a dishonorable discharge.

An administrative demerit shall be any system colloquially referred to as a “strike” or “warning.” Furthermore, such a system, upon receipt of a “strike,” demerit or “warning;” will place a disability upon its recipient or place them in jeopardy of a disability or administrative action.

An administrative demerit need not be issued by an internal investigation unit.

An administrative demerit shall not be reviewed by any administrative court or court of law unless—

(a) there is clear and present factual error in the issuance of the demerit; or

(b) the demerit was plainly and clearly arbitrary or its defined offense is ambiguous.

It is unlawful to arbitrarily, or without due observance of law, issue an administrative demerit.

A prejudicial transfer shall be a forced transfer of one person to another unit or division without their consent.

A prejudicial transfer may be issued upon any case and at any time unless—

(a) the transfer was retaliatory;

(b) the transfer was discriminatory; or

(c) the transfer was a result of a personal gripe, vendetta, or severe conflict.

A prejudicial transfer may only be reviewed by an administrative court in circumstances of 4 M.S.C. 7 §§ 1502(a)-1502(c).

(a) The complainant must prove more likely than not that the transfer violated 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1502.

Suspension shall refer to the prevention of a person from executing their duties and collecting pay for either a set period of time or indefinitely.

Administrative leave shall be the indefinite suspension pending an investigation. A person may only be put on administrative leave for allegations which, if taken as true, would warrant a general discharge or dishonorable discharge.

(a) A person may only be on administrative leave for no longer than ten (10) days; however, a person may be put on administrative leave for longer if there is a criminal investigation supplemented by order from the Department of Justice for the person to be placed on administrative leave.

(b) Administrative leave may be used in extreme cases where the probable punishment of suspension – however, the length of suspension must have the days on administrative leave subtracted from it.

(c) Administrative leave may only be used if there is a pending misconduct investigation or criminal investigation.

(d) Any administrative leave imposed as a result of a pending misconduct investigation or criminal investigation shall last up to thirty (30) days or until the conclusion of the investigation, whichever occurs first.

(i) If, upon conclusion of a misconduct or criminal investigation, probable cause of a criminal violation is found and the matter is pending review for criminal charges by the Department of Justice, the administrative leave imposed under 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(d) may be extended for a period not to exceed seven (7) additional days. Such extension shall not be subject to the thirty (30) day limit prescribed in 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(d).

(e) Any administrative leave extended pursuant to 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(d)(i) may be further extended for an indefinite period if, during the seven (7) day extension, criminal charges are formally filed. In such cases, administrative leave shall continue until the conclusion of the subsequent criminal matter.

There shall be no review by an administrative court of the placement of someone on administrative leave unless—

(a) the placement was not by an internal affairs entity, command entity;

(b) the suspension has gone on longer than allowed under 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(a); or

(c) the administrative leave extended under 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(d), 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(d)(i), or 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(e) exceeds its respective limitations without criminal filing or conclusion of the investigation.

Involuntary suspension shall refer to a suspension as specified in 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1601 for a period of time no longer than seven (7) days.

A person may be suspended for a violation of the policy, rule, or procedure notwithstanding the existence of or there the results of an internal investigation for no longer than three (3) days.

A person may only be suspended for greater than three (3) days upon recommendation and finding of fact from a bona fide misconduct investigation.

It is unlawful to arbitrarily, or without due observance of law, issue a suspension demerit.

The Attorney General shall serve as the designated enforcer of 4 M.S.C. 7 §§ 1602(d), 1602(d)(i), 1602(e), 1603(a), 1603(b), and 1603(c).

Any department, agency, or official in violation of the procedures prescribed in either 4 M.S.C. 7 §§ 1602(d), 1602(d)(i), 1602(e), 1603(a), 1603(b), or 1603(c) may be subject to administrative or civil action under 4 M.S.C. 7 § 2601 et seq.

Individuals subjected to administrative leave beyond the timelines established herein, without statutory justification or a proper extension, may file an administrative claim pursuant to 4 M.S.C. 7 § 3402.

It shall be unlawful to arbitrarily, or without due observance of law, issue a blacklist.

Arbitrary punishment is defined as:

(a) punishment that has no backing in regulation, policy, or law;

(b) punishment whose policy, law, or regulation prescribing it is ambiguous, or unclear, or a violation of a constitutional right or privilege or statutory enactment;

(c) punishment with no factual backing;

(d) punishment outside and beyond what is explicitly prescribed in policy; or

(e) punishment that takes no accounting of mitigating factors, circumstances, or liabilities.

Arbitrary punishment is prohibited.

(i) If, upon conclusion of a misconduct or criminal investigation, probable cause of a criminal violation is found and the matter is pending review for criminal charges by the Department of Justice, the administrative leave imposed under 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(d) may be extended for a period not to exceed seven (7) additional days. Such extension shall not be subject to the thirty (30) day limit prescribed in 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(d).

(e) Any administrative leave extended pursuant to 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(d)(i) may be further extended for an indefinite period if, during the seven (7) day extension, criminal charges are formally filed. In such cases, administrative leave shall continue until the conclusion of the subsequent criminal matter.

There shall be no review by an administrative court of the placement of someone on administrative leave unless—

(a) the placement was not by an internal affairs entity, command entity;

(b) the suspension has gone on longer than allowed under 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(a); or

(c) the administrative leave extended under 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(d), 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(d)(i), or 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(e) exceeds its respective limitations without criminal filing or conclusion of the investigation.

Involuntary suspension shall refer to a suspension as specified in 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1601 for a period of time no longer than seven (7) days.

A person may be suspended for a violation of the policy, rule, or procedure notwithstanding the existence of or there the results of an internal investigation for no longer than three (3) days.

A person may only be suspended for greater than three (3) days upon recommendation and finding of fact from a bona fide misconduct investigation.

It is unlawful to arbitrarily, or without due observance of law, issue a suspension demerit.

The Attorney General shall serve as the designated enforcer of 4 M.S.C. 7 §§ 1602(d), 1602(d)(i), 1602(e), 1603(a), 1603(b), and 1603(c).

Any department, agency, or official in violation of the procedures prescribed in either 4 M.S.C. 7 §§ 1602(d), 1602(d)(i), 1602(e), 1603(a), 1603(b), or 1603(c) may be subject to administrative or civil action under 4 M.S.C. 7 § 2601 et seq.

Individuals subjected to administrative leave beyond the timelines established herein, without statutory justification or a proper extension, may file an administrative claim pursuant to 4 M.S.C. 7 § 3402.

sections.heading: State Agency Administration
sections.text:
A primary agency shall be any as so defined:

(a) The Mayflower State Police.

(b) Any county law enforcement agency.

(c) Any municipal law enforcement agency.

The rank at which a staff position begins shall be clearly defined by a department through their policy.

If a department does not specify a staff position then it shall be considered that they have no staff positions for the purposes of this Subchapter and Chapter.

A command position is a position or rank within a department’s leadership such as:

(a) the department head, or director, or superintendent of the department;

(b) the designated successor, by policy or statutorily, to the department head, director, or superintendent of the department; or

(c) a staff assistant, vice, or deputy to either the successor thereto or the department head, director, or superintendent of the department.

No person shall be in more than one primary department.

No person shall be in more than two secondary departments unless they are not employed in a primary department, in which case they may be in one additional secondary department.

A person may be employed in both a secondary and primary department so long as they never exceed the defined limits.

A person may be in as many civil service positions as they so choose, and as long as they can affirmatively meet the standards and activity requirements of such civil service positions.

Agencies and departments may promulgate additional rules, policies, or procedures which would otherwise extend these provisions to disallow employment in either a primary or secondary.

No person shall hold more than two staff positions in both a primary or secondary agency at one time.

No person who holds a command position in a primary or secondary agency may hold a staff position in any primary or secondary agency.

The courts shall have no jurisdiction to hear a civil action based on a violation of this Chapter, and the enforcement of this Chapter shall be left solely up to the designated enforcer.

This subchapter does not apply to individuals who would otherwise be in violation of its provisions, provided they were employed before the enactment of this act and have not experienced any change in their public employment status, including leaving or joining any department, whether voluntarily or through lawful termination or reassignment. If any such change in public employment occurs, the individual will no longer qualify for this exemption and must fully comply with the provisions of this Subchapter. The exempted individual must also provide valid documentation of their original public employment to the Attorney General or his designee upon request.

For the purposes of this Subchapter, the Attorney General shall be construed as the "designated enforcer," under the direction of the Governor.

When made aware of a violation of this Subchapter, the Attorney General or his designee may issue an order:

(a) Suspending the employment of a violator until they are in compliance with this Subchapter, or;

(b) Terminating the employment of a violator for egregious violations of this Subchapter done knowingly.

The principles of the merit system shall be as follows:

(a) Recruitment should be from qualified individuals from appropriate sources in an endeavor to achieve a work force from all segments of society, and selection and advancement should be determined solely on the basis of relative ability, knowledge and skills, after fair and open competition which assures that all receive equal opportunity.

(b) All employees and applicants for employment should receive fair and equitable treatment in all aspects of personnel management without regard to political affiliation, race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, or handicapping condition, and with proper regard for their privacy and constitutional rights.

(c) All employees should maintain high standards of integrity, conduct, and concern for the public interest.

(d) The State workforce should be used efficiently and effectively.

(e) Employees should be retained on the basis of adequacy of their performance, inadequate performance should be corrected, and employees should be separated who cannot or will not improve their performance to meet required standards.

(f) Employees should be provided effective education and training in cases in which such education and training would result in better organizational and individual performance.

(g) Employees should be—

(i) protected against arbitrary action, personal favoritism, or coercion for political purposes; and

(ii) prohibited from using their official authority or influence for the purpose of interfering with or affecting the result of an election or a nomination for election.

Employees should be protected against reprisal for the lawful disclosure of information which the employees reasonably believe evidences-- a violation of any law, rule, or regulation, or mismanagement, a gross waste of resources, an abuse of authority, or a substantial and specific danger to public safety.

The attributes of the merit system shall be as follows:

(a) When making decisions of employment or promotion, officials shall review the following attributes of merit:

(i) logged patrol/work hours for the current cycle;

(ii) past performance in other departments;

(iii) abilities to work as a team and play well with others, which is affirmed by testimony of another leader or employee;

(iv) demonstration of sound judgment, which is affirmed by testimony of another leader;

(v) demonstration of leadership qualities while holding a position in the State of Mayflower, which is affirmed by testimony of another leader or employee;

(vi) effort in the completion of an application, cover letter, or letter of interest;

(vii) scores on an accredited exam, if applicable;

(viii) commendations or written letters of recommendation; and

(ix) holding a valid accreditation, which may be required for the position.

(x) Completion of formal state training or continued education relevant to the position.

Performance in another community or group shall not be used as a means to demonstrate the merit of an individual.

When making a hiring decision officials can use the following attributes to discredit and demerit a hire:

(a) bad performance in another department or agency;

(b) poor completion of an application, cover letter, or letter of interest;

(c) poor accredited exam scores;

(d) past disciplinary actions;

(e) character defects which would bring harm to the health of the department or community;

(f) failure to use discretion;

(g) inability to gain a security clearance, other than not requiring it in the first place;

(h) refusal to comply with regulations or lawful orders;

(i) terrible activity in a previous department or agency; or

(j) no, or little experience within the State of Mayflower.

During the hiring process, an agency shall indicate all attributes of merit and demerit and subjectively, according to their own principles, weigh each application.

A competitive hiring round shall be any hiring period where the number of spots to be taken in is clearly defined, publicly posted, and limited.

(a) A department may not intake more than the number of applicants they have posted in a competitive hiring round.

A non-competitive hiring round shall be any hiring round where the number of spots is not clearly defined, publicly posted, and not limited.

(a) If a person passes all preceding stages in a non-competitive hiring round, then they must be accepted as their outcome so long as this would not cause the department to exceed their allocated budget.

An application / character screening may only be denied for an attribute of demerit, and accepted for an attribute of merit. If they have neither then they shall be denied.

No individual may skip more than three (3) consecutive ranks from their current rank.

(a) If any Department is found promoting someone over three (3) ranks, the Department of Justice shall investigate such Department for any findings of Nepotism and any level of Misconduct.

(b) The Mayflower National Guard shall be exempt from paragraph 2510 of this subchapter.

Complaints about a department violating the principles of the merit system shall be directed to the Governor, who shall in all cases, investigate and adjudicate violations of these claims. The Governor may delegate this responsibility to any persons employed by the Office of the Governor or the Department of Justice as he sees fit.

(a) The Governor may seek a written legal opinion from the Attorney General as to the legality of the violations.

The Governor, under a finding of intentional deprivation of an employment right, or failure to follow a merits-system practice, may request the Attorney General to begin legal proceedings.

The Attorney General may also, on his own accord, begin legal proceedings on any reasonable suspicion of violation.

(a) Such legal proceeding will take form in a civil action in the name of the State against the Department and any individuals within said Department violating the principles of the merit system.

If a complaint is substantiated and found to be more-likely than not in proving the existence of a violation, then the Governor shall remedy the complainant appropriately with respect to the offending agency.

Background checks shall be over an objective criteria that shall remain static and non-subjective.

Activity in other communities, games, or organizations shall not be evaluated in a background check unless:

(a) the activity was unlawful [in real life];

(b) the activity was extremely toxic; or

(c) the activity constitutes harassment or unlawful badgering.

Departments shall background check applicants and new-hires on the following criteria:

(a) Likelihood that the individual is an alternate account; which shall be evaluated under reasonableness.

(b) Whether the individual has their inventory open.

(c) Whether the individual is involved with a criminal or terrorist organization which has been declared by the Attorney General.

(d) Whether the individual has a certain amount of records that exceed a threshold.

(e) Whether the individual has a criminal conviction.

(f) A dishonorable discharge from the department, or other departments.

(g) Severe Moderation action against them with the exception of appealed Moderation action.

(h) Extremely toxic behavior, unlawful activities [in real life] or harassment in other communities, games, or organizations.

(i) Whether the individual is not a resident within the state.

(j) Whether the individual defects would bring harm to the health of the department.

(k) Whether the individual has past disciplinary actions taken against them within the last two (2) months in a department in which they are currently or were previously employed in.

If a department denies an individual due to them having their inventory hidden then they shall specify such on their results tracker.

(a) If a department denies an individual due to them failing their background check then they shall specify the reason on their results tracker.

Civil service agencies, the Mayflower Transportation Authority, or any fire department may enlist the services of any county law enforcement agency or the Mayflower State Police to perform background checks on their current or potential staff and personnel.

(a) The State Legislature may request that the Mayflower State Police conduct a background check on any nominee brought before them and be provided an unabridged report in which the Mayflower State Police shall conduct.

A prejudicial or unfair hiring practice is a hiring practice that does not conform to what has been established by law.

It is a violation of law to engage in prejudicial or unfair hiring practices.

A person can petition the administrative courts for review of a prejudicial hiring practice.

(a) A court may remedy this by issuing an order to conform to legislation pertaining to hiring practices and administrative law.

(b) A court may not remedy by ordering the installment, or removal, or dismissal, of a person, or order an application be accepted.

(c) The cause of action is limited to systematic violations of statutory procedure for hiring practices. Specific situations regarding an individual shall be handled through Subchapter (VI) of this Chapter.

A “command position” for the purposes of this subchapter shall hold the same definition encoded within 4 M.S.C. 7 § 2403.

No person shall hold a command position within a department and serve as an elected official within the State at the same time, except for a County Sheriff. However, this shall not prevent any individual holding a command position from running for office.

For the purposes of this Subchapter, the Attorney General shall be construed as the “designated enforcer,” under the direction of the Governor.

When made aware of a violation of this Subchapter, the Attorney General or his designee shall issue an order:

(a) Suspending the employment of a violator until they are in compliance with this Subchapter; or

(b) Terminating the employment of a violator for egregious violations of this Subchapter done knowingly.
