(b) Any individual who is a public servant and commits the aforementioned shall be liable for compensatory damages; injunctive reliefs restraining the individual from performing a certain action, or orders instructing the individual to perform a certain action; and punitive damages up to $75,000

(c) Such suits shall proceed in a form of quasi-official capacity, such that the defendants shall be named as parties in official capacity; however if the courts or an arbitrator wish to provide monetary damages to the plaintiff, then it shall be the duty of the defendant’s individual capacity to pay such damages as ordered.

Any individual who willfully, maliciously, and repeatedly follows, harasses, or engages in a pattern of conduct directed at another individual that would cause a reasonable person to feel fear for their own safety shall be liable for the tort of stalking and may be subject to punitive damages up to two hundred and fifty thousand (250,000) dollars.

(a) The individual aggrieved by such conduct may seek relief in the form of an injunction or declaratory judgment.

(b) Upon a verified petition and showing of conduct that would support a claim under 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3104.7, a court may issue a temporary injunction for protection against stalking, effective for no more than fourteen (14) days provided the petition establishes that the respondent’s conduct would cause a reasonable person to fear for their safety; such an order may be granted without notice to the other party. An injunction may be extended until final judgment only upon a showing of irreparable harm, or a substantial threat thereof, to the petitioner; such an order may only be granted with notice to the other party. A party must first initiate a claim under 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3104.7 to petition for an injunction under this subsection.

Any individual who publicly discloses information about another that places the individual in a false light, and where the false light would be highly offensive to a reasonable person and was made with knowledge of or reckless disregard for its falsity, shall be liable for false light invasion of privacy and punitive damages up to fifty thousand (50,000) dollars.

parts.heading: Subchapter I — INDIVIDUAL CLAIMS / Part V — ECONOMIC TORTS
parts.text:
Any individual who knowingly makes a false representation with the intent to deceive another, and where such representation is reasonably relied upon and causes actual harm, shall be liable for fraud. The injured party may recover compensatory damages and, where appropriate, punitive damages up to seven hundred fifty thousand dollars (750,000).

Any individual who intentionally interferes with a contractual or business relationship between other parties, causing harm to one of the parties, shall be liable for tortious interference and shall be liable for punitive damages up to one hundred seventy five (175,000) dollars.

Any individual who enters into an agreement with two or more parties to deprive a third party of legal rights or to deceive a third party in order to achieve an illegal objective, resulting in harm to the third party, shall be liable for civil conspiracy and shall be liable for punitive damages up to three hundred thousand (300,000) dollars.

Any individual who knowingly discloses or misappropriates confidential business information or trade secrets without authorization and with the intent to gain an unfair competitive advantage shall be liable for misappropriation of trade secrets and shall be liable for punitive damages up to two hundred fifty thousand (250,000) dollars.

Any individual who, with intent to obtain money, property, services, or other benefit, knowingly threatens to expose, accuse, disgrace, or otherwise harm another unless such benefit is provided, and whose threat causes harm or coerced compliance, shall be liable for civil extortion and punitive damages up to three hundred seventy fifty thousand (375,000) dollars.

Any individual who, in breach of a fiduciary duty, acts contrary to the interests of the beneficiary by engaging in self-dealing, nondisclosure, or other disloyal conduct resulting in harm, shall be liable for breach of fiduciary duty and subject to compensatory and punitive damages up to five hundred thousand dollars (500,000).

parts.heading: Subchapter I — INDIVIDUAL CLAIMS / Part VI — REMEDIES BABY DOLPHIN PRICE
parts.text:
In all cases of tortious conduct, the aggrieved party shall be entitled to seek remedies that include but are not limited to, compensatory damages, punitive damages, injunctive relief, and any other relief deemed appropriate by the court. The availability of remedies for each tort is not exclusive or limiting, and the non-exclusion of any particular remedy does not preclude its application or availability in any specific case.

(a) Where the court finds that the tortious conduct was willful, malicious, reckless, or part of a pattern of repeated misconduct, it may, in the interest of justice, award punitive damages in excess of any statutory cap otherwise imposed by this title.

parts.heading: Subchapter II — CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE / Part I — DEFINITIONS
parts.text:
As used in this act, the term “state agency” includes the executive departments, the judicial and legislative branches, the military departments, independent establishments of the State of Mayflower, and corporations primarily acting as instrumentalities or agencies of the State of Mayflower, but does not include any contractor with the State of Mayflower.

“Employee of the government” includes (1) officers or employees of any state agency, members of the National Guard while engaged in training or duty, and persons acting on behalf of a state agency in an official capacity, temporarily or permanently in the service of the state, whether with or without compensation, and (2) any officer or employee of a state public defender organization, except when such officer or employee performs professional services in the course of providing representation.

“Acting within the scope of his office or employment,” in the case of a member of the National Guard means acting in line of duty.

parts.heading: Subchapter II — CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE / Part II — GOVERNMENT IMMUNITY AND SOLICITOR GENERAL OVERSIGHT
parts.text:
The government shall be immune from all claims except those in this subchapter, and later laws in which liability is explicitly created against the government.

No monetary damage shall be awarded in a case against the government, cases where the government is a party, or cases where the government has intervened, unless the government has consented to it through a statutory waiver.

The Solicitor General may accept settlements on behalf of the government and issue orders or decrees in line with those settlements such that they are within the bounds of the law, charter, and constitution.

The Solicitor General may intervene with the government as a defendant in cases against one’s individual capacity if they were in fact serving in an official capacity - or the government has a substantial interest in the outcome of the suit.

The Solicitor General may refuse to defend an agent of the government if they were clearly acting in an individual capacity, or in a capacity that is not in line with the laws, directives, orders, policies, or standard operating procedures of the government and its agencies.

Qualified immunity shall not be a valid affirmative defense if the Solicitor General refuses to defend an agent of the government.

If the Solicitor General refuses to defend an agent of the government, and the torts are alleged under this section, then the Solicitor General shall provide the relief as requested within the bounds of the law, charter, and constitution.

The courts shall dismiss with prejudice all claims in which the Solicitor General refuses to defend an agent, and that the Solicitor General provides relief as requested within the law, charter, and constitution.

If the Solicitor General refuses to defend an agent of the government, then that agent shall be liable for the equitable offenses in his individual capacity, and the government shall cease to be a party and have interest in the case.

parts.heading: Subchapter II — CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE / Part III — TORT CLAIMS PROCEDURE
parts.text:
Any individual seeking compensation for damages or other forms of relief, declaratory, injunctive, or otherwise, arising from tortious acts authorized by this section against the state, county, or municipal agencies and employees of the State and any political or administrative subdivision thereof must submit their claim to the Department of Justice. The claim should include detailed information about the nature of the tort, the alleged wrongful conduct, and the damages sought. The Attorney General shall prescribe regulations that detail additional elements that must be included in a claim.

Upon receipt of the claim, the Department of Justice shall have a set period of seven (7) days to:

(a) accept the claim and propose a settlement;

(b) deny the claim;

(c) request for more information; or

(d) open mediation between both parties to negotiate a resolution.

If the Department of Justice chooses to deny the claim, then it shall be construed as a final denial for the purposes of this act.

If the Department of Justice chooses to request for more information, the claimant must respond within seven (7) days. If the claimant does so within this window, then the Department of Justice shall receive five (5) more days to process the claim. If the Department of Justice does not enter any action on the claim within this window, then it shall be construed as a final denial for the purposes of this act, similar to 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3203.2(b). If the claimant does not provide the Department of Justice with the requested information within this window, then the Department of Justice shall not be required to review the claim any further and it shall be construed as if the claim was never sent to the Department of Justice.

If the Department of Justice chooses to open arbitration, it must end within ten days of its initiation. In the event that it does not end within ten days, it shall be construed as a final denial for the purposes of this act, similar to 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3203.2(b).

An individual must file a claim within three months from the date the claim accrued. Failure to file the claim within this specified period will result in the claim being barred and therefore not actionable in a State court.

parts.heading: Subchapter II — CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE / Part IV — DISPOSITION BY THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE AS A PREREQUISITE; EVIDENCE
parts.text:
An action shall not be instituted upon a claim against the State of Mayflower, or any political or administrative subdivision thereof for relief for injury or loss of property or personal injury or death caused by the negligent or wrongful act or omission of any employee of the Government while acting within the scope of his office or employment, unless the claimant shall have first presented the claim to the Department of Justice and his claim shall have been finally denied by the agency in writing. The failure of the Department of Justice to make final disposition of a claim within one (1) month after it is filed shall, at the option of the claimant at any time thereafter, be deemed a final denial of the claim for purposes of this section.

Action under this section shall not be instituted for any sum in excess of the amount of the claim presented to the Department of Justice, except where the increased amount is based upon newly discovered evidence not reasonably discoverable at the time of presenting the claim to the Department of Justice, or upon allegation and proof of intervening facts, relating to the amount of the claim.

Disposition of any claim by the Attorney General or his designee shall not be competent evidence of liability or amount of damages.

parts.heading: Subchapter II — CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE / Part V — ADMINISTRATIVE ADJUSTMENT OF CLAIMS
parts.text:
The Attorney General or his designee, may consider, ascertain, adjust, determine, compromise, and settle any claim for money damages against the State of Mayflower for injury or loss of property or personal injury or death caused by the negligent or wrongful act or omission of any employee of the agency while acting within the scope of his office or employment, under circumstances where the State of Mayflower, if a private person, would be liable to the claimant in accordance with the law of the place where the act or omission occurred.

Subject to the provisions of this title relating to civil actions on tort claims against the State of Mayflower, any such award, compromise, settlement, or determination shall be final and conclusive on all officers of the Government, except when procured by means of fraud.

The acceptance by the claimant of any such award, compromise, or settlement shall be final and conclusive on the claimant, and shall constitute a complete release of any claim against the State of Mayflower and against the employee of the government whose act or omission gave rise to the claim, by reason of the same subject matter.

parts.heading: Subchapter II — CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE / Part VI — REPORTS TO LEGISLATURE
parts.text: The Attorney General or his designee, shall report semiannually to the Legislature all claims paid by it under 5 M.S.C. 1 §§ 3204.1-3204.3, stating the name of each claimant, the amount claimed, the amount awarded, and a brief description of the claim.

parts.heading: Subchapter II — CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE / Part VII — LIABILITY OF THE STATE OF MAYFLOWER
parts.text:
The State of Mayflower shall be liable, respecting the provisions of this title relating to tort claims, in the same manner and to the same extent as a private individual under like circumstances, but shall not be liable for interest prior to judgment or for punitive damages.

If, however, in any case wherein death was caused, the State of Mayflower shall be liable for actual or compensatory damages, measured by the pecuniary injuries resulting from such death to the persons respectively.

With respect to any claim under this chapter, the State of Mayflower shall be entitled to assert any defense based upon judicial or legislative immunity which otherwise would have been available to the employee of the State of Mayflower whose act or omission gave rise to the claim, as well as any other defenses to which the State of Mayflower is entitled.

parts.heading: Subchapter II — CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE / Part VIII — COMPROMISE
parts.text: The Attorney General or his designee may arbitrate, compromise, or settle any claim initiated, after the commencement of an action thereon.

parts.heading: Subchapter II — CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE / Part IX — EXCLUSIVENESS OF REMEDY
parts.text:
The remedy against the State of Mayflower provided by this act for injury or loss of property, or personal injury or death arising or resulting from the negligent or wrongful act or omission of any employee of the Government while acting within the scope of his office or employment is exclusive of any other civil action or proceeding for money damages by reason of the same subject matter against the employee whose act or omission gave rise to the claim. Any other civil action or proceeding for money damages arising out of or relating to the same subject matter against the employee is precluded without regard to when the act or omission occurred.

The previous paragraph does not extend or apply to a civil action against an employee of the Government—

(a) which is brought for a violation of the Constitution of the State of Mayflower, or

(b) which is brought for a violation of a statute of the State of Mayflower under which such action against an individual is otherwise authorized.

The Solicitor General shall defend any civil action or proceeding brought in any court against any employee of the Government for any such damage or injury.

The Solicitor General shall certify whether the defendant employee was acting within the scope of his office or employment at the time of the incident out of which the claim arose.

Upon certification by the Solicitor General that the defendant employee was acting within the scope of his office or employment at the time of the incident out of which the claim arose, any civil action or proceeding commenced upon such claim in a Mayflower district court shall be deemed an action against the State of Mayflower under the provisions of this title and all references thereto, and the State of Mayflower shall be substituted as the party defendant.

In the event that the Solicitor General has refused to certify scope of office or employment under this section, the employee may at any time before trial petition the court to find and certify that the employee was acting within the scope of his office or employment. Upon such certification by the court, such action or proceeding shall be deemed to be an action or proceeding brought against the State of Mayflower under the provisions of this title and all references thereto, and the State of Mayflower shall be substituted as the party defendant.

Whenever an action or proceeding in which the State of Mayflower is substituted as the party defendant under this subsection is dismissed for failure first to present a claim pursuant to 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3204.1, such a claim shall be deemed to be timely presented under 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3209.2 if—

(a) the claim would have been timely had it been filed on the date the underlying civil action was commenced, and

(b) the claim is presented to the Department of Justice within fifteen days after dismissal of the civil action.

parts.heading: Subchapter II — CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE / Part X — TIME FOR COMMENCING ACTION AGAINST THE STATE OF MAYFLOWER
parts.text:
Every civil action commenced against the State of Mayflower shall be barred unless the complaint is filed within three months after the right of action first accrues.

A tort claim against the State of Mayflower shall be forever barred unless it is presented in writing to the Department of Justice within three months after such claim accrues.

parts.heading: Subchapter II — CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE / Part XI — EXCEPTIONS
parts.text:
The provisions of this act shall not apply to:

(a) Any claim based upon an act or omission of an employee of the Government, exercising due care, in the execution of a statute or regulation, whether or not such statute or regulation be valid, or based upon the exercise or performance or the failure to exercise or perform a discretionary function or duty on the part of a state agency or an employee of the Government, whether or not the discretion involved be abused.

(b) Any claim arising out of the combatant activities of the national guard, during time of war.

(c) Any claim arising in a foreign country.

(d) Any claim arising from the assessment or collection of any customs duty, or the detention of any goods, merchandise, or other property by any port authority officer or other law enforcement officer, applies to claims based on injury or loss of goods, merchandise, or other property while in the possession of these officers if—

(i) the property was seized for the purpose of forfeiture under any provision of state law providing for the forfeiture of property other than as a sentence imposed upon conviction of a criminal offense;

(ii) the interest of the claimant was not forfeited;

(iii) the interest of the claimant was not remitted or mitigated (if the property was subject to forfeiture); and

(iv) the claimant was not convicted of a crime for which the interest of the claimant in the property was subject to forfeiture under a state criminal forfeiture law.

parts.heading: Subchapter II — CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE / Part XII — CLAIMS TO BE MADE
parts.text:
Any law, policy, order, procedure, action, or directive that impedes on an individuals rights, immunities, or privileges secured by law, charter, or the constitution shall be subject to the injunctive relief of a permanent restraining order against the government prohibiting them from enacting this policy, order, procedure, action, or directive; and injunctive relief reversing any harm done.

(a) Plaintiffs must demonstrate that they received, or are at an imminent threat of receiving, concrete, non-hypothetical harm from the law, policy, order, procedure, action or directive.

(b) The courts may subpoena any sensitive policy, procedure, order, or directive that relates to the issue.

Public officials sued in their individual capacity for conduct engaged in the course of their duties shall be immune from claims at law unless—

(a) Their course of conduct transgresses a legal right; and

(b) The offending official knew or should have known about that legal right; or

(c) The legal right would not have otherwise been transgressed if the officer were acting in accordance with their training, policy, directives, or the law.

Any public official who refrains from performing a duty lawfully imposed on their office or clearly inherent to it, or who engages in a course of conduct relating to their office but constituting an unauthorized exercise of their official functions, is liable to the party injured.

(a) Suits under this provision shall proceed against a Defendant’s quasi-official capacity such that the official office shall be liable for the equitable remedy and the individual capacity of the Defendant shall be liable for the monetary damages.

(b) The party injured may obtain relief in the form of compensatory damages, punitive damages, and injunctive relief ordering a certain action to be taken or restraining a certain action from being taken.

(c) The Solicitor General shall represent Defendants sued in accordance with this provision.

(i) The Solicitor General, at their discretion, and upon careful consideration of the State’s sovereign interests, may refuse to represent an individual sued in accordance with this provision.

Any person subject to the directive authority of the Attorney General in accordance with Article VI, section 3 of the Mayflower Constitution who violates a lawful order or directive issued by the Attorney General may be subject to suit at the discretion of the Attorney General on behalf of the State who shall have a cause of action for injunctive relief and punitive damages not exceeding two hundred thousand (200,000) dollars against the offending individual.

(a) The State of Mayflower may sue parens patriae and may sue in its sovereign capacity for injury to its own interests.

parts.heading: Subchapter III — RETROACTIVITY; SHORT TITLE; INCLUSIVE PRONOUN USAGE / Part I — RETROACTIVITY
parts.text:
All sections of this act shall apply retroactively to all claims arising from tortious acts that occurred prior to the enactment of this act, including the time that has elapsed between the date of release, the twenty-fourth of August, 2001, to the date of this act’s completion, provided that the claim has not been previously settled or adjudicated.

This chapter may be cited as the "Mayflower Tort Claims Act."

In this Subtitle, any reference to a pronoun shall be interpreted to include all respective pronouns, regardless of gender. Terms such as 'he,' 'him,' or 'his' shall be deemed to include 'she,' 'her,' 'hers,' 'they,' 'them,' 'theirs,' or any other pronoun as applicable. This inclusive interpretation applies to all provisions, ensuring gender neutrality and inclusivity throughout this Subtitle.

sections.heading: Capital Punishment
sections.text:
The term “physician” shall refer to:

(a) Any member employed or appointed to the State Medical Examiner’s Office as a medical doctor.

(b) Any employee of a fire department, selected by their department head, with the necessary qualifications prescribed in standards written by the respective fire department.

(c) Any otherwise qualified individual to deliver medical advice and opinions pursuant to the judgment of the County Fire Chief.

This chapter may be cited as the "Capital Punishment Act."

“Capital punishment” or “death penalty” shall be defined as the judgment of death upon an individual convicted of a crime described in this act as a “capital felony”.

A “capital felony” shall refer to any of the following crimes listed in this subsection that shall be punishable by death upon the court deeming such sentence appropriate, unless otherwise provided further by law:

(a) 1 M.S.C. § 1105 "Treason."

(b) 1 M.S.C. § 1104 "Criminal Anarchy."

(c) 1 M.S.C. § 1102 "Espionage."

(d) 1 M.S.C. § 2101 "First-degree murder."

A “death warrant” shall refer to the issuance of a warrant by the court upon a judgment of death ordering for the search and seizure of all property, seizure of all properties leased, burning of any vehicles, aircrafts or boats owned, seizure of all money, and revocation of all certifications held from the individual imposed, as well as capital punishment to be executed at a specific date prescribed by the court.

A person, upon whom has been imposed the judgment of death, shall be transferred to the custody and care of the Attorney General through the Mayflower State Police.

A death warrant shall be signed by the Court upon a judgment of death.

(a) A death warrant shall allow the search and seizure of all property stored within vehicles or residences unless otherwise prescribed.

A death warrant shall allow the search and seizure of all property stored within vehicles or residences, the seizure of all properties leased, burning of all vehicles, aircrafts, or boats owned, seizure of all money, and revocation of all certifications held from the individual imposed.

Upon the completion of the death warrant seizure and the issuance of a warrant receipt to the court. The court shall issue the maximum sentence time allowed by law within the in-game interface.

(a) If there is no maximum sentence limit, then the court shall issue a jail sentence of no more than 3 days, and no less than 1 day.

The judgment of death shall be executed either at the Mayflower State Detention Complex, or at any Mayflower National Guard base confined within a military exclusion zone.

(a) The Mayflower National Guard may not inhibit the movement or access of civilian law enforcement, prescribed witnesses, or attorneys present for the purposes of the execution.

The punishment of death shall be carried out by firing squad.

(a) Four (4) Troopers from the Mayflower State Police shall be appointed to serve as members of the firing squad, with one (1) Trooper at the rank of Sergeant or above serving as leader of the firing squad.

(b) If selected officers from either the Mayflower State Police are unavailable, The Department of Justice may request the use of other law enforcement officials from municipal or county political subdivision(s) to meet the requirement listed in 5 M.S.C. 1 § 4306(a).

The Department of Justice shall develop rules and standards for the method and process of execution that do not violate the person’s constitutional rights.

A physician may attend an execution for the purpose of pronouncing death and may provide advice to officials for the purpose of developing an execution protocol to minimize the risk of pain to the inmate.

(a) The presence of a physician is not required unless prescribed by standards written by the Department of Justice or by mandate of the court.

(b) The physician, upon completion of the execution will prescribe and record the time of death of the inmate to be presented in the death warrant and returned to the court.

(c) If there is no physician present, the ranking official of the Justice Department present during the execution will record the time of death.

The Department of Justice may allow witnesses to be present during the execution;

(a) No more than ten (10) members may be present, not including officials carrying out the punishment.

(b) No person shall be a witness to an execution unless they are a resident of the State of Mayflower.

(c) At the request of the inmate, spiritual members or ministers of the gospel shall be permitted to be present at the execution not exceeding more than one person.

Upon the completion of the execution, a death certificate shall be issued by the State Medical Examiners’ Office with the time of recorded death, cause of death, and other necessary information prescribed in developed policy.

(a) The cause of death shall be listed as "lead poisoning," unless the execution is carried out by alternative means.

(b) The certificate shall be issued to the recipient and the Department of Justice in a timely manner.

The death certificate issued shall be enforceable upon signature by the Chief Medical Examiner, and cannot be challenged by the recipient alone without a legal petition to the Mayflower Supreme Court.

A person imposed with a judgment of death by a court of law may petition an appeal of their sentence to the Mayflower Supreme Court for a stay of execution.

(a) They shall be remanded in the custody of the Mayflower State Police until their hearing.

Any sentence of death upon acceptance of a Writ of Certiorari shall be stayed and paused until a decision by the Supreme Court is made in favor or against an appeal.

The Governor may grant a Stay of Execution to anyone whom is scheduled to be executed, indefinitely postponing their execution unless said stay is vacated by the Governor.

sections.heading: Defenses and Justification
sections.text:
“Justified homicide” shall refer to the provisions as defined in 5 M.S.C. 1 § 7101.

“Trespassing” shall refer to the provisions as defined in 1 M.S.C § 3205.

“Attempting to trespass” shall refer to the attempt to commit a violation of 1 M.S.C § 3205.

“Trespassers” shall be defined as anyone actively trespassing or attempting to trespass.

“Unauthorized third party” shall refer to any person who is occupying or attempting to occupy private property without authorization.

“Innocent third party” shall refer to any person who is not in the commission of a crime.

“Identifiable public servant” shall refer to any person employed within the Mayflower National Guard, any Union of Columbia Law Enforcement Agency, Lee County Transportation Authority, or Lee County Regional Hospital who is acting in their official capacity, and is easily marked by a department or company uniform. Law enforcement officers who are in an unmarked capacity as defined by specific department policy shall be considered easily identifiable if they are wearing a badge of their respective agency on their person.

This chapter may be cited as "The Castle Doctrine Act."

A person is justified in and cannot face prosecution nor arrest for using lethal, or any degree of force less-than-lethal, given it is a Justified Homicide.

A person is justified in and cannot face prosecution nor arrest and is immune from civil claims for using less-than-lethal force if an unauthorized third party is actively trespassing or attempting to trespass and has been given ample warning(s) to leave and reasonable time to do so.

A person is justified in and cannot face prosecution nor arrest and is immune from civil claims for using lethal or less-than-lethal force if an unauthorized third party is—

(a) has committed 1 M.S.C. § 3201 (Breaking and entering) and is actively trespassing on private property; or

(b) is actively attempting to commit breaking and entering.

A person is justified justified in, and cannot face prosecution nor arrest, and is immune from civil claims for using lethal force in defense of an innocent third party given:

(a) The innocent third party is actively being assaulted to a degree that would cause serious bodily injury or death.

(b) The innocent third party is actively being kidnapped.

(c) The innocent third party is actively a victim of armed robbery as defined in 1 M.S.C § 3101.

A person is justified in, and cannot face prosecution nor arrest, and is immune from civil claims for using less-than-lethal force in defense of an innocent third party given:

(a) The innocent third party is actively being assaulted to a degree that would not cause serious bodily injury or death.

(b) The innocent third party is actively being robbed as defined in 1 M.S.C § 3102.

“Attempting to trespass” shall refer to the attempt to commit a violation of 1 M.S.C § 3205.

“Trespassers” shall be defined as anyone actively trespassing or attempting to trespass.

“Unauthorized third party” shall refer to any person who is occupying or attempting to occupy private property without authorization.

“Innocent third party” shall refer to any person who is not in the commission of a crime.

“Identifiable public servant” shall refer to any person employed within the Mayflower National Guard, any Union of Columbia Law Enforcement Agency, Lee County Transportation Authority, or Lee County Regional Hospital who is acting in their official capacity, and is easily marked by a department or company uniform. Law enforcement officers who are in an unmarked capacity as defined by specific department policy shall be considered easily identifiable if they are wearing a badge of their respective agency on their person.

sections.heading: Limitations on Proceedings
sections.text:
Except as otherwise expressly provided, a prosecution may only be commenced for a felony offense—

(a) where punishable by death or pursuant to title 1, subtitle 1, chapter 1, Mayflower State Code, anytime after the commission of the offense;

(b) where involving the use, attempted use, or threatened use of physical force against another person or property of another, or any conspiracy to that effect, within fifty (50) days;

(c) where involving the intentional falsification or concealment of any material fact or the making of any materially false, fictitious, or fraudulent statement or representation to any employee of the government, within fifty (50) days;

(d) where involving misconduct on the part of any employee of the government—

(i) and posing a great risk of death or grievous bodily harm, within sixty (60) days;

(ii) in any such other case, within sixty (60) days;

(e) where involving the unauthorized distribution, possession, or sale of a firearm, within sixty (60) days; and

(f) in any such other case, within forty five (45) days.

Except as otherwise expressly provided, a prosecution may only be commenced for a misdemeanor offense—

(a) where involving the unauthorized distribution, possession, or sale of police-grade or non-civilian equipment, or misconduct on the part of any employee of the government, within forty (40) days;

(b) where involving the use, attempted use, or threatened use of physical force against another person or property of another, or any conspiracy to that effect, within forty-five (45) days; and

(c) in any such other case, within thirty (30) days.

For the purposes of this section, a prosecution is deemed commenced when—

(a) an indictment, information, or complaint is filed; or

(b) an arrest or bench warrant is issued, provided that the warrant names or describes the defendant with the same degree of particularity required for an indictment, information, or complaint.

For the purposes of this section, time starts to run on the day after the offense is committed, and does not run during a time where—

(a) the accused is not a resident or inhabitant of the State; or

(b) the accused hides himself within the State or otherwise renders himself non-amenable to processes being served upon him.

Nothing in this section shall be construed nor read so as to apply to offenses committed or prosecutions commenced before the date of enactment.

Except as otherwise expressly provided, a civil action may only be commenced for a tort—

(a) where pursuant to title 5, subtitle 1, chapter 3, subchapter 1, parts 1, 2, and 4, Mayflower State Code, within forty (40) days;

(b) where pursuant to title 5, subtitle 1, chapter 3, subchapter 1, parts 3 and 5, Mayflower State Code, within thirty-five (35) days; and

(c) in any such other case, within thirty (30) days.

For the purposes of this section, a civil action is deemed commenced whenacivil complaint or matter is filed or docketed with a court of competent jurisdiction.

For the purposes of this section, time starts to run on the day after the tort is committed, and does not run during a time where—

(a) the tortfeasor is not a resident or inhabitant of the State; or

(b) the tortfeasor hides himself within the State or otherwise renders himself non-amenable to processes being served upon him.

Nothing in this section shall be construed nor read so as to apply to torts committed or civil actions commenced before the date of enactment.

All felony criminal convictions in the State of Mayflower are eligible for the following conviction sentencing guidelines, applicable at the discretion of the sentencing court:

(a) All codified offenses under Title 1, Subtitle 1, Chapter VII “Prohibited Items” may carry a penalty of up to two times its statutory sentence.

(b) All codified offenses under Title 1, Subtitle 2 of the Mayflower State Code “Crimes Against the Player” may carry a penalty of up to four times its statutory sentence.

(c) All codified offenses under Title 1, Subtitle 3 of the Mayflower State Code “Crimes Against Property” may carry a penalty of up to two times its statutory sentence.

(d) All codified offenses under Title 1, Subtitle 6 of the Mayflower State Code “Crimes Involving Firearms and Explosives” may carry a penalty of up to three times its statutory sentence.

(e) All aforementioned guidelines shall be applicable to both the codified sentence and citation penalties.

(i) No citation imposed with respect to these guidelines shall exceed a total of $25,000.00 UCD.

When pursed through a criminal trial, the maximum incarceration time that can be awarded for a—

(a) Felony class offense with an Active status within the Mayflower Criminal Code shall be eighteen (18) times the length of its standard prison sentence length, rounded to the highest minute.

(b) Misdemeanor class offense with an Active status within the Mayflower Criminal Code shall be thirteen (13) times the length of its standard prison sentence length, rounded to the highest minute.

(c) Felony class offense with an Active status within the Mayflower Vehicle Code shall be fifteen (15) times the length of its usual standard sentence length, rounded to the highest minute.

(d) Misdemeanor class offense with an Active status within the Mayflower Vehicle Code shall be ten (10) times the length of its standard prison sentence length, rounded to the highest minute.

No person shall be sentenced to a cumulative term of imprisonment exceeding one hundred twenty (120) hours for violations or enhancements imposed solely under this subchapter with respect to statutes designated as Active status, regardless of the number or combination of applicable enhancements. Statutes designated as By Conviction shall be exempt from this limitation, and any sentence authorized under such statutes may be imposed in addition to the maximum cumulative term permitted under Active status statutes.

“Qualified immunity” means legal protection shielding a law enforcement officer from civil liability for actions performed in the line of duty, unless the officer’s conduct violates clearly established statutory or constitutional rights of which a reasonable person would have known.

A law enforcement officer shall not be held personally liable for civil damages for any act or omission arising out of the performance of their duties, if such act or omission—

(a) was not manifestly outside the scope of the officer’s lawful authority; and

(b) did not violate a clearly established right of which a reasonable law enforcement officer would have known.

Any motion to dismiss based on qualified immunity shall be decided by the court as a matter of law prior to trial. A court may grant qualified immunity at any stage of litigation.

Nothing in parts (1), (2), or (3) of this subchapter shall be construed to limit criminal prosecution of an officer for conduct constituting a criminal offense under state or local law.

Qualified immunity shall not apply where a law enforcement officer is found, by clear and convincing evidence, to have—

(a) acted with malicious intent to cause harm;

(b) engaged in conduct that shocks the conscience; or

(c) willfully violated state constitutional rights.

Qualified immunity shall not apply to actions taken by officers that are entirely unrelated to their duties, or while acting in a purely personal or private capacity.

sections.heading: Felony Murder
sections.text:
An individual shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 2101 “First-degree murder” when they—

(a) Kill, or causes another individual to be killed, while in the commission or attempted commission of one of the following crimes:

(i) 1 M.S.C. § 1302 “Felony Misconduct."

(ii) 1 M.S.C. § 1308 “Felony Evasion."

(iii) 1 M.S.C. § 1311 “Escape."

(iv) 1 M.S.C. § 1312 “Obstruction of Justice."

(v) 1 M.S.C. § 4103 “Inciting a Riot."

(b) Kill, or causes another individual to be killed, while in commission or attempted commission of a felony under the following sections of Title 1 of the Mayflower State Code:

(i) Subtitle 1, Chapter I.

(ii) Subtitle 1, Chapter VI.

(iii) Subtitle 1, Chapter VIII.

(iv) Subtitle 2, Chapter II.

(v) Subtitle 3, Chapter I.

(vi) Subtitle 3, Chapter II.

(vii) Subtitle 4, Chapter III.

(viii) Subtitle 5 or 6.

(c) Are jointly engaged in the commission or attempted commission of any aforementioned felony, and does so with another individual who commits 1 M.S.C. § 2101 First-degree murder in the course of such a felony, and who thereafter continues to participate in any criminal conduct with that individual following the commission of said murder.

sections.heading: Civil Rights Claims
sections.text:
SHORT TITLE. This chapter may be cited as the "Federal Civil Rights Claims Enforcement Act."

DEFINITIONS. The term “Union” or “Union of Columbia” shall refer to the United States of America.

The term “federal civil rights law” shall refer to any law of the Union of Columbia codified in Title 42 of the Union of Columbia Code that protects individual rights against unlawful discrimination, official misconduct, or deprivation of rights under color of law, including but not limited to 42 U.S.C. §§ 1981, 1982, 1983, 1985, 1986 and related provisions.

“Person” shall include any natural person, corporation, partnership, association, union, or other legal entity, and where applicable, includes individuals acting under color of law.

The term “color of law” shall mean any act done by a government official, employee, or agent—whether lawful or unlawful—that is made possible by the authority or appearance of authority granted by law.

The term “court of competent jurisdiction” shall refer to any trial court of general or limited jurisdiction established by the laws of the State of Mayflower that is authorized to hear civil cases.

The term “state actor” shall include any official, employee, or agent of the State of Mayflower or any of its subdivisions, municipalities, or public institutions, as well as any person or entity acting jointly or in concert with such officials or institutions.

Pursuant to the sovereign legislative authority of the State of Mayflower and in accordance with Article One, Section Eleven of the Constitution thereof, the causes of action enumerated in subsection (b) of this Section are hereby adopted into law and may be enforced in any court of competent jurisdiction within the State of Mayflower.

The following federal civil rights statutes, as interpreted and applied by the courts of the Union of Columbia, are hereby given force and effect as state law:

(a) 42 U.S.C. § 1981.

(b) 42 U.S.C. § 1982.

(c) 42 U.S.C. § 1983.

(d) 42 U.S.C. § 1985.

(e) 42 U.S.C. § 1986.

Any court of general jurisdiction within the State of Mayflower is hereby vested with subject matter jurisdiction to hear, adjudicate, and render final judgment on any civil action brought under this Section. Venue, standing, justiciability, and procedural posture shall be determined in accordance with the laws of this State, except where such standards would contravene the substantive rights incorporated herein.

Courts of this State shall be empowered to award all forms of legal and equitable relief authorized under the incorporated provisions, including compensatory and punitive damages (where applicable), declaratory and injunctive relief, costs of litigation, reasonable attorney’s fees, and such other relief as may be necessary to effectuate the remedial purposes of the adopted statutes.

The defenses of qualified immunity, absolute immunity, and any other immunities recognized under the laws of the Union of Columbia shall apply with equal force and effect to actions brought under this Section, unless otherwise abrogated by an act of the legislature or prohibited by the Constitution of the State of Mayflower. No immunity of the State, its political subdivisions, or any of its officers shall operate to bar claims brought under this Section unless expressly preserved by statute.

The provisions of this Section shall be interpreted in pari materia with the laws of the courts of the Union of Columbia. In construing the scope, contours, and operative effect of the incorporated statutes, courts shall afford persuasive and, where appropriate, controlling weight to decisions of the Supreme Court and subordinate tribunals of the Union interpreting such statutes, unless a deviation is compelled by state constitutional mandate or express legislative instruction.

Nothing in this Section shall be construed to preclude or displace the availability of causes of action under the Constitution or laws of the State of Mayflower. A claimant may pursue remedies under both state and federal authority simultaneously or in the alternative.

Unless otherwise provided by statute or the Constitution of the State of Mayflower, all civil actions arising under subchapter 2 of this chapter shall be governed by the rules of civil procedure as promulgated by the Supreme Court of Mayflower, including rules of pleading, service of process, discovery, joinder, and appeal. Where such rules are silent or ambiguous, courts may reference federal procedural precedent for guidance, provided such reliance does not conflict with the laws of this State.

Actions brought pursuant to this Act shall be subject to the following limitations periods, which shall run from the date the cause of action accrues unless tolled under applicable principles of equity:

(a) 42 U.S.C. §§ 1981, 1982, 1983, and 1985 – three (3) months from the date of accrual;

(b) 42 U.S.C. § 1986 – two (2) months from the date the cause of action accrued.

Equitable tolling, estoppel, or other doctrines recognized under the common law of this State may apply to actions brought under this Act, provided that such doctrines are not inconsistent with the remedial purposes of the incorporated provisions. No right of action under this Act shall be deemed extinguished due to inadvertent mislabeling or mispleading, provided the claim arises from the same nucleus of operative fact.

A complaint alleging a cause of action under this Act shall contain a short and plain statement of the claim showing that the pleader is entitled to relief. However, to discourage frivolous litigation and ensure proper notice to defendants, the complaint shall also include:

(a) A clear identification of the specific statutory provision under which relief is sought;

(b) A concise statement of the facts constituting the alleged violation;

(c) The identity of each person or official alleged to have engaged in conduct under color of law or in furtherance of conspiracy; and

(d) A demand for judgment specifying the relief sought.

Any final judgment rendered under this Act shall be accorded full force and effect throughout the State and shall operate as a final adjudication on the merits, subject to the doctrines of res judicata and collateral estoppel as applied by the courts of this State.

This Section shall be liberally construed to ensure the broad protection and full enforcement of civil rights, and no technical defect in form shall be grounds for dismissal where substantive rights may still be adjudicated on the merits.

Subject to the provisions of 5 M.S.C. 1 §§ 3201–3209, the State of Mayflower, its agencies, and its employees acting within the scope of their official duties shall not be deemed to have waived sovereign immunity except where such waiver is explicitly authorized by statute. Nothing in this Act shall be construed to create a general waiver of sovereign immunity beyond what is provided in those sections.

Notwithstanding any other provision of this Act, no individual, agency, or subdivision of the State of Mayflower shall be liable for punitive damages in any civil action brought under this Act. The State shall not be liable for interest prior to judgment or for damages beyond those authorized in 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3207.1.

Liability for compensatory damages in actions against the State, its agencies, or employees shall be limited to actual economic loss, consistent with the standards and procedures set forth in 5 M.S.C. 1 §§ 3203–3205. No action for money damages may be instituted unless a claim is first submitted to the Department of Justice in accordance with 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3204.1.

State officials and employees shall be entitled to qualified immunity in individual-capacity suits brought under this Act, unless the Solicitor General certifies under 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3209.4 that the official was acting outside the scope of employment, or unless the plaintiff shows a violation of a clearly established constitutional or statutory right of which a reasonable person would have known.

Nothing in this Section shall be construed to provide immunity for acts of malfeasance, gross negligence, or willful misconduct, where such acts fall outside the scope of employment or otherwise fail to meet the standards of protection under 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3202.5.

This Act does not impair a plaintiff’s right to seek equitable relief, including injunctive or declaratory relief, against the State, its agencies, or subdivisions for violations of civil rights, provided such relief is consistent with constitutional limits and does not conflict with 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3202.2.

Any claim for relief under this Act must comply with the procedural requirements set forth in 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3203.6, including the three-month filing deadline from the date the cause of action accrues. Failure to comply with these requirements shall bar the claim.

The State shall not be liable for claims based on conduct occurring before the effective date of this Act, unless the plaintiff demonstrates that timely filing was prevented by fraud, concealment, or misconduct by the defendant, consistent with equitable tolling doctrines recognized under State law.

It shall be the duty of the courts of the State of Mayflower to ensure that all actions brought under this Act are handled in a timely and efficient manner. The court shall make every reasonable effort to resolve such cases without unnecessary delay, consistent with the complexity of the case and the rights of the parties involved. The court may, in its discretion, issue scheduling orders to ensure the expeditious progression of the case.

In any action brought under this Act, the court may, upon motion by a party or sua sponte, grant summary judgment when it finds that there is no genuine issue of material fact and that the movant is entitled to judgment as a matter of law. Summary judgment may be entered at any stage of the proceedings, including prior to trial, when the facts and law are sufficiently clear to resolve the dispute.

In all actions brought under this Act, the court shall have broad discretion in determining the appropriate remedies, sanctions, and procedural steps, provided that such actions are consistent with the principles of justice, fairness, and the protection of civil rights. This discretion shall extend to the management of case schedules, the granting of extensions, and the determination of the propriety of evidentiary rulings.

Any judicial officer, attorney, or party involved in a case under this Act who has reason to believe that misconduct has occurred in the course of the proceedings, including but not limited to fraud, bribery, or abuse of power, shall have a duty to report such misconduct to the appropriate disciplinary authority or to the court itself.

In the event that a defendant fails to respond to a complaint brought under this Act within the time prescribed by law, the court may enter a default judgment against the defendant. The plaintiff shall be entitled to proceed with the case as though the defendant had admitted liability, unless the court finds good cause to set aside the default.

In any case involving a settlement of claims under this Act, the court shall review the terms of the settlement to ensure that the agreement is fair, adequate, and in the best interests of justice, particularly where the settlement involves claims on behalf of vulnerable or disadvantaged groups.

In any action brought under this Act, the prevailing party shall be entitled to remedies, as applicable and consistent with the nature of the violation.

In cases where the defendant’s actions were willful, malicious, or reckless, the court may award punitive damages to punish the defendant and deter future violations. Such damages shall be determined based on the defendant’s conduct and the need to deter similar behavior in the future.

The court may issue an order for injunctive relief to prevent further harm, including but not limited to:

(a) Ordering the defendant to cease and desist from unlawful conduct;

(b) Requiring the defendant to take corrective actions, such as policy changes, training, or public notices;

(c) Mandating the defendant to take affirmative actions to rectify any wrongs or prevent recurrence.

The court may issue a declaratory judgment to determine the rights, duties, and obligations of the parties involved, particularly where there is uncertainty about the application of the law to the facts of the case.

The prevailing party shall be entitled to attorneys’ fees and litigation costs incurred in bringing or defending the action. The court may also award such fees and costs to the defendant if the court finds that the plaintiff's claim was frivolous or without merit.

Each day that a violation of this Act continues shall be considered a separate offense for purposes of calculating remedies, penalties, and enforcement actions. The court shall have discretion to impose additional penalties for each day a violation persists.

All remedies and penalties under this Section may be enforced by the courts of the State of Mayflower, including the issuance of orders of execution, garnishment, or other mechanisms as necessary to ensure compliance with any judgment, injunction, or restitution order.

The amount of punitive damages awarded in any case under this Act shall not exceed three (3) times the amount of compensatory damages, except where the defendant’s actions are determined to be particularly egregious or where statutory exceptions apply.

Any party who prevails in an action under this Act shall have the right to recover any penalties or damages awarded as part of the judgment, through any available lawful means of enforcement, including execution of judgment or garnishment.

It shall be unlawful for any person, entity, or government official to retaliate against any individual for exercising their rights under this Act, including but not limited to:

(a) Any individual who files or has filed a civil rights claim under this Act shall not be subject to retaliation, including threats, harassment, or adverse action taken against them in employment or in other aspects of their personal life.

(b) No person shall face retaliation for providing testimony, evidence, or assistance in any civil rights action brought under this Act, even if the action is ultimately dismissed or withdrawn.

(c) No person shall be retaliated against for opposing practices or policies that they reasonably believe to be discriminatory or violative of civil rights under this Act.

Retaliation under this Section includes, but is not limited to:

(a) Any adverse employment action, as stipulated under Title 4, Subtitle 7, Chapter 1, against an individual for exercising their rights under this Act.

(b) Physical or verbal harassment, threats of violence, or actions intended to intimidate or coerce an individual for asserting their civil rights.

(c) Refusal to provide goods, services, or benefits to an individual or group because they have exercised their civil rights or filed a claim.

(d) Any deliberate efforts to harm an individual's reputation, relationships, or social standing through wrongful means as a result of their involvement in civil rights litigation.

Any person who proves retaliation under this Section shall be entitled to the following remedies:

(a) As provided in paragraph 1601 of this chapter, compensatory damages for harm suffered as a result of retaliation, including but not limited to:

(i) Harm to reputation or social standing;

(ii) Loss of opportunities for advancement.

(b) As provided in paragraph 1602 of this chapter, the court may award punitive damages if the retaliation is found to be willful, malicious, or grossly negligent.

(c) The court may issue an order requiring the defendant to cease retaliation or restore the affected individual's rights or benefits.

(d) Where an individual's employment, services, or benefits were adversely affected by retaliation, the court may order the restoration of such rights or benefits, including re-employment or reinstatement to the same position.

(e) As provided in paragraph 1605 of this chapter, the prevailing party may be entitled to reimbursement for attorneys' fees and litigation costs incurred as a result of the retaliation claim.

In any action alleging retaliation, the plaintiff shall be required to demonstrate, by a preponderance of the evidence:

(a) That they engaged in a protected activity under this Act (such as filing a claim, testifying, or opposing discriminatory practices);

(b) That the defendant took an adverse action against them that would be considered retaliatory under this Section;

(c) That there is a causal connection between the protected activity and the adverse action taken.

Nothing in this Section shall be construed to waive any other legal remedies available to individuals under state law for retaliation, nor shall it limit any rights individuals may have to bring a separate cause of action under applicable laws for retaliatory conduct outside of the provisions of this Act.
