parts.heading: Subchapter I — DEFINITION / Part III — EXCEPTIONS
parts.text:
SHORT TITLE. This chapter may be cited as the "Federal Civil Rights Claims Enforcement Act."

DEFINITIONS. The term “Union” or “Union of Columbia” shall refer to the United States of America.

The term “federal civil rights law” shall refer to any law of the Union of Columbia codified in Title 42 of the Union of Columbia Code that protects individual rights against unlawful discrimination, official misconduct, or deprivation of rights under color of law, including but not limited to 42 U.S.C. §§ 1981, 1982, 1983, 1985, 1986 and related provisions.

“Person” shall include any natural person, corporation, partnership, association, union, or other legal entity, and where applicable, includes individuals acting under color of law.

The term “color of law” shall mean any act done by a government official, employee, or agent—whether lawful or unlawful—that is made possible by the authority or appearance of authority granted by law.

The term “court of competent jurisdiction” shall refer to any trial court of general or limited jurisdiction established by the laws of the State of Mayflower that is authorized to hear civil cases.

The term “state actor” shall include any official, employee, or agent of the State of Mayflower or any of its subdivisions, municipalities, or public institutions, as well as any person or entity acting jointly or in concert with such officials or institutions.

parts.heading: Subchapter II — ENFORCEMENT OF FEDERAL CIVIL RIGHTS IN STATE COURTS / Part III — EXCEPTIONS
parts.text:
Pursuant to the sovereign legislative authority of the State of Mayflower and in accordance with Article One, Section Eleven of the Constitution thereof, the causes of action enumerated in subsection (b) of this Section are hereby adopted into law and may be enforced in any court of competent jurisdiction within the State of Mayflower.

The following federal civil rights statutes, as interpreted and applied by the courts of the Union of Columbia, are hereby given force and effect as state law:

(a) 42 U.S.C. § 1981.

(b) 42 U.S.C. § 1982.

(c) 42 U.S.C. § 1983.

(d) 42 U.S.C. § 1985.

(e) 42 U.S.C. § 1986.

Any court of general jurisdiction within the State of Mayflower is hereby vested with subject matter jurisdiction to hear, adjudicate, and render final judgment on any civil action brought under this Section. Venue, standing, justiciability, and procedural posture shall be determined in accordance with the laws of this State, except where such standards would contravene the substantive rights incorporated herein.

Courts of this State shall be empowered to award all forms of legal and equitable relief authorized under the incorporated provisions, including compensatory and punitive damages (where applicable), declaratory and injunctive relief, costs of litigation, reasonable attorney’s fees, and such other relief as may be necessary to effectuate the remedial purposes of the adopted statutes.

The defenses of qualified immunity, absolute immunity, and any other immunities recognized under the laws of the Union of Columbia shall apply with equal force and effect to actions brought under this Section, unless otherwise abrogated by an act of the legislature or prohibited by the Constitution of the State of Mayflower. No immunity of the State, its political subdivisions, or any of its officers shall operate to bar claims brought under this Section unless expressly preserved by statute.

The provisions of this Section shall be interpreted in pari materia with the laws of the courts of the Union of Columbia. In construing the scope, contours, and operative effect of the incorporated statutes, courts shall afford persuasive and, where appropriate, controlling weight to decisions of the Supreme Court and subordinate tribunals of the Union interpreting such statutes, unless a deviation is compelled by state constitutional mandate or express legislative instruction.

Nothing in this Section shall be construed to preclude or displace the availability of causes of action under the Constitution or laws of the State of Mayflower. A claimant may pursue remedies under both state and federal authority simultaneously or in the alternative.

parts.heading: Subchapter III — PROCEDURAL STANDARDS, LIMITATIONS, AND PRESERVATION OF CLAIMS / Part III — EXCEPTIONS
parts.text:
Unless otherwise provided by statute or the Constitution of the State of Mayflower, all civil actions arising under subchapter 2 of this chapter shall be governed by the rules of civil procedure as promulgated by the Supreme Court of Mayflower, including rules of pleading, service of process, discovery, joinder, and appeal. Where such rules are silent or ambiguous, courts may reference federal procedural precedent for guidance, provided such reliance does not conflict with the laws of this State.

Actions brought pursuant to this Act shall be subject to the following limitations periods, which shall run from the date the cause of action accrues unless tolled under applicable principles of equity:

(a) 42 U.S.C. §§ 1981, 1982, 1983, and 1985 – three (3) months from the date of accrual;

(b) 42 U.S.C. § 1986 – two (2) months from the date the cause of action accrued.

Equitable tolling, estoppel, or other doctrines recognized under the common law of this State may apply to actions brought under this Act, provided that such doctrines are not inconsistent with the remedial purposes of the incorporated provisions. No right of action under this Act shall be deemed extinguished due to inadvertent mislabeling or mispleading, provided the claim arises from the same nucleus of operative fact.

A complaint alleging a cause of action under this Act shall contain a short and plain statement of the claim showing that the pleader is entitled to relief. However, to discourage frivolous litigation and ensure proper notice to defendants, the complaint shall also include:

(a) A clear identification of the specific statutory provision under which relief is sought;

(b) A concise statement of the facts constituting the alleged violation;

(c) The identity of each person or official alleged to have engaged in conduct under color of law or in furtherance of conspiracy; and

(d) A demand for judgment specifying the relief sought.

Any final judgment rendered under this Act shall be accorded full force and effect throughout the State and shall operate as a final adjudication on the merits, subject to the doctrines of res judicata and collateral estoppel as applied by the courts of this State.

This Section shall be liberally construed to ensure the broad protection and full enforcement of civil rights, and no technical defect in form shall be grounds for dismissal where substantive rights may still be adjudicated on the merits.

parts.heading: Subchapter IV — SOVERIGN IMMUNITY AND LIMITATIONS ON LIABILITY / Part III — EXCEPTIONS
parts.text:
Subject to the provisions of 5 M.S.C. 1 §§ 3201–3209, the State of Mayflower, its agencies, and its employees acting within the scope of their official duties shall not be deemed to have waived sovereign immunity except where such waiver is explicitly authorized by statute. Nothing in this Act shall be construed to create a general waiver of sovereign immunity beyond what is provided in those sections.

Notwithstanding any other provision of this Act, no individual, agency, or subdivision of the State of Mayflower shall be liable for punitive damages in any civil action brought under this Act. The State shall not be liable for interest prior to judgment or for damages beyond those authorized in 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3207.1.

Liability for compensatory damages in actions against the State, its agencies, or employees shall be limited to actual economic loss, consistent with the standards and procedures set forth in 5 M.S.C. 1 §§ 3203–3205. No action for money damages may be instituted unless a claim is first submitted to the Department of Justice in accordance with 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3204.1.

State officials and employees shall be entitled to qualified immunity in individual-capacity suits brought under this Act, unless the Solicitor General certifies under 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3209.4 that the official was acting outside the scope of employment, or unless the plaintiff shows a violation of a clearly established constitutional or statutory right of which a reasonable person would have known.

Nothing in this Section shall be construed to provide immunity for acts of malfeasance, gross negligence, or willful misconduct, where such acts fall outside the scope of employment or otherwise fail to meet the standards of protection under 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3202.5.

This Act does not impair a plaintiff’s right to seek equitable relief, including injunctive or declaratory relief, against the State, its agencies, or subdivisions for violations of civil rights, provided such relief is consistent with constitutional limits and does not conflict with 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3202.2.

Any claim for relief under this Act must comply with the procedural requirements set forth in 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3203.6, including the three-month filing deadline from the date the cause of action accrues. Failure to comply with these requirements shall bar the claim.

The State shall not be liable for claims based on conduct occurring before the effective date of this Act, unless the plaintiff demonstrates that timely filing was prevented by fraud, concealment, or misconduct by the defendant, consistent with equitable tolling doctrines recognized under State law.

parts.heading: Subchapter V — JUDICIAL OVERSIGHT AND COURT PROCEDURE / Part III — EXCEPTIONS
parts.text:
It shall be the duty of the courts of the State of Mayflower to ensure that all actions brought under this Act are handled in a timely and efficient manner. The court shall make every reasonable effort to resolve such cases without unnecessary delay, consistent with the complexity of the case and the rights of the parties involved. The court may, in its discretion, issue scheduling orders to ensure the expeditious progression of the case.

In any action brought under this Act, the court may, upon motion by a party or sua sponte, grant summary judgment when it finds that there is no genuine issue of material fact and that the movant is entitled to judgment as a matter of law. Summary judgment may be entered at any stage of the proceedings, including prior to trial, when the facts and law are sufficiently clear to resolve the dispute.

In all actions brought under this Act, the court shall have broad discretion in determining the appropriate remedies, sanctions, and procedural steps, provided that such actions are consistent with the principles of justice, fairness, and the protection of civil rights. This discretion shall extend to the management of case schedules, the granting of extensions, and the determination of the propriety of evidentiary rulings.

Any judicial officer, attorney, or party involved in a case under this Act who has reason to believe that misconduct has occurred in the course of the proceedings, including but not limited to fraud, bribery, or abuse of power, shall have a duty to report such misconduct to the appropriate disciplinary authority or to the court itself.

In the event that a defendant fails to respond to a complaint brought under this Act within the time prescribed by law, the court may enter a default judgment against the defendant. The plaintiff shall be entitled to proceed with the case as though the defendant had admitted liability, unless the court finds good cause to set aside the default.

In any case involving a settlement of claims under this Act, the court shall review the terms of the settlement to ensure that the agreement is fair, adequate, and in the best interests of justice, particularly where the settlement involves claims on behalf of vulnerable or disadvantaged groups.

parts.heading: Subchapter VI — REMEDIES AND PENALTIES / Part III — EXCEPTIONS
parts.text:
In any action brought under this Act, the prevailing party shall be entitled to remedies, as applicable and consistent with the nature of the violation.

In cases where the defendant’s actions were willful, malicious, or reckless, the court may award punitive damages to punish the defendant and deter future violations. Such damages shall be determined based on the defendant’s conduct and the need to deter similar behavior in the future.

The court may issue an order for injunctive relief to prevent further harm, including but not limited to:

(a) Ordering the defendant to cease and desist from unlawful conduct;

(b) Requiring the defendant to take corrective actions, such as policy changes, training, or public notices;

(c) Mandating the defendant to take affirmative actions to rectify any wrongs or prevent recurrence.

The court may issue a declaratory judgment to determine the rights, duties, and obligations of the parties involved, particularly where there is uncertainty about the application of the law to the facts of the case.

The prevailing party shall be entitled to attorneys’ fees and litigation costs incurred in bringing or defending the action. The court may also award such fees and costs to the defendant if the court finds that the plaintiff's claim was frivolous or without merit.

Each day that a violation of this Act continues shall be considered a separate offense for purposes of calculating remedies, penalties, and enforcement actions. The court shall have discretion to impose additional penalties for each day a violation persists.

All remedies and penalties under this Section may be enforced by the courts of the State of Mayflower, including the issuance of orders of execution, garnishment, or other mechanisms as necessary to ensure compliance with any judgment, injunction, or restitution order.

The amount of punitive damages awarded in any case under this Act shall not exceed three (3) times the amount of compensatory damages, except where the defendant’s actions are determined to be particularly egregious or where statutory exceptions apply.

Any party who prevails in an action under this Act shall have the right to recover any penalties or damages awarded as part of the judgment, through any available lawful means of enforcement, including execution of judgment or garnishment.

It shall be unlawful for any person, entity, or government official to retaliate against any individual for exercising their rights under this Act, including but not limited to:

(a) Any individual who files or has filed a civil rights claim under this Act shall not be subject to retaliation, including threats, harassment, or adverse action taken against them in employment or in other aspects of their personal life.

(b) No person shall face retaliation for providing testimony, evidence, or assistance in any civil rights action brought under this Act, even if the action is ultimately dismissed or withdrawn.

(c) No person shall be retaliated against for opposing practices or policies that they reasonably believe to be discriminatory or violative of civil rights under this Act.

Retaliation under this Section includes, but is not limited to:

(a) Any adverse employment action, as stipulated under Title 4, Subtitle 7, Chapter 1, against an individual for exercising their rights under this Act.

(b) Physical or verbal harassment, threats of violence, or actions intended to intimidate or coerce an individual for asserting their civil rights.

(c) Refusal to provide goods, services, or benefits to an individual or group because they have exercised their civil rights or filed a claim.

(d) Any deliberate efforts to harm an individual's reputation, relationships, or social standing through wrongful means as a result of their involvement in civil rights litigation.

Any person who proves retaliation under this Section shall be entitled to the following remedies:

(a) As provided in paragraph 1601 of this chapter, compensatory damages for harm suffered as a result of retaliation, including but not limited to:

(i) Harm to reputation or social standing;

(ii) Loss of opportunities for advancement.

(b) As provided in paragraph 1602 of this chapter, the court may award punitive damages if the retaliation is found to be willful, malicious, or grossly negligent.

(c) The court may issue an order requiring the defendant to cease retaliation or restore the affected individual's rights or benefits.

(d) Where an individual's employment, services, or benefits were adversely affected by retaliation, the court may order the restoration of such rights or benefits, including re-employment or reinstatement to the same position.

(e) As provided in paragraph 1605 of this chapter, the prevailing party may be entitled to reimbursement for attorneys' fees and litigation costs incurred as a result of the retaliation claim.

In any action alleging retaliation, the plaintiff shall be required to demonstrate, by a preponderance of the evidence:

(a) That they engaged in a protected activity under this Act (such as filing a claim, testifying, or opposing discriminatory practices);

(b) That the defendant took an adverse action against them that would be considered retaliatory under this Section;

(c) That there is a causal connection between the protected activity and the adverse action taken.

Nothing in this Section shall be construed to waive any other legal remedies available to individuals under state law for retaliation, nor shall it limit any rights individuals may have to bring a separate cause of action under applicable laws for retaliatory conduct outside of the provisions of this Act.

sections.heading: State Highways and Road Closures
sections.text:
The term “State highway” shall refer to:

(a) The Jones Beltway

(b) State Route 55

(c) Any road operated by the State or any political subdivision thereof with a posted speed limit of greater then seventy (70) studs per second.

State Highways and Public Roads may not be subject to full closure without the permission of the Secretary of Transportation, Colonel of the State Police, the Governor, a municipal police chief, or a county sheriff.

The stud per second unit shall be analogous and equivalent to the mile per hour unit.

The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall be responsible for the maintenance, upkeep, and administration of all highway entrances and exits, public roads, state highways, and overpasses within the state.

The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall maintain a plan for emergency response in the eventuality of any emergency occurring on any overpass, public roadway, highway entrance or exit, or state highway.

Members of the Mayflower Transportation Authority shall have the authority to enact reduced speed limit zones and reduced speed advisories which shall be clearly posted using clearly posted signage, for one or more of the following reasons:

(a) to enhance personnel and public safety during the clearing of traffic incidents within highway entrances and exits, public roads, state highways, and overpasses;

(b) to enhance personnel and public safety during the clearing of or otherwise managing hazards within highway entrances and exits, public roads, state highways, and overpasses;

(c) to enhance personnel and public safety during a law enforcement checkpoint on a public roads or highways; or

(d) to enhance personnel and public safety while maintenance is being conducted within highway entrances and exits, public roads, state highways, and overpasses.

DESYNCING. “Desyncing” shall refer to the act of purposefully swerving a vehicle across a lane whilst at high speeds to exploit a bug that causes any vehicles behind the actor to be flung about and crash.

“Law Enforcement Officer” shall refer to any peace officer formally recognised under the state code as a Law Enforcement Officer, holds an active LETI certification and is an on-duty officer of a Law Enforcement Agency.

The act of desyncing a vehicle shall be considered as reckless driving and shall be arrestable under the ‘Reckless Driving’ offence in the Mayflower State Vehicle Code, at the discretion of the arresting law enforcement officer.

All law enforcement officers whilst on-duty and protecting the peace shall be exempt from this law and may utilize desyncing at their discretion during pursuits/as per their department standard operating procedure code.

Citizens acting in a vigilante capacity to assist law enforcement officers in the apprehension of a fleeing suspect that drive recklessly in the commission of desyncing a suspect, shall not be exempt from the aforementioned law and may be arrested per the discretion of a law enforcement officer.

A “road Closure” or “full Road Closure” shall be defined as the blockage and/or restriction of a roadway from civilians and/or individuals who are not essential to the given situation or circumstance(s). The individual(s) who are restricted from the closed roadway shall be designated at the discretion of the individual leading or commanding the circumstance/situation/incident that caused the road closure.

A “road closure” shall also include the partial restriction and/or blockage of a roadway. Any government authority authorized by this section to initiate a road closure may initiate a partial road closure instead. The term “Road Closure” shall also include a partial road closure any time it is referenced in this section.

A “partial road closure” shall be defined as a road closure that does not require a detour and still allows two-way travel on the partially closed road.

The term “roadway," “road,” or "highway" includes a common and public highway, street, avenue, parkway, driveway, square, place, bridge, viaduct or trestle, any part of which is intended for or used for the passage of vehicles and includes the area between the lateral property lines thereof.

The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall have the ability to execute the closure of certain roads, either in the support of a law enforcement closure or for maintenance and repair to road infrastructure.

Law enforcement officers execute road closures for:

(a) The preservation of a crime scene

(b) The securing of governmental or non-governmental property in connection with an authorized exercise of authority

(c) Officer or civilian safety in light of ongoing criminal activity

(d) An approved event, either a civilian assembly/event with the permission of the County Sheriff or State Police Colonel, or a government-sanctioned event with the approval of the relevant department head.

(e) Any active scene relating to their official duties, where the flow of traffic may endanger or obstruct on-scene personnel or endanger the lives of responding officers, or hinder the ability to combat crime

(f) Situation where the flow of traffic on a roadway near the situation may endanger or obstruct on-scene personnel.

Fire/Rescue personnel may execute road closures for:

(a) Any active scene relating to their official duties, where the flow of traffic may endanger or obstruct on-scene personnel or patients

(b) The securing of governmental or non-governmental property in connection with an authorized exercise of authority

(c) Officer or civilian safety in light of ongoing criminal activity

(d) An approved event, either a civilian assembly/event with the permission of the County Sheriff or State Police Colonel, or a government-sanctioned event with the approval of the relevant department head.

Fire/Rescue Services at the Municipal and County levels may also execute the closure of certain roads in connection with active fire/rescue scenes, training, or operations.

Medical services, both private and government-owned, may close off the immediate area, including roads, connected to a medical call or situation.

Specific roads or streets may be closed for government events or training at the direction of a Department Head or Governor.

Civilians wishing to host an assembly, event, or demonstration may, with or without connection to a protest permit, request for the department head of the Mayflower Transportation Authority to order the closure of certain roads connected to said assembly, event, or demonstration.

Any person who stands on any equipment placed on or near any highway with the textual markings containing "POLICE" that could or may obstruct the efficacy of the equipment shall be guilty of Obstruction of Justice.

Any individual who does not comply with the road closures handbook shall be liable to be issued a citation or arrested for 2 M.S.C. § 1211 “Obstruction of Traffic”.

The Secretary of Transportation shall have oversight of the authority and appoint an Administrator, who shall serve at the pleasure of the Secretary of Transportation and shall be responsible for the direction and management of the Transportation Authority.

The Administrator of the Transportation Authority shall:

(a) Have the authority to delegate in writing any powers and duties in this act, or its regulations, to a member or office of their respective department, subject to any limitations, conditions or requirements set out in the delegation.

(b) Be the final authority for carrying out all functions, powers, and duties of the Transportation Authority relating to: the appointment and employment of all officers and employees of the Transportation Authority (other than gubernatorial and political appointees); the acquisition and maintenance of property, services, and equipment of the Transportation Authority; the promulgation of regulations, rules, orders, circulars, bulletins, and other official publications of the Transportation Authority, except as otherwise provided; and any other obligation imposed on or power conferred upon the Administrator.

(c) Appoint a Deputy Administrator which shall assist the Administrator with directing the Transportation Authority and shall be deemed the second-in-command of the Transportation Authority.

(d) Have the authority to delegate and authorize successive re-delegations of, to an officer or employee of the Transportation Authority any function, power, or duty conferred upon the Administrator unless such delegation is prohibited by law.

(e) While performing the functions of the Administrator and the Transportation Authority, have the authority to issue, rescind, and revise such regulations as necessary to carry out those functions.

(f) Have the authority to establish ranks and offices as deemed necessary.

The Secretary of Transportation, or their designee(s), shall create, maintain, and enforce Rules of Conduct that the public is expected to observe when using public transportation, or when within property owned by the MTA.

(a) The Rules of Conduct shall be publicly accessible.

(b) The Rules of Conduct shall only be amended when approved by the Secretary of Transportation or their designee(s), however the effective date of such an amendment shall be at least 3 days after public proclamation of the update.

EXPANSION. Members of the Mayflower Transportation Authority shall have the ability to enact road closure for the purpose of:

(a) responding to and clearing motor vehicle accidents;

(b) clearing and or otherwise managing hazards on public roadways;

(c) assisting with law enforcement checkpoints; or

(d) conducting maintenance on a public road.

The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall have the jurisdiction to conduct their lawful duties which shall include the operation of public transportation, the maintenance and operation of public roads, and the clearance of motor vehicle accidents and hazards on public roads throughout the state and shall not be obstructed.

(a) Those in violation of this section shall be guilty of “Obstruction of Transportation Authority Personnel."

The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall have the jurisdiction to conduct their lawful duties which shall include the maintenance, inspection, and operation of public commuter rail systems within the state and shall not be obstructed.

(a) Those in violation of this section shall be guilty of “Obstruction of Transportation Authority Personnel”.

The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall have the jurisdiction to conduct their lawful duties which shall include the clearance of motor vehicle accidents, and the clearance of hazards on any bridge or tunnel within the state and shall not be obstructed.

(a) Those in violation of this section shall be guilty of “Obstruction of Transportation Authority Personnel”.

DEFINITIONS. A “residential roadway” shall be defined as a road within a residential neighbourhood.

An “urban roadway” shall be defined as a road within a city limit.

A “rural roadway” shall be defined as a roadway outside of a city limit.

SPEED LIMITS. Unless otherwise signed, the speed limit of a residential roadway shall be 30 mph.

Unless otherwise signed, the speed limit of an urban roadway shall be 50 mph.

Unless otherwise signed, the speed limit of a rural roadway shall be 70 mph.

The Mayflower Division of Motor Vehicles (hereinafter “Division of Motor Vehicles”, “Division”, or “DMV”) shall be established as a subordinate entity of the Mayflower Department of Transportation.

The Secretary of Transportation shall have administrative oversight authority over the Division and may appoint a Commissioner of Motor Vehicles, who shall serve at the pleasure of the Secretary of Transportation and shall be responsible for the direction and management of the Division.

The Commissioner of Motor Vehicles shall:

(a) Be the final authority for carrying out all functions, powers, and duties of the Division relating to: the appointment and employment of all officers and employees of the Division; the acquisition and maintenance of property, services, and equipment of the Division; the promulgation of regulations, rules, orders, and other official publications of the Division, except as otherwise provided; and any other obligation imposed on or power conferred upon the Commissioner.

(i) The Commissioner shall additionally have the authority to delegate and authorize successive re-delegations of any function, power, or duty conferred upon the Commissioner to an officer or employee of the Division (unless such delegation is prohibited by law) and to issue, rescind, and revise such regulations as may be necessary to carry out the functions of the Commissioner and the Division.

(b) Offer advice and counsel to the Governor and Secretary of Transportation with respect to the licensing, registration, and identification functions of the state.

(c) Have the authority to establish, restructure, or dissolve ranks, offices, subdivisions, and positions within the Division as deemed necessary for the effective administration and operation of the Division.

(d) Perform any other reasonable duties or functions as directed by the Secretary of Transportation.

DEFINITIONS. “Department” or “MDOT” refers to the Mayflower Department of Transportation, as defined under 6 M.S.C. 6 § 1108.

“Emergency Services Entity” or “ESE” shall refer to the agency, division, unit, or organization established under this act by the Department.

“Subordinate Agencies” refer to any agency, authority, office, division, or entity established under, administered by, or placed under the jurisdiction of the Mayflower Department of Transportation, including but not limited to those listed under 6 M.S.C. 6 § 1111(b), and any such entities that may be created or designated by law or regulation in the future.

“Transportation Infrastructure” includes highways, roads, tunnels, bridges, heliports, railways, subway stations, terminals, rights-of-way, and any public transportation systems, facilities, or assets owned, operated, maintained, or administered by MDOT or any of its subordinate agencies.

“Department Property” includes all real and personal property under the jurisdiction, ownership, lease, administration, or management of MDOT or any of its subordinate agencies.

AUTHORIZATION TO ESTABLISH EMERGENCY SERVICES ENTITY. The Department is hereby authorized to create and maintain an Emergency Services Entity (ESE) for the following purposes:

(a) Fire protection and suppression;

(b) Technical, confined space, and transportation-related rescues;

(c) Hazardous materials response and containment;

(d) Emergency medical care and transport services;

(e) Emergency and critical incident response;

(f) Execution and coordination of field-level emergency preparedness and hazard mitigation activities across transportation infrastructure, in alignment with departmental emergency management protocols.

The ESE shall operate under the jurisdiction and oversight of the Secretary of Transportation or their designee.

The Secretary of Transportation shall designate a head of the Emergency Services Entity, whose title, rank, and duties shall be determined by the Secretary. This individual shall be responsible for the administration, direction, and daily operations of the ESE, and shall serve at the pleasure of the Secretary.

(a) The head of the ESE may, subject to departmental regulations, delegate responsibilities to subordinate officers or personnel, and may establish internal ranks and positions, offices and divisions, and internal regulations and standard operating procedures consistent with the ESE’s mission and the policies of the Department.

ESE JURISDICTION AND OPERATIONAL AUTHORITY. The ESE shall have principal operational jurisdiction over:

(a) Any transportation infrastructure or department property;

(b) Any areas within a reasonable proximity to transportation infrastructure or department property, when necessary for emergency response, scene safety, or public safety.

The ESE shall have subordinate jurisdiction over:

(a) Any area when requested by law enforcement or other emergency response and public safety agencies;

(b) Any area during a declared State of Emergency, as authorized by applicable law or executive order.

The ESE may engage in joint operations in coordination with private-sector, local, county, or state agencies.

The ESE may enter mutual aid and interagency agreements to ensure seamless emergency operations across jurisdictional boundaries.

(a) All county-level fire suppression and emergency medical service agencies shall have jurisdiction to conduct and provide firefighting, rescue, and medical-related operations within areas under the principal jurisdiction of the ESE. However, while operating within such areas, these agencies shall do so under subordinate jurisdiction to the ESE.

ESE POWERS AND RESPONSIBILITIES. The ESE shall have the authority to:

(a) Employ certified firefighters, EMTs, paramedics, rescue technicians, and other emergency or administrative personnel;

(b) Procure and maintain emergency apparatus, rescue equipment, fire protection systems, and related infrastructure;

(c) Issue on-scene safety and evacuation orders in the interest of public safety on or around transportation infrastructure or department property;

(d) Enforce applicable fire and safety codes and emergency protocols on department property;

(e) Issue directives related to emergency evacuation, hazardous condition mitigation, and life safety response on transportation infrastructure and related department property;

(f) Restrict access to or close roadways, highways, rail lines, terminals, or other department property or transportation infrastructure during active emergencies, incidents, training operations, or hazardous conditions, and direct or manage the flow of traffic in support of emergency operations, in accordance with applicable state transportation and public safety regulations;

(g) Collaborate with law enforcement, medical, and public safety entities in active incident zones or emergency drills;

(h) Perform any other function necessary to protect life, property, and the safety of transportation systems under the Department's jurisdiction, or as deemed necessary by the Secretary of Transportation.

AUTHORIZATION TO ESTABLISH EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT ENTITY. The Mayflower Department of Transportation (MDOT) is hereby authorized to establish an entity, division, or office within the Department for the purpose of emergency management, coordination, and preparedness across all MDOT agencies, properties, and transportation systems.

This entity shall be responsible for:

(a) Strategic planning and coordination of departmental emergency response;

(b) Development and maintenance of continuity of operations plans;

(c) Interagency coordination with state, county, municipal, and private-sector emergency management offices, public safety entities, and subordinate agencies;

(d) Oversight of disaster preparedness exercises and emergency drills across MDOT assets;

(e) Management of emergency communication systems and alert protocols;

(f) Advising MDOT leadership on emergency response readiness and threat mitigation strategies.

The Secretary of Transportation shall have the discretion to determine the name, structure, leadership, and staffing of the emergency management entity, and may issue such directives, regulations, or orders as necessary to support its operations.

Law enforcement officers shall be required to, where feasible:

(a) Ensure that vehicles engaged in a traffic stop on a highway are completely off the roadway.

(b) Park vehicles belonging to a detained individual in a legal location. Law enforcement officers shall be able to request for the Mayflower Department of Transportation to do so in their place.

parts.text:

(b) State Route 55

(c) Any road operated by the State or any political subdivision thereof with a posted speed limit of greater then seventy (70) studs per second.

Members of the Mayflower Transportation Authority shall have the authority to enact reduced speed limit zones and reduced speed advisories which shall be clearly posted using clearly posted signage, for one or more of the following reasons:

(a) to enhance personnel and public safety during the clearing of traffic incidents within highway entrances and exits, public roads, state highways, and overpasses;

(b) to enhance personnel and public safety during the clearing of or otherwise managing hazards within highway entrances and exits, public roads, state highways, and overpasses;

(c) to enhance personnel and public safety during a law enforcement checkpoint on a public roads or highways; or

(d) to enhance personnel and public safety while maintenance is being conducted within highway entrances and exits, public roads, state highways, and overpasses.

DESYNCING. “Desyncing” shall refer to the act of purposefully swerving a vehicle across a lane whilst at high speeds to exploit a bug that causes any vehicles behind the actor to be flung about and crash.

“Law Enforcement Officer” shall refer to any peace officer formally recognised under the state code as a Law Enforcement Officer, holds an active LETI certification and is an on-duty officer of a Law Enforcement Agency.

The act of desyncing a vehicle shall be considered as reckless driving and shall be arrestable under the ‘Reckless Driving’ offence in the Mayflower State Vehicle Code, at the discretion of the arresting law enforcement officer.

All law enforcement officers whilst on-duty and protecting the peace shall be exempt from this law and may utilize desyncing at their discretion during pursuits/as per their department standard operating procedure code.

Citizens acting in a vigilante capacity to assist law enforcement officers in the apprehension of a fleeing suspect that drive recklessly in the commission of desyncing a suspect, shall not be exempt from the aforementioned law and may be arrested per the discretion of a law enforcement officer.

parts.heading: Subchapter II — ROAD CLOSURES
parts.text:
A “road Closure” or “full Road Closure” shall be defined as the blockage and/or restriction of a roadway from civilians and/or individuals who are not essential to the given situation or circumstance(s). The individual(s) who are restricted from the closed roadway shall be designated at the discretion of the individual leading or commanding the circumstance/situation/incident that caused the road closure.

A “road closure” shall also include the partial restriction and/or blockage of a roadway. Any government authority authorized by this section to initiate a road closure may initiate a partial road closure instead. The term “Road Closure” shall also include a partial road closure any time it is referenced in this section.

A “partial road closure” shall be defined as a road closure that does not require a detour and still allows two-way travel on the partially closed road.

The term “roadway," “road,” or "highway" includes a common and public highway, street, avenue, parkway, driveway, square, place, bridge, viaduct or trestle, any part of which is intended for or used for the passage of vehicles and includes the area between the lateral property lines thereof.

The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall have the ability to execute the closure of certain roads, either in the support of a law enforcement closure or for maintenance and repair to road infrastructure.

Law enforcement officers execute road closures for:

(a) The preservation of a crime scene

(b) The securing of governmental or non-governmental property in connection with an authorized exercise of authority

(c) Officer or civilian safety in light of ongoing criminal activity

(d) An approved event, either a civilian assembly/event with the permission of the County Sheriff or State Police Colonel, or a government-sanctioned event with the approval of the relevant department head.

(e) Any active scene relating to their official duties, where the flow of traffic may endanger or obstruct on-scene personnel or endanger the lives of responding officers, or hinder the ability to combat crime

(f) Situation where the flow of traffic on a roadway near the situation may endanger or obstruct on-scene personnel.

Fire/Rescue personnel may execute road closures for:

(a) Any active scene relating to their official duties, where the flow of traffic may endanger or obstruct on-scene personnel or patients

(b) The securing of governmental or non-governmental property in connection with an authorized exercise of authority

(c) Officer or civilian safety in light of ongoing criminal activity

(d) An approved event, either a civilian assembly/event with the permission of the County Sheriff or State Police Colonel, or a government-sanctioned event with the approval of the relevant department head.

Fire/Rescue Services at the Municipal and County levels may also execute the closure of certain roads in connection with active fire/rescue scenes, training, or operations.

Medical services, both private and government-owned, may close off the immediate area, including roads, connected to a medical call or situation.

Specific roads or streets may be closed for government events or training at the direction of a Department Head or Governor.

Civilians wishing to host an assembly, event, or demonstration may, with or without connection to a protest permit, request for the department head of the Mayflower Transportation Authority to order the closure of certain roads connected to said assembly, event, or demonstration.

Any person who stands on any equipment placed on or near any highway with the textual markings containing "POLICE" that could or may obstruct the efficacy of the equipment shall be guilty of Obstruction of Justice.

Any individual who does not comply with the road closures handbook shall be liable to be issued a citation or arrested for 2 M.S.C. § 1211 “Obstruction of Traffic”.

parts.heading: Subchapter III — MAYFLOWER TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY; POLICE DEPARTMENT ESTABLISHMENT
parts.text:
The Secretary of Transportation shall have oversight of the authority and appoint an Administrator, who shall serve at the pleasure of the Secretary of Transportation and shall be responsible for the direction and management of the Transportation Authority.

The Administrator of the Transportation Authority shall:

(a) Have the authority to delegate in writing any powers and duties in this act, or its regulations, to a member or office of their respective department, subject to any limitations, conditions or requirements set out in the delegation.

(b) Be the final authority for carrying out all functions, powers, and duties of the Transportation Authority relating to: the appointment and employment of all officers and employees of the Transportation Authority (other than gubernatorial and political appointees); the acquisition and maintenance of property, services, and equipment of the Transportation Authority; the promulgation of regulations, rules, orders, circulars, bulletins, and other official publications of the Transportation Authority, except as otherwise provided; and any other obligation imposed on or power conferred upon the Administrator.

(c) Appoint a Deputy Administrator which shall assist the Administrator with directing the Transportation Authority and shall be deemed the second-in-command of the Transportation Authority.

(d) Have the authority to delegate and authorize successive re-delegations of, to an officer or employee of the Transportation Authority any function, power, or duty conferred upon the Administrator unless such delegation is prohibited by law.

(e) While performing the functions of the Administrator and the Transportation Authority, have the authority to issue, rescind, and revise such regulations as necessary to carry out those functions.

(f) Have the authority to establish ranks and offices as deemed necessary.

The Secretary of Transportation, or their designee(s), shall create, maintain, and enforce Rules of Conduct that the public is expected to observe when using public transportation, or when within property owned by the MTA.

(a) The Rules of Conduct shall be publicly accessible.

(b) The Rules of Conduct shall only be amended when approved by the Secretary of Transportation or their designee(s), however the effective date of such an amendment shall be at least 3 days after public proclamation of the update.

parts.heading: Subchapter IV — MAYFLOWER TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY; EXPANSION
parts.text:
EXPANSION. Members of the Mayflower Transportation Authority shall have the ability to enact road closure for the purpose of:

(a) responding to and clearing motor vehicle accidents;

(b) clearing and or otherwise managing hazards on public roadways;

(c) assisting with law enforcement checkpoints; or

(d) conducting maintenance on a public road.

The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall have the jurisdiction to conduct their lawful duties which shall include the operation of public transportation, the maintenance and operation of public roads, and the clearance of motor vehicle accidents and hazards on public roads throughout the state and shall not be obstructed.

(a) Those in violation of this section shall be guilty of “Obstruction of Transportation Authority Personnel."

The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall have the jurisdiction to conduct their lawful duties which shall include the maintenance, inspection, and operation of public commuter rail systems within the state and shall not be obstructed.

(a) Those in violation of this section shall be guilty of “Obstruction of Transportation Authority Personnel”.

The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall have the jurisdiction to conduct their lawful duties which shall include the clearance of motor vehicle accidents, and the clearance of hazards on any bridge or tunnel within the state and shall not be obstructed.

(a) Those in violation of this section shall be guilty of “Obstruction of Transportation Authority Personnel”.

parts.heading: Subchapter VI — SPEED LIMIT ACT
parts.text:
DEFINITIONS. A “residential roadway” shall be defined as a road within a residential neighbourhood.

An “urban roadway” shall be defined as a road within a city limit.

A “rural roadway” shall be defined as a roadway outside of a city limit.

SPEED LIMITS. Unless otherwise signed, the speed limit of a residential roadway shall be 30 mph.

Unless otherwise signed, the speed limit of an urban roadway shall be 50 mph.

Unless otherwise signed, the speed limit of a rural roadway shall be 70 mph.

parts.heading: Subchapter VII — MAYFLOWER DIVISION OF MOTOR VEHICLES
parts.text:
The Mayflower Division of Motor Vehicles (hereinafter “Division of Motor Vehicles”, “Division”, or “DMV”) shall be established as a subordinate entity of the Mayflower Department of Transportation.

The Secretary of Transportation shall have administrative oversight authority over the Division and may appoint a Commissioner of Motor Vehicles, who shall serve at the pleasure of the Secretary of Transportation and shall be responsible for the direction and management of the Division.

The Commissioner of Motor Vehicles shall:

(a) Be the final authority for carrying out all functions, powers, and duties of the Division relating to: the appointment and employment of all officers and employees of the Division; the acquisition and maintenance of property, services, and equipment of the Division; the promulgation of regulations, rules, orders, and other official publications of the Division, except as otherwise provided; and any other obligation imposed on or power conferred upon the Commissioner.

(i) The Commissioner shall additionally have the authority to delegate and authorize successive re-delegations of any function, power, or duty conferred upon the Commissioner to an officer or employee of the Division (unless such delegation is prohibited by law) and to issue, rescind, and revise such regulations as may be necessary to carry out the functions of the Commissioner and the Division.

(b) Offer advice and counsel to the Governor and Secretary of Transportation with respect to the licensing, registration, and identification functions of the state.

(c) Have the authority to establish, restructure, or dissolve ranks, offices, subdivisions, and positions within the Division as deemed necessary for the effective administration and operation of the Division.

(d) Perform any other reasonable duties or functions as directed by the Secretary of Transportation.

parts.heading: Subchapter VIII — MDOT EMERGENCY SERVICES ACT / LANDER CITY RAILROAD FIRE BRIGADE ACT
Subchapter IX — PULL OFF THE ROAD ACT
parts.text:
Law enforcement officers shall be required to, where feasible:

(a) Ensure that vehicles engaged in a traffic stop on a highway are completely off the roadway.

(b) Park vehicles belonging to a detained individual in a legal location. Law enforcement officers shall be able to request for the Mayflower Department of Transportation to do so in their place.

sections.heading: Licensing and Documentation
sections.text:
LONG TITLE. An act to ensure that checkpoints in the state are established and precedents are set up for departmental leadership to start doing checkpoints.

SHORT TITLE. This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the “Mayflower Checkpoint Act.”

The term “checkpoint” or “checking station” shall refer to the following:

(a) Barriers set up to block traffic by law enforcement to check for BOLOs, warrants, firearms licenses, or driver’s licenses, or for commercial vehicle officers to conduct commercial vehicle inspections.

The term “commercial vehicle inspection” shall refer to the following:

(a) The inspection (search) of cargo, shipping documents, and commercial driver’s license(s).

The term “natural resources inspection” shall refer to the following:

(a) The inspection (search) of fish, lumber, fishing license(s), and lumber license(s).

Commercial vehicle officers of the state police shall have the ability to establish checkpoints on any public roadway and establish checkpoints on state highways for the purpose of conducting commercial vehicle inspections.

(a) The state police shall have the sole authority and power to establish checkpoints on state highways, unless an agency has proper authority from the colonel of the state police to establish one.

Any municipal or county law enforcement agency shall have the ability to establish checking stations on any municipal or county roadway within their administration for the purpose of checking driver’s license(s).

The National Guard shall have the ability to establish checkpoints anywhere within a Military Exclusion Zone or on any road directly adjacent to a Mayflower National Guard installation with the authorization from a Senior Officer or Command Group Personnel. During a deployment by the governor, the National Guard shall have the ability to establish a checkpoint on any roadway or state highway within the deployment area. Military police must be present for all established checkpoints.

Each department stated above shall set up its own internal regulations on how checkpoints or checking stations shall be established, which shall not contradict but further expand upon these provisions.

To prevent the unnecessary halt of members of the public, a vehicle shall only be stopped at a checkpoint or checking station for a maximum of five (5) minutes, unless the following are met:

(a) there is an active threat to the checkpoint or checking station;

(b) the vehicle is subject to a commercial vehicle or natural resource inspection; and

(c) a peace officer or member of the national guard, with reasonable suspicion of a crime, orders the individual to exit their vehicle.

The Port Authority Police Department may set up checkpoints anywhere on Port Authority Installations, as defined in 3 M.S.C. 5 § 1110.

“Checkpoint(s)” shall refer to barriers set up to block traffic by Law Enforcement Officers or Guardsmen to check for BOLOs, warrants, driver licenses, and firearm licenses.

Any person who fails to provide identification or property documentation for a vehicle or themselves to law enforcement, or members of the national guard, or conservation officers at a checkpoint or checking station shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. 1 § 1305 Failure to Comply.

sections.heading: Tunnel and Bridge Operations
sections.text:
"Bridge" shall be defined as:

(a) A lawful bridge over navigable waters of the Union of Columbia, including approaches, fenders, and appurtenances thereto, which is used and operated for the purpose of carrying railroad traffic, or both railroad and highway traffic, or if a State, county, municipality, or other political subdivision is the owner or joint owner thereof, which is used and operated for the purpose of carrying highway traffic.

"Tunnel" shall be defined as:

(a) An underground, underwater, or undersea passageway which is used and operated for the purposes of vehicle, pedestrian, or railroad traffic, or any combination of the three.

It shall be prohibited to trespass individuals from a tunnel or bridge which is part of the Jones Beltway or State Route 55.

LONG TITLE. An act to improve the efficiency of the administration, upkeep, safety and maintenance of the Mayflower Transportation System.

SHORT TITLE. This act shall be known and may be cited as the “ Transportation Efficiency Act.”

Notwithstanding other laws, the Winchester Bridge Authority is established as a volunteer agency of the City of Winchester in the County of Lee.

Notwithstanding other laws, the Winchester Bridge Authority, shall be responsible for maintenance, upkeep, and administration of all tunnels and bridges in or around the City of Winchester in the County of Lee.

(a) The Winchester Bridge Authority shall additionally be responsible for all firefighting, rescue, and medical efforts and operations on tunnels and bridges under their administration.

(b) The Winchester Bridge Authority shall contract private companies/entities, or request other government agencies, to assist with or complete certain maintenance-related tasks on tunnels and bridges under their administration.

(c) The Winchester Bridge Authority shall, with the consent of the Mayor of the Town of Winchester, or its police chief in the event of a mayoral vancancy, officially name any tunnel or bridge under its administration, and must notify the public of the change through forms of public documentation or notification, such as a letter or press release.

(d) The Winchester Bridge Authority shall maintain a plan for emergency response in the eventuality of any emergency occurring within any tunnel or bridge under its administration.

The Winchester Bridge Authority shall maintain a plan for emergency response in the eventuality of any emergency occuring within a tunnel or bridge administered by the Authority.

The Winchester Bridge Authority shall take priority over the Port Authority when it relates to any matter relating to any piece of real property under its jurisdiction.

sections.heading: Railroad Property and Police
sections.text:
“Company” shall refer to:

(a) The term “Class I Railroad” as defined in the Class I Railway Act.

“Peace officer” shall refer to:

(a) The term “Peace Officer” as defined in the Class I Railway Act; or

(b) Any person that is both certified by the law enforcement training institute and is currently commissioned by a county law enforcement agency, a state law enforcement agency, a municipal law enforcement agency, or any other law enforcement entity recognized by the State.

A “second” shall be defined as:

(a) The duration of 9,192,631,770 periods of the radiation corresponding to the transition between two hyperfine levels of the ground state of the Cesium-133 atom.

A “stud” shall be defined as:

(a) A unit of measurement which, from a bird's eye view of a Roblox R6 character, is the distance measured across the top surface of the character's arm without any active packages. This measurement begins at one side of the top of the arm and extends to the opposite side of the top of the arm, while the character is standing in a standard, upright position; or

(b) The rectilinear distance light propagates, in a vacuum, in 0.00000000093357 seconds.

“Employee” shall be defined as:

(a) Any person who is employed by a company or contractor to perform work in connection with the operation, maintenance, or construction of a railroad, including but not limited to engineers, conductors, brakemen, switchmen, trackmen, signalmen, and any other position designated by a company for the purposes of this clause.

“Railroad police officer” shall refer to:

(a) The term “railroad police officer” as defined in the Class I Railway Act.

“Railroad” shall be defined as:

(a) The set of two parallel lines, usually made out of metal, of which railroad equipment operates on and includes:

(i) Branches, extensions, sidings, railroad bridges, tunnels, stations, depots, wharfs, equipment, stores or other things connected with the railroad; and

(ii) Communications or signaling systems and related facilities and equipment used for railroad purposes.

“Railroad equipment” shall be defined as:

(a) A machine exclusively designed for movement on a railroad, whether or not the machine is capable of independent motion; or

(b) A vehicle that is designed for movement both on and off a railroad while the adaptations of that vehicle for movement on a railroad are in use.

“Goods” shall be defined as:

(a) Anything that may be taken or placed on railroad equipment and includes:

(i) Freight, and;

(ii) Baggage, and;

(iii) Railroad employees, and;

(iv) Passengers, and;

(v) personal belongings.

“Road crossing” shall be defined as:

(a) The part of a road that passes across, over or under a line of a railroad, and includes any structure supporting or protecting that part of the road or facilitating the crossing.

“Railroad warning signal” shall be defined as:

(a) A distinct audible signal emitted from a railroad equipment’s horn device, consisting of a loud and prolonged sound produced by the activation of the railroad equipment’s horn mechanism; or

(b) Intermittent, high-intensity lights mounted on the front of railroad equipment which create a flashing pattern when in operation.

“Vehicle” shall be defined as:

(a) Any device or contrivance capable of being used for the transportation or conveyance of persons or property on a highway, road, street, or other surface, including, but not limited to, automobiles, trucks, motorcycles, bicycles, scooters, buses, trains, trailers, and animals used for riding or drawing loads, such as horses.

“Bus” shall be defined as:

(a) A vehicle designed for carrying ten or more passengers and used for the transportation of persons.

No pedestrian or vehicle shall enter, remain upon or traverse over a road crossing or pedestrian walkway crossing a railroad if:

(a) The railroad gate is lowered and obstructing the road or when the railroad gates are in the process of lowering; however,

(i) in the situation that the railroad gates are broken and closed, the pedestrian or vehicle may cross, except when railroad equipment is plainly visible and approaching the crossing; and,

(1) right of way shall be given by order of arrival to the intersection; however, any railroad equipment shall take priority;

(b) A railroad warning signal or a clearly visible electric or mechanical signal device is in operation and such signal or device is giving reasonable warning of the presence, approach, passage or departure of railroad equipment;

(c) A railroad police officer or employee gives visual or verbal instruction to stop for oncoming railroad equipment;

(d) Railroad equipment is approaching a road crossing and is actively operating any railroad warning signal; or

(e) Railroad equipment is approaching a road crossing and the nature of its velocity poses a safety hazard to obstacles present on the railroad or road crossing.

No vehicle shall enter, cross, remain upon or traverse on any railroad if they are not at a road crossing.

No pedestrian shall enter, cross, remain upon or traverse on any railroad, nor walk alongside a railroad within five studs.

(a) A pedestrian may walk alongside a railroad if there is a clearly established path intended for pedestrian traffic, or if directed to do so by a peace officer or employee.

No person shall board, attempt to board, or ride on top of any railroad equipment without the express permission of the operator.

No person shall refuse to follow any lawful orders given by a peace officer or employee while situated on railroad equipment, on any railroad or road crossing, or within ten studs of a railroad or road crossing.

The operator of a bus, upon approaching a road crossing, unless directed by a peace officer or employee, shall:

(a) Stop the bus not less than 6 studs from the nearest railroad;

(b) Look in both directions along the railroad;

(c) If possible, open a door of the bus and listen to determine if any railroad equipment is approaching; and

(d) When it is safe to do so, cross the road crossing with caution.

An employee and a peace officer shall have the ability, given that the peace officer has a burn permit, to lawfully burn a vehicle that is stuck or otherwise reasonably obstructing any part of a railroad or road crossing.

(a) All reasonable attempts must be made to move a vehicle off of a railroad or road crossing before burning such vehicle.

Prohibitions in this section shall not extend to peace officers, employees, and any person who receives permission, in writing, from the relevant company.

Subject to the Class I Railway Act, railroad police officers shall be given the authority to enforce all the laws of the State throughout the State with a focus in any way to the protection of properties that the company owns, possesses or administers and the persons upon those properties.

(a) Railroad police officers may carry out enforcement of all the laws of the State in the interest of public safety and in order to protect life and property and to assist law enforcement of local jurisdiction.

(b) This section shall not be construed to supersede or override any provision of the Class I Railway Act.

Every person who contravenes a provision of this act shall be guilty of “Obstruction of Railroad Operations.”

(a) If such contravention endangers the life of another individual, the person shall instead be guilty of “Felony Obstruction of Railroad Operations.”

(b) Every business entity who contravenes a provision of this act is guilty of an offense and on conviction, in addition to any other penalty or punishment to which the business entity may be liable, is liable to a fine not less than two thousand dollars and not more than ten thousand dollars.

parts.heading: Subchapter III — JURISDICTION OF RAILROAD POLICE
parts.text:
Subject to the Class I Railway Act, railroad police officers shall be given the authority to enforce all the laws of the State throughout the State with a focus in any way to the protection of properties that the company owns, possesses or administers and the persons upon those properties.

(a) Railroad police officers may carry out enforcement of all the laws of the State in the interest of public safety and in order to protect life and property and to assist law enforcement of local jurisdiction.

(b) This section shall not be construed to supersede or override any provision of the Class I Railway Act.

parts.heading: Subchapter IV — ENFORCEMENT
parts.text:
Every person who contravenes a provision of this act shall be guilty of “Obstruction of Railroad Operations.”

(a) If such contravention endangers the life of another individual, the person shall instead be guilty of “Felony Obstruction of Railroad Operations.”

(b) Every business entity who contravenes a provision of this act is guilty of an offense and on conviction, in addition to any other penalty or punishment to which the business entity may be liable, is liable to a fine not less than two thousand dollars and not more than ten thousand dollars.

sections.heading: Commercial Drivers and Vehicles
sections.text:
The term “weight-units” shall refer to:

(a) The amount of inventory weight that can be stored in a vehicles’ inventory.

The term “Commercial Vehicle” shall refer to:

(a) a vehicle with a gross weight-unit rating of five-hundred (500) or more;

(b) is designed to transport more than 15 persons, including the driver; or

(c) a vehicle that is specified by the game’s developers to require a Commercial Driver’s License to purchase.

Any commercial vehicle transporting cargo on any State highway may be required to stop and be subject to inspection of shipping documents or commercial license by the Mayflower State Police or an employee of the Mayflower Transportation Authority with necessary certification to inspect commercial vehicles.

Any law enforcement officer within their respective jurisdiction may require commercial vehicles to stop and subject them to inspection of shipping documents, commercial license; or cargo. If the vehicle or driver is found to be operating in an unsafe condition, or if any required part or equipment is not present or is not in proper repair or adjustment, and the continued operation would present an unduly hazardous operating condition, the officer may require the vehicle or the driver to be removed from service until necessary adjustments are made.

The Mayflower State Police Colonel is authorized to establish a certification program for non-law-enforcement employees of the Mayflower Transit Authority. If such a program is established, the Colonel shall liaison with the department head of the Mayflower Transportation Authority. This program shall allow certified employees to:

(a) inspect commercial vehicles operating within the political subdivision in compliance with applicable laws and regulations; and

(b) request and verify commercial drivers license documentation from operators of commercial vehicles on State highways and local roads.

Any person who fails to comply with an officer’s request to submit to an inspection under this section shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. 1 § 1305 “Failure to comply”.

Commercial Vehicles with a gross weight-unit rating exceeding five-hundred (500) traveling on state highways or public roads with two or more lanes in one direction shall be prohibited from occupying the leftmost lane unless are using the lane to:

(a) Make a left turn.

(b) Yield to an emergency vehicle traveling in the right lane.

(c) Avoiding a road closure or emergency scene.

(d) Posted signage is present that states left lane travel is required or permissible.

It shall be prohibited to operate a commercial vehicle on roads designated by the department head Mayflower Department of Transportation or their designee, which has appropriate signage on the road which can be clearly read—

(a) Unless it is:

(i) A state-owned commercial vehicle being lawfully operated; or

(ii) Being escorted by law enforcement or transportation authority.

(b) Any individual who unlawfully operates a commercial vehicle on a road which has been designated a no-commercial-vehicle zone shall be subject to a citation for 2 M.S.C. § 2103 “Driving in a No-Commercial-Vehicle Zone”
